courses.title: Applied Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Foundational principles and practical applications of analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) across various business domains with a focus on challenges involved in these techniques.

courses.title: Statistics for Applied Data Analytics
courses.description: Statistics, probability, probability distributions and other fundamental data analysis concepts and tools. Development of simple models to support subsequent evaluation and data-supported decisions.

courses.title: Visualization and Storytelling With Data
courses.description: Tools and techniques to effectively analyze and visualize data and communicate the results. Python libraries, modules, techniques and best practices.

courses.title: Regression Modeling for Applied Predictive Analytics
courses.description: Linear regression and logistic regression models, coefficient interpretation and performance analysis. Advanced modeling techniques.

courses.title: Applied Data Management and Database Systems
courses.description: Overview of the data pipeline, data sources, data interchange formats and the organization of data for analytics and modeling, problems, solutions and best practices.

courses.title: Applied Machine Learning for Business Applications
courses.description: Exploration of machine learning principles and practices using real-world data, models and techniques. Initial data explorations to deployment to maintenance of machine learning systems.

courses.title: Applied Optimization and Simulation
courses.description: Applied mathematical programming including simulation methods, constrained optimization methods, linear programming, mixed integer programming and statistical and discrete event simulation methods. Case studies.

courses.title: Analytics Business Strategy and Communication
courses.description: Development of astute business acumen and strong communication skills for analytics professionals and leaders in relation to strategy, storytelling, communication and change management.

courses.title: Applications of Deep Learning and AI in Business
courses.description: Exploration of deep learning models, deep neural networks and artificial intelligence sequence modeling and implementation. Applications of targeted techniques to real-world business scenarios.

courses.title: Project Management for Analytics Professionals
courses.description: A comprehensive look into the analytics project life cycle from discovery through deployment. Use of appropriate metrics and best practices to monitor and validate results.

courses.title: Applications in Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: A comprehensive survey of generative artificial intelligence and artificial intelligence for decision-making; transformer and diffusion models; reinforcement learning and causal inference. Hands-on implementation.

courses.title: Applied Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Capstone
courses.description: An integrative culminating experience of the MSAAN program. The practical application of knowledge and skills gained throughout the program to address a significant business problem.

courses.title: Innovators Forum
schools: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
programs: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation

courses.description: Product planning and task clarification, voice of customers, quality function deployment, conceptual and embodiment design, axiomatic theory of design, product quality and manufacturability, design decision-making.
courses.recommended_prep: AME 305.

courses.title: Turbine Design and Analysis
courses.description: Physics of turbine operation; design and analysis for the development of turbine hardware for propulsion and power generation.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic thermodynamics and mechanics such as AME 310, familiarity with MATLAB to the level of TAC 168.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Andrew and Erna Viterbi School of Engineering

courses.title: Engineering Vibrations I
courses.description: The theory of free and forced vibrations with and without damping; systems with single and multiple degrees of freedom; solution methods; introduction to continuous systems.

courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: General principles underlying heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation; steady and transient conditions; heat exchangers.

courses.title: Automotive and Flight Propulsion
courses.description: Analysis of combustion engines: reciprocating-piston, gas turbines, rockets. Tradeoffs compared to non-combustion sources. Ideal and non-ideal cycle analysis and performance evaluation; pollutant formation and remediation.
courses.recommended_prep: AME 309

courses.title: Senior Projects Laboratory
courses.description: Team engineering design project to model, construct and test a physical principle or system. Complete industrial research project including proposal, design review, presentation, technical report.

courses.title: Senior Projects Laboratory
courses.description: Individual engineering projects designed and constructed to model and test a physical principle or system.

courses.title: Linear Control Systems I
courses.description: Transform methods, block diagrams; transfer functions; stability; root-locus and frequency domain analysis and design; application to flight control, state space and multiloop systems.

courses.title: Bio-inspired Robotics
courses.description: Robotics terminology; limitations of conventional robots; converting biologically inspired concepts into implementable engineering designs; potential applications.

courses.title: Aerodynamic Theory
courses.description: Basic relations describing the inviscid flow field about bodies and wings moving at subsonic and supersonic speeds.

courses.title: Aircraft Design
courses.description: Aircraft design and analysis, design requirements and specifications; integration of structure, propulsion, control system, and aerodynamic configuration; performance analysis and prediction.

courses.title: Aerospace Structures I
courses.description: Design, qualification, and workmanship of aircraft, spacecraft and launch vehicle structures. Aerospace standards, external and internal loads and finite element software applied to structural systems.
courses.recommended_prep: MASC 310

courses.title: Mechanics of Composite Materials for Modern Structures
courses.description: Current and potential applications of composite materials including manufacturing methods; determining mechanical properties; failure analysis; and design, inspection, and repair considerations.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Undergraduate Design Projects II
courses.description: Analysis, design, fabrication, and evaluation of devices intended for entry in local and national design competitions. Intended for students with prior project experience. Upper division standing. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Innovative Conceptual Design for New Product Development
courses.description: A logic-based framework for conceptual design, including systematic concept generation and improvement, in innovative product developments.
courses.recommended_prep: Bachelor's degree in engineering or physical sciences

courses.title: Modern Topics in Aerospace Design
courses.description: Current topics in Aerospace Engineering are addressed by a number of industry panelists. Students, under panelists' supervision and guidance, complete independent research reports and briefings. Recommended preparation: AME 261, AME 441, AME 481 or equivalents. Genuine interest in design of flight vehicles. Open only to Senior, Master, and Doctoral students.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Andrew and Erna Viterbi School of Engineering

courses.title: Advanced Mechanical Design
courses.description: Specific problems and methods of analysis in mechanical systems design.
courses.recommended_prep: Engineering Design and Principles on the level of AME 410

courses.title: Mechatronics Systems Engineering
courses.description: Use of mechanical, electrical and computer engineering, math and computer science to design of high performance and sophisticated products and processes and systems involving mechatronics.
courses.recommended_prep: Bachelors degree in engineering or physical sciences. Hand-on skills computer programming (particularly C).

courses.title: Machine Learning for Engineering Applications
courses.description: Modeling engineering challenges, supervised and unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, support vector machines, Bayesian learning, large language models, transform engineering with machine learning.

courses.title: Continuum Mechanics
courses.description: A unified mathematical description for modeling the mechanics and thermodynamics of continua, including topics like elasticity, inelastic material modeling and fluid behavior.

courses.title: Mechanics of Solids
courses.description: Fundamental theory of linear elasticity applicable to multiple branches of solid mechanics.
courses.recommended_prep: Mechanics of deformable bodies or solid mechanics on the level of CE 225 or AME 204.

courses.title: Machine Learning and Computational Physics
courses.description: Machine learning applications in computational physics and engineering; relationships between computational physics and ML algorithms; hybrid physics-informed ML prediction with tools for uncertainty quantification.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic familiarity with Python/Matlab

courses.title: Applied Elasticity
courses.description: Cartesian tensors; kinematics of deformation, balance laws, and constitutive equations; variational principles; finite elasticity; plates and cylindrical shells; viscoelasticity; analytical and numerical solutions for elasticity.

courses.title: Advanced Computational Design and Manufacturing
courses.description: Study concepts behind computational representations, algorithms and mathematical foundations, and their applications in computer-aided design and manufacturing. Develop hands-on computational skills in team projects.
courses.recommended_prep: Programming (C++ or MATLAB) on the level of TAC 168 (MATLAB), or TAC 165 (C++) or CSCI 102 (C++)

courses.title: Compressible Gas Dynamics
courses.description: Compressible flow equations; Rayleigh/Fanno flows; shock/expansion waves and interactions; potential flow, small disturbance theory and similarity; hypersonics; viscosity, high-temperature and radiation effects.

courses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Combustion
courses.description: Chemical equilibrium, flame temperature, chemical kinetics, transport phenomena, conservation equations of multi-component reacting flows, laminar flames, droplet combustion, flame speed, combustion pollutants, atmospheric pollution processes.

courses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Combustion
courses.description: Advanced topics in combustion including analytical methods, stretch effects, stability, ignition and extinction of flames, plasma-assisted combustion, turbulence effects, detonations, and micropower generation.

courses.title: Emerging Manufacturing Technologies
courses.description: Overview of emerging manufacturing technologies across different length scales (macro-micro-nano), including top-down approaches, bottom-up approaches and material synthesis/assembly.

courses.title: Engineering Vibrations II
courses.description: Multi-degree of freedom systems; continuous systems; modal analysis. Beams, rods, membranes, plates, shells. Approximate methods; Galerkin, Rayleigh Ritz; assumed-mode, finite elements.

courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems, Vibrations, and Chaos
courses.description: Flows on a line and circle; phase plane methods; bifurcation theory; limit cycle/relaxation oscillations; chaotic systems, one-dimensional maps, the Lorenz equations, fractals and strange attractors.

courses.title: Advanced Engineering Dynamics
courses.description: Principle of virtual work, constraints, Lagrange's equations, Gibbs-Appell equations, Gauss's principle, theory of rotations, dynamics of rigid bodies, Hamiltonian mechanics, control and mechanics.

courses.title: Linear Algebra in Engineering Science
courses.description: Systems of linear equations; eigenvalues and eigenvectors; singular values and singular vectors; linear transformations; regression and optimization; data-driven learning.
courses.recommended_prep: Multivariable calculus at the level of MATH 229

courses.title: Partial Differential Equations for Engineering Applications
courses.description: Solving linear heat, wave, Laplace and Poisson equations, separation of variables and Fourier series, special functions, Fourier and Laplace transforms, characteristics, Greens functions, similarity solutions.

courses.title: Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Basic concepts; variational methods; isoparametric formulation; plane stress; plane strain; axisymmetric structures; plates and shells; structural dynamics; stability and buckling; computer applications; nonlinear analysis.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge in strength of materials equivalent to CE 225 or AME 204; Extensive knowledge of MATLAB at the level of CE 108

courses.title: Aircraft Structures Analysis
courses.description: Stress Analysis. Linear Elasticity. Thin Plates. Finite Element Methods. Structural stability. Vibration of Continuous Systems. Emphasis on aerospace and aeronautical applications

courses.title: Dynamics of Incompressible Fluids
courses.description: A unified discussion of low-speed fluid mechanics including exact solutions; approximation techniques for low and high Reynolds numbers; inviscid flows; surface waves; dynamic stability; turbulence.
courses.recommended_prep: Vector/tensor notation, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, complex variables and differential equations at the level of AME 525/AME 526 (which are strongly recommended if lacking this background)

courses.title: Flight Vehicle Stability and Control
courses.description: Modeling, simulation, control and estimation of air vehicles, including the development of custom models and simulations for student-developed aircraft; extensions to non-air vehicles.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra and differential equations on the level of MATH 245. Linear control theory on the level of AME 451. Flight mechanics on the level of AME 459.

courses.title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Convergence, consistency, stability: finite difference, finite element, and spectral methods; direct and iterative procedures for steady problems; linear diffusion and advection problems; nonlinear advection problems. Recommended preparation: AME 526.

courses.title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Generalized curvilinear coordinates; grid generation; numerical techniques for transonic and supersonic inviscid flows: boundary layer flows; reduced Navier-Stokes equations; compressible and incompressible viscous flows. Recommended preparation: AME 511 or AME 530a.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics in Engineering Science
courses.description: Probability theory; random variables and vectors; joint, marginal, and conditional distributions; Bayes' theorem; introduction to stochastic processes; statistical inference; regression and generative models.
courses.recommended_prep: Multivariable calculus at the level of MATH 229

courses.title: Linear Control Systems II
courses.description: State space representation, linearization, solution of state equations; controllability and observability; state feedback, state observers; optimal control; output feedback.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of a programming language (MATLAB, SIMULINK)

courses.title: Computer Control of Mechanical Systems
courses.description: Computer control as applied to machine tools, mechanical manipulators, and other mechanical machinery; discrete time controller design; microprocessor implementation of motion and force control servos.

courses.title: Design for Manufacturing Assembly
courses.description: Overview of methods and tools for creating products that are easier to manufacture and assemble thereby reducing manufacturing costs.

courses.title: Foundations for Manufacturing Automation
courses.description: An overview of the building blocks that underlie automation; mechanics-based models for designing automated systems; decision-making tools and methods for supporting manufacturing automation.
courses.recommended_prep: AME 451 or background in Linear Controls

courses.title: Systems Architecting
courses.description: Introduction to systems architecture in aerospace, electrical, computer, and manufacturing systems emphasizing the conceptual and acceptance phases and using heuristics.

courses.title: Seminar in Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Recent developments and research in aerospace and mechanical engineering and related fields. Oral and written reports.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Andrew and Erna Viterbi School of Engineering

courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Engineering Materials
courses.description: Mechanical properties of materials; macroscopic mechanical behavior related to structure and microstructure of the material; elementary dislocation theory related to basic strengthening mechanisms; fatigue and fracture; nanomaterials.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate introduction to chemistry and the equivalent of MASC 310

courses.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
courses.description: Phase plane, describing function, applications to mechanical and aerospace systems. Lyapunov stability theory. Popov theorem. Circle criterion. Lyapunov redesign. Sliding mode control. Backstepping. Passivity.
courses.recommended_prep: Background in dynamics and classical control system

courses.title: Additive Manufacturing Technologies
courses.description: Overview and working principles of commonly used additive manufacturing processes; process models; process and material selection; cost estimation methods; current applications and future directions.

courses.title: Fatigue and Fracture
courses.description: Behavior of materials under cyclic and static fatigue; plastic instability; life-time predictions; brittle and ductile fracture; crack propagation and plastic blunting.

courses.title: Computational Design of Machine Components
courses.description: Computer-aided design of machine components widely encountered in automotive and aerospace applications including fasteners, stiffeners, airfoils, etc. Intended for students with little CAE experience.

courses.title: Design and Advanced Manufacturing of Machine Components
courses.description: Modern CAE design for automotive and aerospace machine components; characterization methods, design tools and manufacturing techniques. Intended for students with prior CAE experience.
courses.recommended_prep: Computer-aided design/analysis on the level of AME 308 or AME 563

courses.title: Computational Multiphysics Modeling in Engineering Science
courses.description: Mathematical formulation and computational implementation of the partial differential equations governing coupled physical phenomena often treated separately; e.g., electro-chemo-thermo-fluid-solid mechanics.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra at the level of AME 525, partial differential equations at the level of AME 526, and exposure to Python programming at the level of AME 508.

courses.title: Aerospace Structures II
courses.description: Finite element analysis of aerospace structures including heat transfer, joints, bellows, pressure vessels, flexible dynamics, random vibrations, repairs, buckling, fatigue/fracture and stress concentrations.
courses.recommended_prep: An undergraduate background in aerospace or mechanical engineering.

courses.title: Materials Selection
courses.description: Materials selection in relationship to design and fabrication, economic considerations, methodology of selection, performance parameters; case studies.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate level course in materials (equivalent to MASC 310)

courses.title: Race and Class in Los Angeles
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of race and the economic, political, gender, and social dimensions of contemporary Los Angeles including topics such as residential segregation, economic inequality, and city politics.

courses.title: Peoples and Cultures of the Americas
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introduction to cultures and people in the Americas; the social, historical, economic and cultural formations that together make up the Latino/a American imaginary.

courses.title: Introduction to American Studies and Ethnicity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to American studies and ethnic studies. Provides an overview of major theories, concepts, and issues.

courses.title: LGBTQ America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines how U.S. sexual identity and experience are represented in the 20th and 21st century and introduces the interdisciplinary field of LGBTQ Studies.

courses.title: Introduction to Native Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of Native American studies, including Indigenous intellectualism and resistance through language revitalization, film-making, and the recognition of one another.

courses.title: Introduction to American Popular Culture
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the relation between U.S. national culture, race, and popular culture.

courses.title: Sex in America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores how the proliferation of sexual cultures, identities, politics shape everyday lives in the United States and beyond.

courses.title: Race and Mixed Race
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the politics of interracial marriage and intimacy, mixed race identities, and trans-racial adoption.

courses.title: The Making of Asian America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Historical, social, and cultural analysis of (East, South, and Southeast) Asians in the United States. Theme examined: immigration, race and gender relations, ethnic culture, community, and identity.

courses.title: Introduction to African American Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the socio-historical and political imperatives of multi-disciplinary scholarship foundational to the study of African Americans.

courses.title: Black Social Movements in the U.S.
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: This course examines black social movements for freedom, justice, equality, and self determination. Beginning with Reconstruction, movements include labor, civil rights, radical feminism, socialism, reparations, Black Nationalism, prisoners' rights, and Hip Hop.

courses.title: Exploring Ethnicity through Film
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the constructions of American ethnicity/race in film.

courses.title: America, the Frontier, and the New West
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to an interdisciplinary study of American political, cultural and social life with a particular emphasis on the Western United States as a region. Recommended preparation: HIST 200, ENGL 263

courses.title: Documenting Latinx Los Angeles Food Cultures
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores Latinx food in Los Angeles through an anthropological lens. Students experience, document and analyze local food knowledge and traditions through active field study.

courses.title: The Middle East in Hollywood
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An examination of how Hollywood representations of the Middle East have changed over the last 100 years, focusing on how representations influence perceptions and policies.

courses.title: Latinx Media Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Introduces students to critical analyses of media texts, industries and technologies that shape the lives of Latinx communities in the United States.

courses.title: Asian American Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines political attitudes, behavior and participation of Asian Americans in diverse U.S. society.

courses.title: Black Music and the Political Imagination
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores the changing political meanings of black music throughout the 20th century, from freedom to a threat to civil order, from racial integration to Black liberation.

courses.title: Re-Viewing Religion in Asian America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of the religions traditions, institutions, and experiences of Asians and Pacific Islanders in the U.S.

courses.title: Latina/o LA
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of spatial and social patterns of the Latino population in Los Angeles. Emphasis on economic, demographic and cultural processes. Duplicates credit in the former GEOG-340.

courses.title: Law and Identities
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the complex and contested interaction between the law and racial, gender, religious, ethnic, and sexual identities using historical and contemporary cases.

courses.title: Food, Health and Culture in Los Angeles
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of Los Angeles diverse food cultures as well as the food justice issues that affect many low-income residents of neighborhoods surrounding USC campus.

courses.title: Law and American Indian Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines indigenous sovereignties and the historical andcontemporary legal histories and cases which inform them.

courses.title: Race and the Environment
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Relationships between environmentalism, environmental problems and racial-ethnic minorities. Rise of environmental justice movement. Assessment of social science methods used to investigate these relationships. Duplicates credit in the former GEOG-350.

courses.title: Junior Seminar in American Studies and Ethnicity: Theories and Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Advanced study in interdisciplinary theories and methods for analyzing race and ethnicity in the United Stes, including a comparative study of topics such as inequality, gender, and class.

courses.title: African American Art
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A survey of the fine arts produced by people of African descent in the United States from the nation's inception in the late 18th century until the contemporary moment.

courses.title: Leadership in the Community -- Internship
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: 8-10 hours per week in a community-based internship plus 2 hour class discussion. Theoretical and practical issues associated with community leadership.

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Asian American Communities
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of current social and political issues facing Asian American communities with emphasis on Los Angeles region; design and implementation of community-based research projects.

courses.title: Carceral Geographies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Focusing on California, interdisciplinary research teams will study why there are so many new US prisons. What is their relationship to shopping malls, gated communities, globalization?

courses.title: Social Media Storytelling for Latinx Audiences
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Create native journalistic content for current social media and emerging platforms with an emphasis on engaging content for Latinx audiences and underrepresented communities.

courses.title: Political Participation and American Diversity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines how diverse groups in the U.S. interact with the American political system.

courses.title: Latino Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of the historic and contemporary roles of Latinos in the American political system; patterns of political participation and representation are examined.

courses.title: Native American Literature
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of Native American literature, including oral traditions and print genres, such as short story, poetry, novel, and autobiography, from 1700 to the present. Recommended preparation: ENGL 263.

courses.title: African American Anthropology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An examination of anthropological research on race and African American culture, from the 18th century to the present.
courses.recommended_prep: AMST 385, ANTH 263

courses.title: Latinx Music in the Americas
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines diverse sonic genres in the Americas -- salsa, merengue, cumbia, reggaeton -- and how they remix the politics of race, gender, sexuality, migration and diaspora.

courses.title: African-American Narrative
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Development of the novel in African-American literature beginning with the anti-slavery fiction of William W. Brown and his pre-Emancipation contemporaries and concluding with the emerging novelists of the late sixties.

courses.title: Race, Gender and Sexuality
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of sexual discourses in the United States in the context of slavery, empire, sex work, labor markets, schools and prisons.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity in Entertainment and the Arts
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Examines how race and ethnicity as social categories are shaped by communication media; focuses on how race and ethnicity sustain entertainment and media industries.
courses.recommended_prep: COMM 206

courses.title: Latino News Media in the United States

Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: History and growing importance of Latino print and broadcast news media in covering immigration, discrimination, culture, social differences and other aspects of U.S. Latino life.

courses.description: Surveys interdisciplinary theories and methodologies in Caribbean studies, focusing on the Circum-Caribbean and diasporic roots/routes of cultural studies (including ethnography, popular culture, performance).

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Seminar exploring crucial theoretical, methodological and historical issues in the development of African American Studies.

courses.description: Analyzes works in critical (dis)ability theory and its intersections with decolonial studies, critical race studies, feminist studies.

courses.description: Exploration of issues involved in conducting research in the interdisciplinary field of Chicano/Latino Studies and guides students through the design and completion of a journal-quality research paper.

courses.description: Leads graduate students in Latinx Studies in developing or revising a dissertation or masters thesis chapter, or research seminar paper, or adapting manuscripts for publication.

courses.description: Exploration of the intersection between the urban form and the social life of cities, looking at systemic problems of urban societies and potential design solutions.
courses.recommended_prep: ARCH 218

courses.title: Shelter Design Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to design at an occupiable scale -- from tents and pavilions to single units of housing, including issues of materiality, accessibility, constructability, functionality, etc.

courses.title: Architectural Design III
courses.description: Special integrative year including design issues relating to housing.

courses.title: Architectural Design III
courses.description: Special integrative year including design issues relating to housing.

courses.title: Principles of Spatial Design I
courses.description: Introduction to design principles and processes; sequence of exercises emphasizing development of basic skills, ideas, and techniques used in the creation of simplified urban space design projects.

courses.title: Intensive Survey: Prehistory to the Present
courses.description: An intensive historical overview of architecture from prehistory to the present, emphasizing interrelationships of various global cultures and how social considerations were translated into form. Not available for credit to architecture majors.

courses.title: Building Science II
courses.description: The design of a building as a complex of interacting systems; relations of subsystems; influences of production and marketing on design.

courses.title: Building Science II

courses.title: Digital Tools for Architecture
courses.description: Exploration of digital tools with an emphasis on building information modeling (BIM), parametric modeling, and interoperability including special topics in Architecture/Engineering/Construction (AEC) and sustainable design. Recommended preparation: basic computer skills.

courses.title: Design of Building Structures
courses.description: Problems and processes of design of building structures; structural investigation for design; codes and standards; design of elements and systems of wood, steel, masonry, and concrete for gravity and lateral loads.

courses.title: History of Architecture: Contemporary Issues
courses.description: Examination of the buildings, issues and images, the polemics and personalities that are animating current architectural discourse and practice.

courses.title: Design for the Luminous and Sonic Environment
courses.description: Ideas, problems, and computations related to the design of buildings in response to the luminous and sonic environment.

courses.title: Place and Culture
courses.description: (Study abroad programs only) Study of the relationships between places and culture through readings, lectures, discussion and weekly field trips.

courses.title: Experimental Futures
courses.description: Examination of experimental architecture, both historically, in the present day and the future. New waves of experimentation have the potential to bring about positive change in architecture.
courses.recommended_prep: ARCH 228

courses.title: Architectural Product Design Workshop
courses.description: Exploration into development of students' own architectural product and working prototype, using digital fabrication techniques for creating a physical prototype or coding for development of an app.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Practices for Architecture
courses.description: Development of business acumen around new architectural products, materials, systems, etc. Marketing, pitching, business plan development and networking are important aspects of business that all early entrepreneurs need to learn and understand.
courses.recommended_prep: ARCH 318

courses.title: Professional Practicum Workshop
courses.description: Students are required to have an architecture-related internship. Students reflect on the nature of their internships and the practice in general through readings and assignments.

courses.title: Architectural Studies- Expanding the Field
courses.description: Survey of opportunities, specializations, and professions related to architecture provides a resource for professional growth for architecture majors, and introduction to the field for non-majors.

courses.title: Architectural Design IV
courses.description: Selected areas of specialization; three projects chosen with advisement from a variety of studio offerings that concentrate on different areas of vital concern.

courses.title: Architectural Design IV

courses.title: Principles of Spatial Design II
courses.description: Emphasis on developing advanced urban spatial design solutions set within contemporary urban conditions, with a particular emphasis on ecology, public space, neighborhoods and districts. Prerequisite: Arch 303.

courses.title: Topics in Modern Architecture in Southern California
courses.description: Investigation of modern architecture in Southern California within its cultural and historic contexts.

courses.title: Building Science III

courses.title: Building Science III
courses.description: Design of building systems as an experimental process. Prereq: ARCH 305abL.

courses.title: Global Studies: Topics in Architecture, Urbanism, History and Art

courses.title: Design Foundation
courses.description: Introduction to basic architectural design principles for problem solving scenarios; foundational architectural design course for systematic thinking.

courses.title: Computer Transformations
courses.description: To explore the potential of computer-integrated design software; to develop techniques for critical analysis of architectural precedents; to expand the ability to visualize options; to expand perception; and to learn the basics of computer-integrated design.

courses.title: Architectural Technology
courses.description: Architectural design considered as a technological problem; influence of technology on design; buildings as integrated sets of subsystems.

courses.title: Geodesign Practicum
courses.description: Application of design concepts, planning protocols and spatial analysis skills to a complex planning or design problem sponsored by a local public, private or not-for-profit client in a studio setting.

courses.title: Perspectives in History and Theory in Architecture
courses.description: Perspectives in Architecture and Urbanism is an advanced course that allows students to delve deeply into one aspect of world history, theory and/or contemporary issues to develop more focused and critical understanding of that discourse.

courses.title: Visual Communication and Graphic Expression
courses.description: An exploratory study of fundamental and innovative visual communication principles and graphic expression techniques to facilitate the design enquiry process for architects.

courses.title: Digital Architectural Photography
courses.description: Perceiving and documenting the built environment through the perspective and frame of the digital camera. Mastering the basic principles of the digital image through an understanding of frame, light, exposure, color correction and printing output.

courses.title: Architectural Photography- Film and Digital
courses.description: See how light alters the visual impact of architectural forms; master high-resolution images both with film and digital; become a professional image developer/processor utilizing photographic software.

courses.title: Light, Color and the Character of Material
courses.description: Color theory, constructed drawings, constructed shadows, descriptive geometry, constructed perspective drawing, and layered wash techniques lead to experimentation with methods representing materiality and construction in design projects.

courses.title: Field Studies in Architecture

courses.title: Field Studies in Urbanism

courses.title: Field Studies in Tectonics

courses.title: Nonconventional Materials for the Built Environment
courses.description: An exploration of materials science topics relevant to the application of nonconventional materials in architecture, design, and engineering, addressing a broad range of materials, from the experimental to the vernacular.
courses.recommended_prep: ARCH 211

courses.title: Great Houses of Los Angeles
courses.description: An introduction to the architectural philosophies of seven influential California architects through reading and site visits to significant case studies.

courses.title: Walking the City

courses.title: Mixed Use Development Process
courses.description: Design, financial, legal and management challenges of mixed use real estate development; field project.

courses.title: Architectural Studies Capstone
courses.description: Introduction to methods of inquiry, research framework, and scholarly writing necessary to develop a comprehensive foundation for the Architectural Studies Capstone (ARCH 470b)

courses.title: Architectural Studies Capstone
courses.description: Collaborative research project and research paper in an area of concentration.

courses.title: Conversations on the Expanded Role of the Architect
courses.description: Modeled after Renaissance Salons, this "flipped classroom" course relies on lectures by luminaries and discussions as a means to interrogate the role of the architect.

courses.title: Furniture Design

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in various specialty areas of architecture.

courses.title: Comprehensive Architectural Design

courses.title: Critical Topics in Architecture
courses.description: Seminar supporting the research, development, and writing of Degree Project Paper provides a comprehensive base of information for the final Bachelor of Architecture studio.

courses.title: Architectural Design V
courses.description: The final architectural project under the guidance of a faculty adviser to demonstrate architectural knowledge, skills, and professional interests and goals.

courses.title: Graduate Architecture Design I
courses.description: A general introduction to architectural principles, intended to develop design and critical thinking skills and proficiency to communicate those ideas effectively. Open to graduate architecture majors only.

courses.title: Graduate Architecture Design I
courses.description: A general introduction to architectural principles, intended to develop design and critical thinking skills and proficiency to communicate those ideas effectively. Open to graduate architecture majors only.

courses.title: Theories of Computer Technology
courses.description: Fundamental theories and meanings of computation as a technique in architectural design.

courses.title: Digital Fabrication- Materials and Methods of Production
courses.description: Overview of multiple fabrication, manufacturing, and construction techniques used in the production of architecture, furniture and industrial design.

courses.title: Building Systems: Materials and Construction
courses.description: Studies of construction system development within the architectural design context; processes and issues of selection, evaluation, optimization, integration, design control, and innovation, Departmental approval.

courses.title: Material + Process: Material Systems
courses.description: Confronts the conventional concepts behind modern building science and material applications, re-applying the processes of fabrication and methods of construction to investigate materiality. Prerequisites: ARCH 211 or ARCH 511.

courses.description: Issues and problems in the development of structural systems for buildings; design criteria, system choice, design development, optimization, subsystem integration. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.description: A compressed course in design criteria and calculation methods for mechanical and passive solar systems (loads, plant system, duct, and storage sizing) and lighting and acoustics (CIE and IES methods, dBA and NC systems). Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.title: Current Topics in Building Science
courses.description: Critical studies in building science ranging from sustainability, lighting, acoustics, materials and methods, structures, energy issues, digital media, and fabrication. Students focus on minimum of two topics.

courses.description: Methodologies and exercises on contextual design and environmentally sound technologies (EST's) applications for the sustainability of urban infrastructures, operative landscapes, and building integration in the urban system.

courses.title: Structural Design and Analysis
courses.description: a. Introduction to behavior and analysis of building structures. Structural loading, materials, and element types will be explored to understand the basic building blocks of buildings. b. Investigation and design of building structural systems for gravity, wind and seismic loading. Comprehensive design exploration of framing type, materials, detailing, layout, form and integration. Recommended preparation: One-semester college-level course in physics or calculus.

courses.title: Structural Design and Analysis
courses.description: a. Introduction to behavior and analysis of building structures. Structural loading, materials, and element types will be explored to understand the basic building blocks of buildings. b. Recommended preparation: One-semester college-level course in physics or calculus.

courses.title: Professional Practicum

courses.title: Professional Practice: Legal and Economic Context, Project Documentation
courses.description: The laws and regulations that affect architecture as well as building economics and financing. Development of comprehensive project documentation, detailing, specifications, drawing formats and organizations.

courses.title: Case Studies: The Development of Urban Housing
courses.description: An exploration of the various elements and stages of the housing development process. Recommended preparation: a preliminary understanding of real estate or housing.

courses.title: Urban Housing: Types and Typologies
courses.description: Applications and precedents for the architect interested in designing multi-family housing. Review of the sources of modern housing types, the impact of building codes and technology on the form and construction of housing, and study of housing densities, comparative analysis of multi-family residential patterns. Major emphasis on critical knowledge of historic housing typologies as they are applied to site conditions and groupings, building form, section, organization, and the design of individual dwellings. Recommended preparation: two years of undergraduate architectural studies.

courses.title: Urban Housing: Programs, Precedents, and Recent Case Studies
courses.description: Historical overview of the major domestic and international housing developments and innovations since the early 20th century case study format examining a wide range of issues that determine the form of urban housing in various cultures. Major emphasis on the detail analysis of social, technical, and design factors affecting recent housing developments. Recommended preparation: two years of undergraduate architectural studies.

courses.title: Urban Ecology
courses.description: Lectures, laboratory exercises and field trips introducing basic knowledge of the continually transforming landscape as a base for human settlement.

courses.title: Landscape Construction: Topographic Design

courses.title: Landscape Construction: Performance Approaches

Topics range from ecological infrastructure to design with weather patterns. A systematic approach to case studies, landscape technologies, and field trips seeds the knowledge base and representational methods necessary to design and build these complex landscape performances.

courses.title: Plant Ecology + Identification
courses.description: Principles and concepts of plant ecology and regional plant identification; introduction to California native plant species and communities with field trips and case studies.

courses.title: Planting Design
courses.description: Principles of planting design for landscape architecture focusing on form/space and sustainable performance. Planting design strategies for improved planetary health and resilience.

courses.title: Media for Landscape Architecture
courses.description: Development of methods and skills for the study of landscape architecture design and for project presentation, including natural resource and urban mapping.

courses.title: Topics in Media for Landscape Architecture
courses.description: Exploration of emerging techniques for landscape architecture study, presentation and documentation; topics may vary each semester; may be repeated for credit when subject matter is different.

courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design

courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design

courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design

courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design

courses.title: Landscape as Urbanism: Case Studies
courses.description: Cities predominantly in the Global South are studied in relationship to landscape systems. Focus on historic and future urbanization at the interface of natural systems and climate dynamics.

courses.title: Contemporary Theories of Landscape Architecture
courses.description: Explores contemporary landscape architecture theories, propositions and projects in the context of cities. The exploration methodology includes the study of epochal projects and theoretical texts.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Urban Ecology
courses.description: Builds on knowledge related to the impacts of anthropocentrism on our current environmental/landscape condition - stresses on biodiversity, urban heat island, sea-level rise, etc, and strategies at mitigating these conditions - urban forestry, building soils, etc.
courses.recommended_prep: ARCH 531

courses.title: Media for Landscape Architecture: 3D Design
courses.description: Developing and communicating landscape architecture design intent using visualization tools for three-dimensional studies.

Recommended Preparation: ARCH-549.

courses.title: Conservation Methods and Materials
courses.description: Concepts and techniques for building conservation including identification of treatments, recordation and research, material properties and behavior, building forensics, and project implementation. Recommended preparation: ARCH-549.

courses.title: Introduction to Historic Site Documentation
courses.description: Survey of basic guidelines and standards for documentation in historic preservation, including cultural resource surveys, historic structures reports and Historic American Building Survey and Historic American Engineering Record recordation.

courses.title: History of American Architecture and Urbanism
courses.description: History of American architecture and urbanism from prehistory to World War II examined in relation to European influences and indigenous developments.

courses.title: Heritage Conservation Practicum Advanced Documentation

courses.title: Global Perspectives in Heritage Conservation
courses.description: In-depth analysis of international heritage conservation practice with a focus on a single country, continent, or world region outside the United States. Topics will vary from year to year; may be repeated for credit when subject matter is different.

courses.title: Readings in Heritage Conservation Theory
courses.description: Trans-disciplinary intensive reading and discussion course related to issues in contemporary heritage conservation.

courses.title: Sustainable Conservation of the Historic Built Environment
courses.description: Analysis of the intersection between green building and historic resources with an emphasis on stewardship and sustainability.

courses.title: A History of Architectural Theory: 1400-1914

courses.title: Urbanism Themes and Case Studies

courses.title: Architecture Themes and Case Studies

courses.title: Contemporary Architectural Theory

Introduces a range of geometric first principles, technologies and techniques through contemporary design tools.

courses.title: Global History of Designed Landscapes

courses.title: Cross Cultural Topics in Landscape Architecture History

courses.description: Course outlines the building design and its performance diagnostic processes required to assure indoor environmental quality and the building occupants environmental health, productivity, and physiological comfort.

courses.title: Lighting Design

courses.title: Technology-Enabled Architecture, Engineering and Construction

courses.title: Field Studies

courses.title: Introduction to Astronautics
courses.description: Gateway to the Astronautical Engineering major. Introduction to space, space exploration and the space business. Elements of orbits, spacecraft systems, rocket propulsion, and communications. Laboratory: introduction to graphics, computation and simulation.

courses.title: Foundations of Astronautical Engineering
courses.description: Coordinate systems and transformations. Spherical trigonometry. Filtering and estimation. Spacecraft orbits and orbital maneuvers. Rocket propulsion, spacecraft attitude dynamics, spacecraft communications, and space environment.
courses.recommended_prep: Skill in MATLAB programming.

courses.title: Team Projects I
courses.description: Participation in ASTE undergraduate student team projects. Intended for lower-division students or those with little prior project experience. Departmental approval.

courses.title: Astronautical Gas Dynamics
courses.description: Introduction to compressible and rarefied gas flows with applications to rocket propulsion and the dynamics of supersonic and hypersonic vehicles and spacecraft; ionized gases and plasmas.

courses.title: Spacecraft Systems Engineering
courses.description: Spacecraft subsystems and the space environment. Systems engineering as applied to spacecraft. Propulsion; attitude; control and data handling; flight software; telecommunications; power; thermal control; payloads.
courses.recommended_prep: Skill in MATLAB programming and spreadsheets

courses.title: Mission Systems Design
courses.description: Space systems engineering process: requirements definition; trade studies; system integration; technical reviews; cost and schedule development; case studies; ethics. Capstone design experience.

courses.title: Rocket Propulsion
courses.description: Liquid- and solid-fueled engines. Adiabatic flame temperature. Duct flows with area change, heat addition, mass addition. Rocket heat transfer. Staging. Electric and nuclear thrusters.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic proficiency in a high-level programming language (e.g., MATLAB on the level of TAC 168 or Python on the level of TAC 115)

courses.title: Spacecraft Dynamics
courses.description: Two-body motion. Rigid-body motion. Attitude dynamics and maneuvers. Spacecraft stabilization: gravity gradient, reaction wheels, magnetic torques. Thruster attitude control. Senior standing.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Team Projects II
courses.description: Participation in ASTE undergraduate student team projects. Intended for students with prior project experience. Departmental approval.

courses.title: Special Topics

courses.title: Spacecraft System Design
courses.description: System components; vehicle structure, propulsion systems, flight dynamics, thermal control, power systems, telecommunication. Interfaces and tradeoffs between these components. Testing, system reliability, and integration.

courses.title: Design of Low Cost Space Missions
courses.description: Reviews all aspects of space mission design for practical approaches to reducing cost. Examines "LightSat" mission experience and potential applicability to large scale missions. Graduate standing in engineering or science. Recommended preparation: ASTE 520 or some experience in space engineering.

courses.title: Human Spaceflight
courses.description: Engineering, technologies, and systems for human spaceflight. Life support, space environments, crew accommodations. Mission operations, safety. Astrodynamics, launch and space vehicles, space stations, planetary bases.

courses.title: Space Exploration Architectures Concept Synthesis Studio
courses.description: Programmatic/conceptual design synthesis/choice creation methods for complex space missions. Aerospace system engineering/architecting tools to create innovative projects. Evaluated by faculty/industry/NASA experts. Graduate standing in engineering or science. Recommended preparation: ASTE-520 or experience in space industry

courses.title: Safety of Space Systems and Space Missions
courses.description: Engineering methodology and analysis techniques for safety certification and mission assurance of robotic and human space systems and space missions by government and commercial industry. Recommended preparation: ASTE 520 or some experience in space engineering. Open only to Engineering graduate students.

courses.title: Space Environments and Spacecraft Interactions
courses.description: Space environments and interactions with space systems. Vacuum, neutral and ionized species, plasma, radiation, micrometeoroids. Phenomena important for spacecraft operations.

courses.title: Systems for Remote Sensing from Space
courses.description: The operations and applications of instruments which produce images of ground scene or probe the atmosphere from space. Graduate standing in engineering or physics.

courses.title: Spacecraft Structural Dynamics
courses.description: Applied analytical methods (vibrations of single and multi degree of freedom systems, finite element modeling, spacecraft applications); requirements definition process; analytical cycles; and design verfication. Graduate standing in engineering or science.

courses.title: Human Factors of Spacecraft Operations
courses.description: Engineering fundamentals and experimental methods of human factors design and evaluation for spacecraft which incorporate human-in-the-loop control.

courses.title: Ground Communications for Satellite Operations

courses.title: Liquid Rocket Propulsion
courses.description: Liquid-propelled rocket propulsion systems. Capillary devices for gas-free liquid acquisition in zero gravity. Ground and in-orbit operations. Propellant life predictions and spacecraft end-of-life de-orbiting strategies.

courses.title: Solid Rocket Propulsion
courses.description: Fundamental concepts, implementation and applications of solid rocket propulsion. Propellants, performance, ballistics, structures and systems used for space launch vehicles, sounding rockets and rocket motors.

courses.title: Advanced Spacecraft Propulsion
courses.description: Nuclear, electric, sails, and far-term propulsion systems. Overviews of nozzles, heat transfer, electromagnetics, rarefied gases, and plasma physics. Analysis of electrothermal, electrostatic and electromagnetic thrusters. Graduate standing in engineering or science.

courses.title: Space Launch Vehicle Design
courses.description: Fundamentals, technologies, and design of space launch vehicles. Propulsion, trajectory analysis and optimization, static and dynamic structural loads, stability, control, and safety.
courses.recommended_prep: ASTE 575 or equivalent course work in spacecraft propulsion

courses.title: Rocket and Spacecraft Propulsion
courses.description: Space missions, rocket dynamics, and propulsion requirements. Thermodynamics and combustion; compressible gas dynamics in nozzles. Liquid- and solid-propellant rockets; launch systems. Advanced propulsion.

courses.title: Entry and Landing Systems for Planetary Surface Exploration
courses.description: Multi-disciplinary engineering theory, simulation techniques, and unique technologies for landing robotic and human space vehicles on the surface of planets and moons.
courses.recommended_prep: ASTE 520 or similar course in fundamentals of space systems

courses.description: Physical principles; two-body and central force motion; trajectory correction maneuvers; position and velocity in conic orbits; Lambert's problem; celestial mechanics; orbital perturbations.

courses.title: Orbital Mechanics II
courses.description: Theory of perturbations of orbits; numerical methods in orbital mechanics; satellite dynamics; averaging methods; resonance; mission analysis.

courses.title: Spacecraft Attitude Dynamics
courses.description: Dynamics of systems of particles and rigid bodies; spacecraft attitude systems; attitude maneuvers (spin, precession, nutation, etc.); attitude stabilization and attitude determination; simulation methods.

courses.description: Introduction to astrophysics including stellar parameters, evolution, end states (white dwarfs, supernovae, black holes) and extrasolar planetary systems; emphasis on physical processes and cosmic significance.

courses.title: Galaxies and Large-Scale Structures in the Universe
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Galaxies and clusters of galaxies: their content, structure, dynamics, distribution, and motions; the cosmic microwave background: theory and observation; elements of observational cosmology. Prerequisite: PHYS-153L or PHYS-163L.

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Concepts of space-time, general relativity applied to an homogeneous and expanding universe. Universe's content and thermal history. Introduction to current observational tests of cosmology. Prerequisite: PHYS 153L or PHYS 163L.

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The Universe: its content and thermal history. Density anisotropies: initial conditions, linear and non-linear evolution. Observables, current and future data, theory-observations comparison.

courses.title: Management of Small Businesses
courses.description: Strategic, organizational, financial, and human issues facing the small business.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Starting and managing one's own business: developing a viable concept, organizing the enterprise, market and financial planning, and controlling the organization. (Duplicates credit in BAEP 451)

courses.title: Feasibility Analysis
courses.description: Students develop, analyze, and validate entrepreneurial concepts (including marketing, operational, and financial considerations) using customer feedback and risk assessment to conclude worthiness to pursue.

courses.title: Venture Management
courses.description: Design and application of organization structures and systems in management of new ventures.

courses.title: Venture Initiation: Launching and Scaling Your Startup
courses.description: Learn to build a startup from concept to reality. Focus on real-world entrepreneurial action and execution. Prerequisite: BAEP 452.

courses.title: Founder's Dilemmas
courses.description: Prepares potential founders, hires, and investors for the decisions they will face both before and during their involvement with new ventures.

courses.title: Seminar in Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Perspectives into the art and science of entrepreneurship under the guidance of a master instructor. Specific topics vary.

courses.title: The Entrepreneurial Mindset- Taking the Leap
courses.description: A deeper insight into the entrepreneurial mind, how it approaches opportunities and challenges and gives leadership to an organization.

courses.title: The Science of Peak Performance
courses.description: Ingrains expertise and application of the science of peak performance, broadens preparation for personal challenge, and builds business-centered critical thinking and applied analytical skills.

courses.title: Sales Mindset for Entrepreneurs
courses.description: The sales planning decisions that entrepreneurs make, including how to accelerate startup revenue, what metrics drive success and how to build great sales teams.

courses.title: The Entrepreneur's Guide to Intellectual Property
courses.description: The fundamentals of intellectual property -- its value, its basic workings, and its role in entrepreneurship, business in general, science, the arts, and the professions.

courses.title: Entertainment Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Explore the current entrepreneurial trends and opportunities in the entertainment industry and uncover the key success factors for entrepreneurs in this industry.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Family Business
courses.description: Explores the dynamics of family and privately held businesses. Exploring generational and extended family issues, opportunities and obstacles faced in today's environment.

courses.title: Introduction to Social Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Analysis of social enterprise models from micro-finance to job development. Analysis of basic issues regarding the difference between socially responsible companies, for-profit, and non-profit-run enterprises.

courses.title: Practicum in Business Issues (Internship)
courses.description: Combined classroom discussion and field application of business theories and practices; part-time internship employment. Project to be jointly defined by student, employer and professor. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Field Project in Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Individual or team projects solving real problems for an enterprise. Situation analyses; research proposal composition; field research techniques; statistical analysis; oral and written presentations. Open only to Juniors and Seniors. Graded Credit/No Credit.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Current developments in the field of entrepreneurship: topics to be selected each semester.

courses.title: Introduction to New Ventures
courses.description: Study and development of analytical and conceptual skills in the management of new enterprises and new ventures within large organizations. Duplicates credit in BAEP 549, GSBA 550, GSBA 550ab and GSBA 551.

courses.title: Venture Feasibility
courses.description: Assess the viability of and develop potential new business opportunities through the application of analytic frameworks and field research. Duplicates credit in BAEP 556 and BAEP 566.

courses.title: Cases in New Venture Management
courses.description: Cases and readings expose students to the challenges of developing long-range strategies for entrepreneurial ventures. Case work emphasizes developing new industries, growth through strategic alliances, and issues involved in the long-term strategic positioning of emerging companies.

courses.title: Venture Initiation
courses.description: Learn to launch and scale a new business through entrepreneurial action and execution. Prerequisite: BAEP 552 or BAEP 556 or BAEP 566.

courses.title: Founder's Dilemmas: Anticipate and Avoid Startup Pitfalls
courses.description: Delves into founders' early decisions about when and whether to found, co-founders, hires, and investors that tend to get them into trouble down the road.

courses.title: Technology Feasibility
courses.description: Assess the viability of and develop potential technology business opportunities through the application of analytic frameworks and field research. Duplicates credit in BAEP 552 and BAEP 566.

courses.title: Technology Commercialization
courses.description: Identification, evaluation and commercialization of new technologies. Emphasis will be placed on the legal, financial and marketing aspects of technology transfer and development.

courses.title: The Entrepreneurial Advisor: Problem Solving for Early-Stage Companies
courses.description: Experiential course designed to develop skills in framing and solving complex problems in young companies. Apply skills to real ventures participating in course projects.

courses.title: Investing in New Ventures
courses.description: Focus on the entrepreneurial skill set applied to new venture opportunities. Taught from the business plan reader's point of view; focus on selecting opportunities, structuring the relationship, adding value and realizing the value of that investment.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition
courses.description: Issues faced by the entrepreneur who wishes to acquire an enterprise; appropriateness of an enterprise, understanding funding sources and valuation methods, developing a plan for due diligence, negotiating and consummating the transaction. The acquisition process, approaches to valuation, and the roles of the various parties in negotiating and consummating an acquisition of an existing business.

courses.title: Investing in Impact Ventures

courses.description: Introduction to the scientific method; basic instruction in molecular biology with emphasis on how biological research advancement has impacted medicine, commerce and society in general.

courses.description: Exploration of molecular biology, biochemistry, microbiology, nutrition and the history of biology through the study of food, focusing on food's relationship to the biological world.

courses.title: The Nature of Human Health and Disease
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The human organism; the nature of inherited and acquired diseases;the biological and societal basis for the AIDS epidemic; therapy,drug design and the future. Not available for major credit.

courses.title: Evolution

courses.description: Changes in the physical and biological universe over time; origins of life, dinosaurs, human evolution. Implications of evolutionary mechanisms and mass extinctions for human survival.

courses.title: The Biology of the Brain

courses.title: Introduction to Biological Research

courses.title: Introduction to Microbiology

courses.description: Comparative approach to bacteria, Archaea and viruses; their structure, life cycles, geochemical activity, ecology and nutrition. Fundamentals of metabolism and microbial genetics.
courses.recommended_prep: BISC 312 or BISC 330 or CHEM 330 or CHEM 350

courses.title: The Kingdom Plantae: An Introduction to Botany
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the major lineages of vascular plants by the comparative examination of anatomy, physiology, diversity, evolution and integration of form, function and ecology.

courses.title: General Physiology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Physiological functions of the circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integuementary, musculoskeletal, nervous, respiratory, and urogenital systems in animals. Lecture, 3 hours; Laboratory, 3 hours.

courses.title: Statistical Thinking for Quantitative Biology

courses.description: Introduction to general statistical theory with higher-level mathematics for biological data analysis. Basic programming in R. Discussion of techniques to describe, visualize and model different types of data.

courses.title: Introduction to Ecology

courses.title: Molecular Biology

courses.title: Genetics

courses.title: Mammalogy

courses.title: Applications of Molecular Biology to Medicine
