courses.description: Graphic communication and drawing; Free-hand sketching; Use of CAD software; Drawing in 2-D, including lettering, dimensioning, and detailing; Drawing and modeling in 3-D.

courses.title: Programming for Civil and Environmental Engineers
courses.description: Computer programming, organization of problems for computational solution, flow charts, programming; numerical methods; analysis and solution of civil engineering problems.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Basic concepts of environmental engineering including topics of water, land, energy, air, climate, resource management, human society and professional development.

courses.title: Statistical Data Analysis in Engineering
courses.description: Data exploration and visualization, fundamentals of probability distributions and statistical inference (including notions of confidence interval, maximum likelihood, regression).

courses.title: Statics and Dynamics
courses.description: Statics, kinematics and kinetics of systems of particles and rigid bodies; equivalent force systems; distributed forces and applications; moments of inertia, momentum, energy; vibrations; Eulers equations.

courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Bodies
courses.description: Analysis of stress and strain; axial, flexural, and torsional behavior of slender bars; elastic deflections; combined stresses; introduction to elastic stability and energy methods.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Fluid statics; relative velocity field; total acceleration; divergence theorem; conservation of mass, energy, and momentum applied to engineering problems in laminar and turbulent flow.

courses.title: Computational Methods in Engineering
courses.description: Application of computer-oriented numerical analysis methods and tools to a broad spectrum of practical science and engineering problems. Use of Python, R and computer algebra.

courses.title: Elementary Theory of Structures
courses.description: Deformations and deflections of elastic systems; statically indeterminate beams, arches, and frames; secondary stresses; computer analysis of simple structural systems.

courses.title: Environmental Chemistry and Analysis
courses.description: Physiochemical characterization of water, soil and air; chemical processes in aquatic, atmospheric, and geospheric environments; air, soil and water pollution chemistry and abatement.

courses.title: Risk and Decision Analysis in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to probabilistic concepts and to the formulation and solution of related problems in civil and environmental engineering.

courses.title: Environmental Engineering Microbiology
courses.description: Fundamentals and applications of microbiology in the context of natural and engineered environmental systems.

courses.title: Construction Contracts and Law
courses.description: Legal aspects of property development and construction: land use, construction practices and specifications, architecture and engineering contracts, agency, subcontracting, professional registration, liability, insurance, liens, bonds.

courses.title: Machine Learning for Civil and Environmental Engineers
courses.description: Introduction to machine learning including: regression; classification; unsupervised learning; applications and challenges specific to civil and environmental engineering data; and integration with physics-based modeling.

courses.title: Coastal Engineering and Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of wave motion and coastal wave transformation. Statistical analysis of oceanographic conditions. Basics of coastal infrastructure design and coastal planning.

courses.title: Water Resources and Coastal Engineering
courses.description: Control and utilization of inland and coastal water, quantitative hydrology, groundwater, probability concepts, extreme events, coastal hydrodynamics, wave-structures interactions, multiple purposes water projects, economic study.

courses.title: Water Quality Science and Engineering
courses.description: Water quality criteria and fundamentals of acceptability; processes employed in treatment of water and wastewater; water reclamation and reuse; sustainability in water and wastewater systems.

courses.title: Structural Design I
courses.description: Structural design processes for wood, steel, concrete, and masonry structural beams, columns, and connections; determination of structural loads; framing systems; and applications of structural mechanics to the design process.

courses.title: Structural Design II
courses.description: Design of structural systems in wood, steel, concrete and masonry, and the performance of structural systems for wind and seismic forces.

courses.title: Computational Structural Analysis
courses.description: Analyze continuous beams, trusses and frame structures using analytical methods and Matlab programming; finite element analysis of plane stress problems, steel beams and concrete beam-column joints.

courses.title: Introduction to Structural Dynamics
courses.description: Response of single and multiple degree of freedom systems to dynamic excitation; structural modeling and approximate solutions; introduction to earthquake resistant design.

courses.title: Construction Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the construction processes; estimating and bidding, construction administration, planning and scheduling, equipment and methods, labor relations, cost control systems, safety and ethics.

courses.title: Construction Estimating
courses.description: Fundamental principles and practices of advanced building cost estimating using Revit Models and industry standard databases.
courses.recommended_prep: CE 460

courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: Fundamentals of the engineering behavior of soil: soil composition and minerology, soil classification, compaction, vertical and lateral stresses, seepage, strength, compressibility; common geotechnical laboratory tests

courses.title: Sustainable Design and Construction
courses.description: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED); green building strategies; carbon footprinting; calculating the embodied energy of building materials; cyclical processes in design and construction.

courses.title: Building Information Modeling: Project Visualization and Sim
courses.description: Building Information Modeling, current BIM technologies; coordination of design and construction; information management throughout building lifecycle; project visualization and simulation for integrated practice.

courses.title: Principles of Transportation Engineering
courses.description: Planning, design, construction, maintenance, and operation of facilities for air, water, rail and highway transit systems.

courses.title: Civil and Environmental Engineering Capstone Design
courses.description: Civil and Environmental Engineering capstone design project incorporating all disciplines of Civil Engineering and Environmental Engineering.

courses.title: Subsurface Foundation Design
courses.description: Site exploration and characterization; analysis and design of structural foundations, including spread footings, mats, piles and drilled shafts; retaining wall and braced excavation design.

courses.title: Engineering Economics in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Principles of engineering economics; modeling and evaluation of receipts and outlays timing; relevance to and applications within Civil and Environmental Engineering projects.

courses.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Design
courses.description: Engineering design of unit operations and processes for water and wastewater treatment: coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, disinfection; primary, secondary, tertiary, advanced treatment; sludge treatment and processing.

courses.title: Innovation in Engineering & Design: Global Grand Challenges
courses.description: The innovative and human-centered design of products, services, and technologies to help solve the needs of people affected by global crises

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Architecture, Engineering and Construction Practices
courses.description: Systems, processes, and constraints governing the initiation, direction, engineering, and delivery of major construction projects. Professional construction management, responsibilities, and practice.

courses.title: Data Management for Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.description: The basics of databases and database management systems as applied to engineering problems. Introduction to data mining concepts, techniques and knowledge discovery in database principles.

courses.title: Seismic Design of Structures
courses.description: Seismic hazard analysis; seismic code provisions; seismic design of steel and concrete structures, floor diaphragms, foundation systems; protective systems design; post-earthquake safety assessment procedures.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of reinforced concrete and structural steel design on the level of CE 456 and CE 457.

courses.title: Game Theory for Interactive Autonomy
courses.description: Game-theoretic modeling of strategic interactions between autonomous systems and humans. Autonomous driving, collaborative robotics, multi-agent decision-making. Nash Equilibrium, reinforcement learning.
courses.recommended_prep: Multivariable calculus on the level of MATH 229; probability theory on the level of MATH 407; basic coding skills on the level of CE 108.

courses.title: Climate Change and Atmospheric Aerosols
courses.description: Climate change; climate science fundamentals; Earth's energy balance and atmosphere; greenhouse gas dynamics; fundamentals of airborne particles; climate-aerosol interactions; particle-radiation and particle-cloud interactions.
courses.recommended_prep: ENE 428

courses.title: Quantifying Uncertainty in Civil & Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to uncertainty quantification; fundamentals of probability theory, forward propagation of uncertainties, probabilistic inference from data; civil and environmental engineering applications.
courses.recommended_prep: Calculus and linear algebra on the level of MATH 245. Programming and basic knowledge of Python or Matlab on the level of CE 108 or ITP 115.

courses.title: Data Analytics in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Application of Fourier series, wavelets, auto-regressive models and Markov models to civil engineering systems. Introduction to deep learning methods and applications to time series analysis.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra on the level of MATH 245, programming on the level of CE 108 or ITP 115 or ITP 168 or CSCI 102.

courses.title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
courses.description: Fundamental and design-oriented understanding of the "state-of-the-practice" of geotechnical earthquake engineering, related to analysis and design of foundations, slopes and retaining walls.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of soil phase parameters and phase relations; effective stress concepts; and soil strength parameters and laboratory strength testing procedures on the level of CE 467L

courses.title: Retaining Structures and Slope Stability
courses.description: Principles and practices underlying analysis, design, construction and stability of retaining walls, braced excavations and slopes.
courses.recommended_prep: A course in Geotechnical Engineering/Soil Mechanics at the level of CE 467L

courses.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete
courses.description: Advanced beam flexural analysis; shear behavior of beams; beam-columns and interaction diagrams; torsion; structural wall design; analysis of D-regions; nonlinear behavior of RC systems.
courses.recommended_prep: CE 457; CE 225 or AME 204; CHEM 105AL or CHEM 115AL; PHYS 152L

courses.title: Modeling and Analysis of Tall and Special Structures
courses.description: Integration of structural modeling with the analysis and design of tall and special structures to resist earthquake motion through inelastic response.
courses.recommended_prep: Experience with ETABS and SAP

courses.title: Dynamics of Structures
courses.description: Forced vibrations of discrete and distributed systems; energy methods; analytical dynamics; computational techniques; approximate methods; random vibration concepts; nonstationary response; structural control; nonlinear system response.

courses.title: Aquatic Chemistry
courses.description: Quantitative prediction of chemical speciation in aquatic systems, including acid-base chemistry, precipitation/dissolution, complexation, oxidation/reduction and phase partitioning of organics. Applications to water treatment.
courses.recommended_prep: General chemistry (CHEM 105aLg and CHEM 105bL); differential and integral calculus (MATH 125 and MATH 129); linear algebra (MATH 245); basic mechanics and conservation of energy (PHYS 151).

courses.title: Construction Planning and Preconstruction
courses.description: The steps and processes for the planning and pre-construction phases of a project using tools and technologies for budgeting, scheduling and planning.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of construction practices at the level of CE 501

courses.title: Fundamental Concepts of Computing and Programming in Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Concepts of computing and programming related to engineering; Form and operation of modern computational devices; Data structures and algorithms that support CEE software applications.

courses.description: Principles of physical chemistry relevant for the life sciences: thermodynamics, chemical equilibria, molecular dynamics, kinetics, molecular structures and interactions, spectroscopy, statistical thermodynamics and macromolecular structures. Duplicates credit in CHEM 430a.

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Atomic structure, theory of bonding, molecular structure, metallic state, coordination compounds, transition and nontransition metals, magnetic and optical properties, crystal field theory, mechanism of reactions.

courses.title: Chemical Nanotechnology

courses.description: Studies in the fundamental principles governing nanoscale materials. Structure and chemical bonding, preparative methods, and electrical, optical and magnetic properties of nanoscale materials and applications.

courses.title: Properties and Sustainability of Polymers

courses.title: Advanced Chemical Biology Laboratory

courses.title: Introduction to Theory & Practice of X-Ray Crystallography

courses.description: Introduction to single crystal X-ray diffraction theory and its extension to two-dimensional diffraction. Application of modern instrumentation and software techniques to problems of current chemical interest.

courses.title: Structure and Bonding in Inorganic and Organometallic Chemis

courses.title: Advanced Chemical Biology

courses.title: Advanced Chemical Biology

courses.title: Basic Principles of Physical Methods in Biochemistry

courses.title: Structure and Mechanism in Organic Chemistry

courses.title: Synthetic Organic Chemistry

courses.title: Introduction to Molecular Spectroscopy

courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Chemistry

courses.title: Community Health Science Administration, Assessment and Eval

courses.title: Health Assessment
courses.description: The importance of health assessment; identification of strategies to understand the needs and priorities of a healthy community.

courses.title: Practicum 1

courses.title: Practicum 2

courses.title: Community Health Funding and Support
courses.description: Approaches to the generation and allocation of financial support for community oral health policies, programs and systems.

courses.title: Practicum 3

courses.title: Introduction to Literary Theory

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Trends and genres in Arabic literature from the classical (pre-modern), through the modern and contemporary periods. In English.

courses.title: Decadence and Modernity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of the notion of "decadence" and its impact on modern and contemporary literary/cultural production, with a comparatist focus on different linguistic traditions.

courses.title: Fictions of the First Person
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of prose fiction in the first person as a model of fiction in general and as a reflection of the fictional structure of selfhood.

courses.title: Modern Arab Culture and Literature
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines contemporary Arab state-society relations using literature to illustrate how people construct meanings and portray issues of national, social, and cultural significance.

courses.title: Modernist Fiction
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of the Modernist aesthetic in narrative texts by Gide, Joyce, Kafka, Woolf and others; possible focus on related trends in other literary traditions.

courses.title: Fictions of Africa
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to African cultural history by way of a comparative study of major literary works and intellectual thought from representative regions and countries in Africa.

courses.title: Psychoanalysis and the Arts

courses.description: Introduction to psychoanalytic literature on the arts, including classic texts by Freud, Jones, Lacan, Derrida, and others. Readings of theoretical and fictional works.

courses.description: A historical and theoretical study of flamenco's aesthetic, social, political and philosophical implications in Spanish culture. Relate flamenco to other artistic and cultural practices and questions of national, ethnic, racial, class, gender or sexual identity.

courses.title: Utopias
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of selected utopias in their historical context as "no places" whose projections of alternate cultures always comment on their own.

courses.title: Dante

courses.title: Soundtracks of Our Lives
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The reciprocal, ideological relations between modes of listening, sounds, music; and literature, film, culture. Examines a range of issues in auditory culture across a broad historical span.

courses.title: Literature, Theory, History
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the relation between historical and theoretical approaches to literary works.

courses.title: Los Angeles Crime Fiction
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The noir tradition in books and films set in Los Angeles. Emphasis on generic conventions, representations of the city, and discourses of class, gender, race.

courses.title: Family in Theory and Literature
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Representations of the family in literary works and films across different cultures and historical periods. Readings in anthropology, philosophy, psychoanalysis, and feminist and gender theory.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Writing of an honors thesis under individual faculty supervision.

courses.title: Teaching Practicum for Graduate Students
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Practical principles for the long-term development of effective teaching within College disciplines. Intended for teaching assistants in Dornsife college.

courses.title: Sound Clash: Popular Music and American Culture

courses.description: Music as inter-cultural communication and method for exploring race and ethnicity in the constitution of American culture and American self; role of music industry.

courses.description: Cultural, social, political, and economic dynamics of communication technologies, including internet architecture, social media, participatory cultures, privacy, surveillance, networked journalism, big data, algorithms, online activism.

courses.title: Media and Society

courses.title: The Business and Culture of Celebrity

courses.description: Employs the concept of "celebrity" as an optic through which to view and assess some of the key aspects of the communication revolution.

schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

courses.title: The Evolution of K-Pop

courses.description: Examines the various stages of K-pop's transformations and related issues in the process of its rise as a global popular culture.

courses.title: Argumentation and Advocacy

courses.title: Intercultural Communication

courses.description: Cultural variables and social psychological processes that influence intercultural interaction; relationship between communication and culture in diverse settings including business, medicine, and education.

courses.title: Rhetoric in Classical Culture

courses.description: Social and economic impacts of information and communication technologies; social factors that shape technological change; issues include access, privacy, freedom of expression, productivity, democratic control.

courses.title: Los Angeles: Communication and Culture

courses.title: Media Consumption

courses.title: The Rhetoric of London

courses.description: Examination of the modern city as a communicative text with London as the case study.

courses.title: Community Engagement and Service Learning

courses.title: Public Diplomacy and Global Citizenship

courses.title: Media Technologies and Free Speech

courses.title: Forensics Laboratory

courses.title: Sports, Communication and Culture
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

courses.title: Interpreting Popular Culture
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

courses.title: Sports and Social Change
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Application of critical, sociological and rhetorical theories to sports events and sport media; examination of the role of sports in enacting social change.

courses.title: Ethics in Human Communication

courses.description: Value perspectives on communication in varied settings: interpersonal, organizational, and public. Issues of truth and responsibility in family and social interactions, advertising, and governmental communication.

courses.title: The Rhetoric of Rome
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Examination of the modern city as a communicative text with Rome as the case study.

courses.title: Fashion, Media and Culture

courses.description: Fashion as a form of communication and culture; fashion's role in identity, body politics, art, nationhood, celebrity and Hollywood culture, youth cultures and subversive practices.

courses.title: Seminar in Communication

courses.title: Canceled, Shamed, Accused: Contemporary Crisis Communication

courses.title: Public Diplomacy in Los Angeles

courses.title: The Internet, Economy and Society

courses.title: Global Entertainment

courses.title: Italian Media: Popes, Politicians, and Popular Culture

courses.title: Music as Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Examines music's unique characteristics as a communicative form and the cultural, economic, political and social influences in music interpretation and production.

courses.title: Podcasting: Origin Stories
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

courses.title: Critical Theories of Sport

courses.title: Global Networks of Sport

courses.title: Perspectives on the Networked Press

courses.title: Visual Communication and Social Change

courses.title: Entertainment, Marketing and Culture

courses.title: Advanced Issues in Communication and Technology
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

courses.title: Crisis and Culture: The Anthropocene
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Critically examines four key dimensions of the Anthropocene -- climate change, mass extinction, reproductive justice and pandemics -- from a cultural studies approach.
courses.recommended_prep: COMM 206, COMM 309

courses.title: Campaign Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Problems in political communication: creating an informed electorate, use of mass media, factors in voter persuasion. Guest experts in political analysis, opinion polling, communication evaluation.

courses.title: Directed Research

courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduatecredit. Available to juniors and seniors only.

courses.title: Research Practicum
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Students gain research experience in the design, implementation, analysis, and reporting of communication research. Students serve as research assistants to faculty members. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Honors Seminar
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Advanced study of issues in communication; recent developments in communication and rhetorical theories. Open only to students in COMM honors program; recommended for seniors. Recommended preparation: COMM 301L.

courses.title: Honors Thesis
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Writing of the honors thesis. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Entertainment and Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Examines social and political controversies over conflicting ethical standards for communication in a variety of media: mass-media, communication technology and entertainment.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Selected topics in communication.

courses.title: Theoretical Approaches to Multidisciplinary Design Projects
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Focuses on theories and research in communication and social sciences to bridge disciplines to produce a proposal, business plan, publication, or a research project.

courses.title: Social Movements as Rhetorical Form
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Study of the rhetoric of social change; methodologies for analysis and appraisal; investigation of specific collective protest and reform movements. Not open to M.A. in Communication Management majors.

courses.title: Humanistic and Social Scientific Approaches to Human Communication I
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Overview of humanistic and social scientific approaches to the study of communication; emphasis on rhetorical/critical and macro social scientific perspectives. Not open to M.A. in Communication Management majors.

courses.title: Humanistic and Social Scientific Approaches to Human Communication II
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Overview of humanistic and social scientific approaches to the study of communication; emphasis on macro and micro social scientific, symbolic, and structural perspectives. Not open to M.A. in Communication Management majors,

courses.title: Quantitative Research Methods in Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Epistemological assumptions, design, and beginning methods of quantitative analysis in communication research.

courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Developing expertise in qualitative methods, including participant-observation, ethnography, discourse analysis and historiography in communication research.

courses.title: Data Science for Communication and Social Networks
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Learn to harness the power of data science and computational techniques to study social and communication networks and extract value, knowledge and insights from big data.
courses.recommended_prep: DSCI 552

courses.title: Black Popular Culture: Theory and Central Debates
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Examines black popular cultures as indexes for historical struggles over race, gender, nationalism, identity, subjectivity, aesthetics, institutional resources, political/cultural autonomy, and ideology.

courses.title: Seminar in Science and Technology Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in the interdisciplinary field of Science and Technology Studies.

courses.title: Human-AI Interaction
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: The impact of AI-powered technology on human interaction, examining how related theories, research and design practices co-evolve with technological advancement.

courses.title: Networked Publics: Theories and Encounters
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Examines models of a democratic public sphere, with special focus on design and use of networked information infrastructures supporting free speech.

courses.title: Fandom, Participatory Culture and Web 2.0
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Emerging models of audience engagement and participation in a networked culture with a strong focus on grassroots communities and their relationships with cult media content.

courses.title: Media and Politics
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Mass media in American political life, including political reporting, election campaigns, non-electoral politics, and the media as a political issue.

courses.title: Advanced Applied AI for Digital Media Product Development
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: A culmination of foundational training in communication, data science and machine learning. Building AI solutions for digital media and product development.
courses.recommended_prep: Proficiency in Python programming and machine learning fundamentals.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the school. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Global Media Industries
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Conduct research, design and produce a group-based research report and website to assess disruption within Global Media Industries over the past year or two.

courses.description: Conduct original or revised global media and communication research thesis projects for submission to academic journals and conferences.

courses.title: Grant Writing in Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Finding the right grant; how to develop theory, optimize funding, write critial components of grants, form collaborations with experts; how review panels work.

courses.title: Studies in Communication Theory
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Current problems in communication theory and research; advanced, specialized interest areas of individual faculty on the frontiers of knowledge.

courses.title: Interpretive and Cultural Approaches in Organizational Communication
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Interpretive, critical and cultural research in organizational communication; emphasis on narrative approaches to ethnographic studies, critical essays, and quantitative intercultural research in organizational communication.

courses.title: Communication Networks
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Conceptual and analytic issues in network perspectives; emphasis on communication patterns, processes, content, influences and impacts.

courses.title: Network Society
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Advanced research seminar examining the interaction between communication technology, society, economy, politics, and culture from interdisciplinary and cross-cultural perspectives. Not available for degree credit for M.A. in Communication Management students. Not available for Communication Management M.A. students.

courses.title: Survey Construction and Validation
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Principles of survey construction and validation; format selection, sampling, question wording, adaptation for international audiences, response option formats, order, and avoiding acquiesence bias and breakoffs.

courses.title: Experimental and Quasi-Experimental Designs
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Advantages and drawbacks to experimental designs and quasi experimental designs for social research and theory building. Emphasis on how to design and report experiments.

courses.title: Science Fiction as Media Theory
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Considers science fiction as a genre that has consistently reflected on communication technologies and their consequences and the ways science fiction metaphors have shaped media and cultural theory.

courses.title: The Practice of Research
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Translating data into a compelling research narrative, iterating between data analysis and writing.

courses.title: Economic Cultures

courses.description: Explores and analyzes the interaction between culture and economy by observing different types of economic practices.

courses.title: Independent Study

courses.description: A supervised course tailored to specific student interests. The professor and student develop a syllabus that permits exploration of advanced or specialized topics. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Preliminary Research Paper

courses.description: Independent research designed to demonstrate the student's ability to conceptualize, conduct, and present scholarly research. Parallel to COMM 794. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Symbols and Conceptual Systems: Thematic Option Honors Progr
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of the structures through which we shape our experience in religion, philosophy, literature, music, and the visual arts, and of competing theories of interpretation. Students may not take this course on a P/NP basis.

courses.title: Culture and Values: Thematic Option Honors Program
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Systematic reasoning about values and ways of living; close reading of great literary and philosophical works from a range of classical traditions to the present.

courses.title: The Process of Change in Science: Thematic Option Honors Pro
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Critical problems in the development of scientific thought, studied as vehicles for understanding the content and structure of the sciences. Specific subject matter in selected scientific disciplines will be presented. Students may not take this course on a P/NP basis.

courses.title: Change and the Future: Thematic Option Honors Program
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of historical change; social and political theory and revolutionary thought; introduction to competing images of future states of affairs; the continuing process of change. Students may not take this course on a P/NP basis.

courses.title: Writing Seminar I: Thematic Option Honors Program
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The first level writing course focuses on the relationship between critical thinking and analytic writing through the close reading of primary texts. Seminars are supplemented with biweekly one-on-one tutorials.

courses.title: Writing Seminar II: Thematic Option Honors Program
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Instruction on analytic writing that integrates methods of research, identifying and addressing specific audiences and presenting ideas publicly. Readings examine modernity and postmodernity.
courses.recommended_prep: CORE 111

courses.title: Liberal Arts Reading Salon
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Critical readings of a series of texts in the liberal arts designed to promote discussion of important themes, theoretical approaches, research directions, and interdisciplinary connections. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Modes of Inquiry
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Modern tools of cultural and discursive analysis which seek to demystify "the natural," as it appears in the formation of cultures, their institutions, and individuals.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive interdisciplinary exploration of a selected theme, problem, process, or period.

courses.title: Teaching Analytical Writing through Readings in the Humanities
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories and practices in university-level teaching of close-reading and analytical writing, using texts central to Western tradition. Graduate student professionalization throught topical workshops and discussions. Open to assistant lecturers and teaching assistants only. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Histories of Art, Design and Visual Culture
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: A loosely chronological, thematic survey of art, visual culture, design, and critical theory from the early modern period through modernism (1500 1950).

courses.title: Critical Theory in Art, Design and Visual Culture
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: An issues-based introduction to critical theory in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, especially as it relates to philosophy, art, design, and visual culture.
courses.recommended_prep: CRIT 150

courses.title: Global Art, Design and Visual Culture since 1960
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: A critical history of art, design, visual culture, and visual theory since 1960, addressing through a postcolonial/decolonial lens the concepts and practices of "global" art.
courses.recommended_prep: CRIT 150 and CRIT 160

courses.title: Race, Fashion and Pop Culture
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Exploration of fashion, pop culture, entertainment, beauty and style politics through the lens of race, class and gender.
courses.recommended_prep: CRIT 150

courses.title: Identity and Visual Representation
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: A critical study of the relationship between identity or coalitional politics and specific practices, meanings, and sitings of contemporary art and design.
courses.recommended_prep: CRIT 150, CRIT 160, CRIT 350 or permission of instructor

courses.title: Performing and Visualizing the City
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Explores the relationships among art, design, visual culture, urban spaces and institutions, through urban, social and visual theory.
courses.recommended_prep: CRIT 150gp, CRIT 160g, CRIT 350gw or permission of instructor

courses.title: Theory and History of Performance Studies
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Exploration of the various theories and methodologies associated with performance and visual studies as interrelated with the histories of practice in these fields.

courses.title: History and Theory of Art and Exhibitions
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Gives broad and deep overview of history of art as a conceptual and practical category, emphasizing development of exhibitionary sites and engagement with public sphere.

courses.title: Art and Curatorial Visits
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Site visits relating to art and curatorial practices, from art museums and artists studios to public art offices and performance venues, and meet professionals.

courses.title: Visiting Artist and Scholar Seminar
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Lecture and discussion course in the professional practice of art featuring formal presentations by visiting artists and scholars. (Duplicates credit in FA 515)

courses.title: Methods of Curating: Introduction to Curatorial Practicum
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: First in a sequence of three courses on history/theory of curatorial methods, with practical experience necessary to mounting exhibitions and devising interfaces with the public. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 555a)

courses.title: Curatorial Practicum: Individual/Group Projects
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Second in a sequence of three courses on history/theory of curatorial methods, with practical experience necessary to mounting exhibitions and devising interfaces with the public. Prerequisite: CRIT 555. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 555b)

courses.title: Curatorial Practicum: Group Project Summation
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Third in a sequence of three courses on history/theory of curatorial methods, with practical experience necessary to mounting exhibitions and devising interfaces with the public. Prerequisite: CRIT 556. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 555c)

courses.title: Performance Theory and Praxis
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Social Practice as a transitional platform for intersectional themes between visual art, media culture, political advocacy, policy making and public space.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 590)

courses.title: Field Internship Experience
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Supervised internship in an art institution or an art agency, or with an independent curator or artist, on projects and research specific to public space. Recommended preparation: Completion of first year of courses. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 591)

courses.title: Master's Thesis

courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 594a)

courses.title: Master's Thesis
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Recommended preparation: 28 units of coursework. Graded IP/CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 594b)

courses.title: Master's Thesis
schools: Roski School of Art and Design
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Recommended preparation: 28 units of coursework. Graded IP/CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 594z)

courses.title: Explorations in Computing
courses.description: A behind-the-scenes overview of the computational/algorithmic principles that form the basis of today's digital society. Exploration areas include social media, web search, videogames and location-based services.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of algorithmic thinking as a primer to programming. Introduction to C++.

courses.title: Object Oriented Programming
courses.description: Basic datatypes, assignments, control statements (if, switch, for, while), input/output (printf, scanf, cin, cout), functions, arrays, structures, recursion, dynamic memory, file handling. Programming in C/C++.

courses.title: Data Structures
courses.description: Data structures including linked lists, balanced search trees, heaps, hash tables; probability and number theory applicable to the analysis of randomized data structures.

courses.title: Programming Fundamentals for Computing
courses.description: Introduction to Python and C++ with examples from various domains in computational science; intended for students without prior programming experience.

courses.title: Programming for Applications of Computing
courses.description: Solutions to computational science problems using Python and C++; data structures; searching and sorting algorithms; computational efficiency.

courses.title: Discrete Methods in Computer Science
courses.description: Boolean algebra, propositional and first-order logic, proof techniques. Sets, functions, series, summations. Big-O notation; algorithm analysis. Recursion; basic sorting algorithms. Graphs and basic graph algorithms.

courses.title: Principles of Software Development
courses.description: Object-Oriented Programming in Java; using Java threads, Web Services and SQL to write client/server applications; team project; vibe coding with AI tools.

courses.title: Introduction to Algorithms and Theory of Computing
courses.description: Algorithm analysis. Greedy algorithms, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, graph algorithms. NP-completeness and basic recursion theory and undecidability. Sorting lower bounds. Number-theory based cryptography.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the software engineering process and software lifecycle. Covers project management, requirements, architecture, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance phase activities in team based projects. Prerequisites: CSCI 201. Duplicates credit in former CSCI 377.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Operating Systems
courses.description: Basic issues in concurrency, deadlock control, synchronization scheduling, memory management, protection and access control, inter-process communication, and structured design. Laboratory experiences with Unix-like operating system.

courses.title: Internetworking
courses.description: Global Internet: design principles, layering, protocol design/analysis. Networked applications, Internet structure/architecture, Protocols for transport/congestion control, network layer/routing, link layer/MAC. Network security.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with C and C++.

courses.title: Computer Systems
courses.description: Computer organization; entity abstraction and representation; program execution; code optimization; memory usage; exception handling; processing control; computer performance; hands-on work done in C and assembly.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence: Principles and Foundations
courses.description: Concepts and algorithms underlying the understanding and construction of intelligent systems. Agents, problem solving, search, representation, reasoning, planning, machine learning.

courses.title: Cross-Platform App Development
courses.description: Programming applications with dynamic graphical user interfaces. Topics include events, controls, resources, data bindings, styles and user experience.

courses.title: Video Game Programming
courses.description: Underlying concepts and principles required for programming video games (topics include vectors, transformations, 3-D math, geometric primitives, matrices).

courses.title: Capstone: Design and Construction of Large Software Systems
courses.description: Group project with an outside stakeholder to develop real-world software solutions to large-scale problems. Topics include software engineering, professional preparation, and recent computer science research. Duplicates credit in CSCI 477a and CSCI 477b.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Concurrency, deadlock control, synchronization, process and thread scheduling, memory management, file systems, security and access control, communication and networking, distributed file systems, data management. Duplicates credit in CSCI 350.
courses.recommended_prep: CSCI 201 or CSCI 455; CSCI 356 or EE 352

courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.description: Computer graphics, OpenGL, 2D and 3D transformations, Bzier splines, computer animation, rendering including ray tracing, shading and lighting, artistic rendering, virtual reality, visualization.

courses.title: Game Prototyping
courses.description: Developing games or technology based on current and relevant special topics.

courses.title: Computer and Network Security
courses.description: A broad overview of security threats and defenses, security systems and functionalities. Includes homeworks and in-class exercises to provide practical experience working with such systems. Prerequisite: CSCI 104.

courses.title: Principles of Functional Programming
courses.description: An introduction to alternative programming paradigms including functional programming and logic programming.

courses.title: Professional C++
courses.description: Applications of advanced concepts in C++ including lambda expressions, templates, secure coding, parallel programming, writing performant code, CMake and continuous integration.

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Natural language processing; language modeling; deep neural networks for language processing; language technologies and their socioeconomic and societal impacts.
courses.recommended_prep: Fluency with Python programming on the level of ITP 216 or TAC 216

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Networks
courses.description: Network architectures; layered protocols, network service interface; local, wide area, wireless networks; Internet protocols; link protocols; addressing; routing; flow control; software defined network; multimedia networks.

courses.title: Parallel and Distributed Computation
courses.description: Introduction to parallel programming techniques, models and optimization strategies; Application mapping to multi-core, accelerator, GPU and cloud platforms; High Performance Computing and Data Science applications.
courses.recommended_prep: High-level programming

courses.title: System-on-Chip
courses.description: Design flow, tools, and issues related to System/Network-on-Chip (S/Noc) design for real-time embedded systems with applications in mobile, cloud, aerospace, and medical electronics.

courses.title: Computer Systems Organization
courses.description: Register Transfer level machine organization; performance; arithmetic; pipelined processors; exceptions, out-of-order and speculative execution, cache, virtual memory, multi-core multi-threaded processors, cache coherence.

courses.title: Numerical Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Rounding errors in digital computation; solution of linear algebraic systems; Newton's method for nonlinear systems; matrix eigenvalues; polynomial approximation; numerical integration; numerical solution of ordinary differential equations.
courses.recommended_prep: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development
courses.description: Hands-on AI: data mining, machine learning, optimization and fairness in the context of applications with environmental and societal benefit.
courses.recommended_prep: Python programming skills. Courses that use Python (depending on instructor) include: CSCI 113, CSCI 353, CSCI 360, CSCI 445, EE 250, EE 364, TAC 115, and TAC 116.

courses.title: Foundations of Machine Learning
courses.description: Algorithms for learning behavior from data, including both mathematical underpinnings and practical techniques. Covers supervised learning, deep learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning.
courses.recommended_prep: CSCI 360, comfortable with mathematical derivations, such as those in MATH 225; comfortable with manipulating vectors and matrices

courses.title: Theory of Computation
courses.description: History of the theory of computing, foundational theorems and theoretical frameworks of computer science, solvable and unsolvable problems.

courses.title: Cryptography: Secure Communication and Computation
courses.description: Introduction to modern Cryptography; Mathematical/algorithmic studies of methods for protecting information in computer and communication systems: Public-Key Cryptosystems, zero-knowledge proofs, data privacy. Prerequisites: CSCI 270.

courses.title: Programming Game Engines
courses.description: Building the core components of a modern 3D game engine including shaders, animation, collision detection, artificial intelligence algorithms, multithreading and profiling.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Advanced Game Project
courses.description: Design, iterative prototyping, and development of a 1st playable level.

courses.title: Advanced Game Project
courses.description: The practice of design in various areas of game production, iterative stage two prototyping and development of refined videogame.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of game design at the level of CTIN 489L

courses.title: Senior Project
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An original project will be constructed applying computer technology (in either hardware or software) to produce a result useful in the physics classroom or laboratory.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics in computer science.

courses.title: Numerical Analysis and Computation
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Linear equations and matrices, Gauss elimination, error estimates, iteration techniques; contractive mappings, Newton's method; matrix eigenvalue problems; least-squares approximation, Newton-Cotes and Gaussian quadratures; finite difference methods. Prerequisite: linear algebra and calculus.

courses.title: Numerical Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Computational linear algebra; solution of general nonlinear systems of equations; approximation theory using functional analysis; numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations.

courses.title: Applied Probability
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Probability spaces; properties of probability and expectation; discrete and continuous random variables; indicator method; conditioning; transformations; laws of large numbers; Central Limit Theorem without measure theory

courses.title: Applied Probability
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Markov processes in discrete or continuous time; renewal processes; martingales; brownian motion and diffusion theory; random walks, inventory models, population growth, queuing models, shot noise.

courses.title: Games as a Service and Live Operations: Foundations
courses.description: Fundamentals of free-to-play game development and live operations; creation of original prototypes; and measurement of player engagement.
courses.recommended_prep: Introductory games coursework on the level of CTIN 458, CTIN 488, or CTIN 489 is helpful but not required.

courses.title: Games as a Service and Live Operations: Development
courses.description: Take a Live Operations game from concept through pre-production and production planning to a playable Alpha level. Build new modes, mechanics, systems, and content.
courses.recommended_prep: Foundational games coursework on the level of CSCI-507.

courses.title: Games as a Service and Live Operations: Launch
courses.description: Take a Live Operations game from Alpha through beta versions to a polished launch candidate; iterative usability testing and player metrics; plan post-launch operations.
courses.recommended_prep: Foundational and developmental games coursework on the level of CSCI-507 and CSCI-508.

courses.title: Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems
courses.description: Components, software and applications of cyber-physical systems; autonomy; control techniques; development and testing; artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms.
courses.recommended_prep: Fundamentals of control and automata theory; familiarity with Matlab, Simulink, and R

courses.title: Research Methods and Analysis for User Studies
courses.description: Introduction to research methods and data analysis techniques for human subject research; experimental research design, correlational research, data analysis, ensuring validity and ethics.

courses.title: Computer Animation and Simulation
courses.description: Fundamental techniques of computer animation and simulation, knowledge and/or experience in the design, scripting, production and post-production stages of computer animation. Prerequisite: CSCI-420 or CSCI-580. Recommendedpreparation: Familiarity with calculus, linear algebra, and numerical computation; C/C++ programming skills.

courses.title: Game Engine Development
courses.description: The principles of developing game engines targeted at modern PC and game console hardware.

courses.title: Advanced Mobile Devices and Game Consoles
courses.description: Explore the complex engineering process required to design and build a real-time graphics engine to support physical realism on mobile devices. Recommended preparation: CSCI 420 or CSCI 580 or an equivalent course in graphics.

courses.title: Graduate Advanced Game Project
courses.description: Team projects intended to address the multifaceted technical and creative challenges that are inherent to comprehensive game development.
courses.recommended_prep: CSCI 522 or CTIN 488

courses.title: Graduate Advanced Game Project
courses.description: The practice of design in various areas of game production, iterative stage two prototyping and development of a refined videogame.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of interactive design and production at the level of CTIN 532L

courses.title: Security Systems
courses.description: Protecting computer networks and systems using cryptography, authentication, authorization, intrusion detection and response. Includes lab to provide practical experience working with such systems.

courses.title: Applied Cryptography
courses.description: Intensive overview of cryptography for practitioners, historical perspective on early systems, number theoretic foundations of modern day cryptosystems and basic cryptanalysis.

courses.title: Innovation for Defense Applications
courses.description: Development of problem statements and innovative software prototypes for defense, intelligence and homeland security applications; team projects; hands-on experience.
courses.recommended_prep: An introductory programming class such as CSCI 103 and the ability to write short programs or scripts to manipulate data.

courses.title: Algebraic Combinatorics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Combinatorics motivated by Representation Theory and Algebraic Geometry. Topics may include: representations of the symmetric group, symmetric functions, Young tableaux and plane partitions, permutation enumeration.

courses.title: Multimodal Probabilistic Learning of Human Communication
courses.description: Principles and techniques to understand, build, and utilize multimodal machine learning algorithms through automatically understanding, recognizing, and analyzing phenomena of human communication. Recommended preparation: CSCI 542 or CSCI 567 or CSCI 573 or equivalent.

courses.title: Linear Programming and Extensions
courses.description: Linear programming models for resource allocation; simplex and revised simplex methods; duality; sensitivity; transportation problems; selected extensions to large scale, multiobjective and special structured models.

courses.title: Augmented, Virtual and Mixed Reality
courses.description: Technical design and implementation of immersive environments; visual simulations, interactive 3D graphics and games.
courses.recommended_prep: CSCI 420 or CSCI 580

courses.title: Foundations of Modern Data Management and Processing
courses.description: Modern database system architectures; indexing for analytical and transactional workloads, query pipelining; materialization, vectorization, optimization, scheduling; join algorithms, consistency and concurrency control.
courses.recommended_prep: SQL and basics of database management systems: indexing structures (hash and B+-tree), query optimization, query execution, concurrency control, transaction processing techniques, crash recovery protocols (CSCI-485 or CSCI-585). Good programming skills, preferably in C/C++ languages (CSCI-103).

courses.title: Applied Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Introduction to key components of human language technologies, including: information extraction, sentiment analysis, question answering, machine translation.

courses.title: Distributed Systems
courses.description: The theory and practice of distributed systems. Topics include: distributed storage systems, fault tolerance, consensus, consistency, transactions, distributed data processing and efficient cloud computing.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of operating systems at the level of CSCI 350 and computer systems at the level of CSCI 356. Strong C++ experience is highly recommended.

courses.title: Computer Networking
courses.description: Protocol design for computer communication networks, network routing, transport protocols, internetworking.
courses.recommended_prep: C-language programming

courses.title: Introduction to Cryptography
courses.description: Modern secret codes. Public key cryptosystems of Rivest- Shamir-Adleman, Diffie-Hellman and others. The underlying number theory and computational complexity theory.

courses.title: Computer Systems Architecture
courses.description: Computer architecture from a design perspective: Pipelined processors, speculative execution, VLIW, vector processors, GPU/GPGPU, memory technology and systems, interconnection networks, shared-memory and message-passing multiprocessors, chip multiprocessors.

courses.title: Machine Learning I: Supervised Methods
courses.description: Distribution-free and probabilistic methods for supervised classification and regression; learning algorithms; optimization techniques; feature-space transformations; parametric and nonparametric methods; Bayes decision theory; artificial neural networks.
courses.recommended_prep: knowledge of Python at the level of EE 541 (A Computational Introduction to Deep Learning); knowledge of multivariate calculus.

courses.title: Building Knowledge Graphs
courses.description: Foundations, techniques and algorithms for building knowledge graphs and doing so at scale. Topics include information extraction, data alignment, entity linking and the Semantic Web.
courses.recommended_prep: DSCI 553 and Experience programming in Python

courses.title: Deep Learning and Its Applications
courses.description: Deep learning research in computer vision, natural language processing and robotics; neural networks; deep learning algorithms, tools and software.
courses.recommended_prep: CSCI 567, Python programming, calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, knowledge of machine learning

courses.title: Web Technologies
courses.description: Study of client-side and server-side Web programming languages, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin. Vibe coding with IDEs, AI Assistants and LLMs.
courses.recommended_prep: knowledge of at least two programming languages.

courses.title: Information Retrieval and Web Search Engines
courses.description: Examines key aspects of information retrieval as they apply to search engines; web crawling, indexing, querying and quality of results are studied.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity in programming in multiple languages, C, C++, and/or Java and experience with a database

courses.title: Quantum Computing and Quantum Cryptography
courses.description: Introduction to quantum computing and quantum cryptography; quantum Fourier sampling with applications to factoring, quantum search, quantum key distribution.
courses.recommended_prep: CSCI 570 and knowledge of linear algebra at the level of EE 510 (preferred) or MATH 225

courses.title: Multimedia Systems Design
courses.description: End-to-end multimedia systems - content creation, compression, distribution using modern standards, DRM solutions, Digital-Cinema pipeline, multimedia classification, virtual-augmented reality, natural-language multimedia queries, multimodal media analysis, stereoscopic-holographic technologies.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: A: Software life-cycle processes; planning considerations for product definition, development, test, implemetation, maintenance. Team project. Graduate standing.

courses.title: Embodied Intelligence
courses.description: Advanced topics in embodied intelligence: multi-view reconstruction, visual reasoning, visual centric manipulation and locomotion, 3D deep learning for robotics.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with recent deep learning techniques at the level of CSCI 566 and basic robotic algorithms at the level of CSCI 545.

courses.title: 3-D Graphics and Rendering
courses.description: Course outlines the process of creating images from 3D models. Includes transformations, shading, lighting, rastorization, texturing, and other topics.

courses.title: Advanced Game Project Pre-Production
courses.description: Pre-production processes for team projects intended to address the multifaceted technical and creative challenges that are inherent to comprehensive game development.
courses.recommended_prep: CTIN 458 and CTIN 497

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Database system architecture; conceptual database models; semantic, object-oriented, logic-based, and relational databases; user and program interfaces; database system implementation; integrity, security, concurrency and recovery. Recommended Preparation: Knowledge of relational databases, SQL, relational algebra and physical database design is required. Open only to graduate students.

courses.title: Geospatial Data Analysis
courses.description: Techniques to efficiently store, manipulate, index, query and analyze geospatial information in support of real-world geographical and decision-making applications.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of database management at the level of CSCI 485 and machine learning at the level of CSCI 467

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Computer Science Research Colloquium
courses.description: Exploration and critical assessment of research activities in computer science. Course will serve as a forum for current research presentations from academia and industry. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

courses.title: Scientific Computing and Visualization
courses.description: Hands-on training on the basics of parallel computing and scientific visualization in the context of computer simulations in science and engineering. Recommended preparation: CSCI 455 and MATH 458 .

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Course content to be selected each semester from recent developments in computer science.

courses.title: Mathematics of High-Dimensional Data
courses.description: Modern developments in data representation/analysis, nonconvex optimization, high-dimensional probability, sketching, clustering, low-rank models, inverse problems, applications in imaging, machine learning, computer vision and neuroscience.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 503 and EE 510

courses.title: Optimization for the Information and Data Sciences
courses.description: Convex sets, functions, and optimization problems. Basic convex analysis and theory of convex programming. Novel, efficient first-order algorithms. Applications in the information and data sciences.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 503 and EE 510

courses.title: Seminar in Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Guest speakers, workshops, presentations, discussion, challenges and opportunities of interdisciplinary research in operations research and artificial intelligence.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Andrew and Erna Viterbi School of Engineering

courses.title: Elements of Human-Computer Interaction Research
courses.description: Design interviews, surveys, and experiments to identify and collect user data. Infer user needs using statistical and machine learning tools. Address validity and ethical concerns.
courses.recommended_prep: A knowledge of: research methods at the level of CSCI-517 or equivalent; statistical methods at the level of PM-511a, PM-511b or equivalent; and ethics in technology at the level of CSCI-631 or CSCI-663 or DSCI-531.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Data-Driven Decision-Making
courses.description: A unified treatment of data-driven decision-making for both single- and multi-agent systems from the perspectives of artificial intelligence and operations research.
courses.recommended_prep: Optimization (at the level of CSCI 675 or ISE 630); machine learning and its coding in Python (at the level of CSCI 467, CSCI 567, or ISE 529); basic probability (at the level of ISE 220) and linear algebra (at the level of MATH 225 or MATH 235).

courses.title: Machine Learning for/with Mixed-Integer Optimization
courses.description: Using mixed-integer optimization (MIO) to solve problems in artificial intelligence (Al) and machine learning (ML). Leveraging Al/ML to improve MIO solvers.
courses.recommended_prep: Optimization (at the level of CSCI 675, ISE 630, or ISE 631); machine learning (at the level of CSCI 567, ISE 568, CSCI 467, EE 460, ISE 529, or CSCI 559) using Python

courses.title: Analytics for Social Impact
courses.description: Use of analytics to address societal challenges arising in public health, social services and conservation; fairness, interpretability, robustness, optimization, machine learning and causal inference.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with modeling using integer optimization (e.g., at the level taught in ISE 631) and experience with ML using Python.

courses.title: Automata Theory, Logic and Formal Verification
courses.description: Omega-Regular Languages, Automata over infinite words and trees, Logic and Automata for timed languages, First-order Logic and MSO, Mu Calculus, Probabilistic Logics and Model Checking.
courses.recommended_prep: Big-O notation, algorithm analysis, propositional and first-order logic (CSCI 170), software development (CSCI 270), and complexity theory (CSCI 475). Software verification and program analysis/synthesis (CSCI 610 or CSCI 625) is preferred, but not required.

courses.title: Program Synthesis and Computer-Aided Verification
courses.description: Introduction to the principles and practices of software verification and program synthesis.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of discrete math and algorithm design. Background in systems and software engineering.

courses.title: Large Scale Optimization and Machine Learning
courses.description: Large-scale optimization algorithms that arise in machine learning: stochastic optimization, accelerated methods, parallelization, nonsmooth optimization, online optimization, variance reduction, min-max games.

courses.title: Robot Learning
courses.description: Robot learning in theory and practice; reinforcement and imitation learning, simulations-to-real-world transfers; computer vision; multi-agent systems, safety; applications and projects.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of robotics at the level of CSCI 445 or CSCI 545 and fundamental concepts in machine learning at the level of CSCI 467.

courses.title: Natural Language Dialogue Systems
courses.description: Computational models of natural language dialogue; conversational interfaces to artificial systems; dialogue system architectures and applications; Reinforcement learning of dialogue policies.

courses.title: Robot Manipulation
courses.description: Selected topics from core and active research areas in manipulation, including perception informed by 3D geometry and deep learning, planning algorithms, dynamics, and robot learning.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with robotics at the level of CSCI 445L or CSCI 545 and familiarity with machine learning at the level of CSCI 467. For those without such preparation, concurrent enrollment with these courses will be helpful.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Networking
courses.description: Computer communication protocols and systems, including classic and contemporary literature. The emphasis is on conceptual issues in the design and implementation of computer internetworks.

courses.title: Crafting a Research Agenda
courses.description: Formulation of a computer science research agenda, examination of trends within sub-areas of computer science and identification of fruitful and problematic research directions.
courses.recommended_prep: At least one year of graduate-level research experience.

courses.title: Networked Systems in Cloud Computing
courses.description: Systems and network design and protocols in cloud computing and data centers networks.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Design of Reliable Digital Systems
courses.description: Fault models; test generation; fault simulation; self-checking and self-testing circuits; design for testability; fault tolerant design techniques; case studies; search techniques; memory testing.

courses.title: Introduction to Online Optimization
courses.description: Foundation and advances of the theory of online learning/online convex optimization/sequential decision making.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with probability, convex analysis, calculus, and analysis of algorithms

courses.title: Advanced Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Computational models of natural language. Formalisms for describing structures of human language, and algorithms for learning language structures from data. Recommended preparation: Proficiency in programming, algorithms and data structures, discrete math, probability theory, and calculus. Open only to doctoral students. (Duplicates credit in former CSCI 562)

courses.title: Approximation Algorithms
courses.description: Algorithmic techniques include combinatorial algorithms and rounding of linear and semi-definite programs. Applications include network design, graph cuts, covering problems, and approximation hardness.

courses.title: Convex and Combinatorial Optimization
courses.description: Topics include: Convex sets and functions; convex optimization problems; geometric and Lagrangian duality; simplex algorithm; ellipsoid algorithm and its implications; matroid theory; submodular optimization.

courses.title: Theoretical Machine Learning
courses.description: The mathematical foundation of machine learning with a focus on algorithm design for sequential prediction problems.
courses.recommended_prep: MATH 208x, MATH 225, MATH 125g, CSCI 570 and CSCI 567

courses.title: Seminar in Computer Science Research
courses.description: Introduction of Ph.D. students to the broad range of computer science research. Two semesters registration required. Open to Computer Science doctoral students only. Graded CR/NC. Duplicates credit in former CSCI 597.

courses.title: Practicum in Teaching Computer Science
courses.description: Practical principles for the long-term development of effective teaching in Computer Science. Intended for teaching assistants for classes offered by the Computer Science department. Graded CR/NC. Open only to Computer Science doctoral students.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Course content to be selected each semester from recent developments in computer science.

programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Ways of thinking about the differences and relations among different cultural media: literature, film, video, manga/comics, aE*new media,aE* and so forth.

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Major developments in twentieth-century literary criticism, with special attention to theoretical work of the past three decades. (Duplicates credit in former COLT 502)

courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Studies in Culture
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Examination of culture as an instrument of discursive practice that shapes social formations in Asia, Europe, North and Latin America.

courses.title: Introduction to Translation Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Introduction to the graduate certificate in Translation Studies; study of canonical works in translation theory.

courses.title: Translating Race
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Contemporary notions of racial, cultural, and religious difference across languages and history.
courses.recommended_prep: COLT 510

courses.title: Translation in Theory and Practice
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Workshop in translation; capstone to graduate certificate in Translation Studies.

programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Literary and cultural currents from classical antiquity through modernity. Varying focus on specific genres, periods, movements or problematics.
