Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least on semester of enrollment in the graduate program.

courses.title: Professional Development I: Publication
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Preparation of book and article manuscripts for publication and placement in presses and journals; revising dissertations for publication; preparing papers for conferences. Students produce an article manuscript ready for submission to a journal. Duplicates credit in former COLT-603. Open only to doctoral students.

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Intensive study of a theoretical tradition or critical movement, or of an individual topic or thinker, in literary criticism or theory.

courses.title: Seminar in Literature, Culture and Thought
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Varying focus on social and political thought, psychoanalysis, and philosophy in relation to literary and cultural analysis.

courses.title: Seminar in Film and Visual Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
programs: Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Intensive study of various types of discourse (film, photography, literature) and their intersection with wider social, political, and theoretical issues.

courses.title: Professional Development II: Writing the Prospectus

courses.description: Methodology of writing a dissertation prospectus; a structured workshop environment for completing a prospectus.

courses.title: Introduction to the Art of Animation
courses.description: Theory and practice of animation across organic and digital media with an emphasis on self-exploration. Open to freshman in Animation and Digital Arts majors only.

courses.title: Introduction to the Art of Movement
courses.description: Theory and practice of animation with a focus on movement, gesture, timing and performance. Open to freshman in Animation and Digital Arts majors only.

courses.title: Design Fundamentals for Animation I
courses.description: Developing skills in design, composition, shape language, image-making, and visual thinking to create more sophisticated style frames and imagery for animation practice.

courses.title: The Rise of Digital Hollywood
courses.description: An overview of the evolution of computer graphics in modern media.

courses.title: Intermediate Animation Production
courses.description: Tools, skills and procedures used in animation production with a focus on professional execution of independent and collaborative productions. Prerequisite: CTAN 102. Open to sophomore animation majors only.

courses.title: Introduction to 3-D Character Animation
courses.description: 3-D animation performance utilizing preset rigs and virtual characters. Emphasis on timing, gesture, and performance.

courses.title: Design Fundamentals for Animation II
courses.description: Applying design principles in image-making and motion with software skills in After Effects to produce creative content and expand animation practice.

courses.title: Introduction to Storyboarding
courses.description: A practical introductory course that emphasizes the fundamentals of digital storyboarding to include storyboarding basics, proper composition, staging for clarity, pitching and critique.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic drawing skills

courses.title: Intermediate Character Animation for Games
courses.description: An applied introduction to the techniques used for animating 3-D bipedal human character content for the movement and interactive experience within 3-D video games.

courses.title: 3-D Character Performance Animation
courses.description: Advanced 3-D character animation with an emphasis on performance, lip-syncing, timing and execution. Prerequisite: CTAN 202L. Open only to juniors in Animation and Digital Arts.

courses.title: Professionalism of Animation
courses.description: Understanding the business of the animation industry. Developing presentation skills for interviewing and pitching, preparing personal marketing tools, researching employment opportunities, and practicing networking techniques.

courses.title: Cinematography for Animators
courses.description: The basic cinematic principles for animation, and how to shoot storyboards for the best composition to serve the story.

courses.title: Ideation and Pre-Production
courses.description: Emphasis on lateral thinking working across boundaries to find underlying principles in terms of ideation: the act of becoming an agent of ideas.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Understanding the requirements and relationships between theory and practice regarding the complexity of an animated film in idea and execution.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: b: Completion and exhibition of the short animated film to demonstrate understanding and further examination of the possibilities of animation time based graphic media. Open to senior animation majors only.

courses.title: Concept Design for Animation
courses.description: Creating characters and environments for animation, live action, and video games.

courses.title: Studio Careers: Story to Screen
courses.description: Seminar featuring guest speakers from major animation studios to provide an overview of a feature animation pipeline from development to pre-production, production and post-production.

courses.title: The World of Visual Effects
courses.description: Introduction to the expanding field of visual effects; topics include integration for cinematic storytelling and the study of digital productions employing the latest visual effects.

courses.title: Writing for Animation
courses.description: Workshop exploring concept and structure of long and short form animated films through practical writing exercises.

courses.title: Story Structure for Animation
courses.description: Storytelling principles as they pertain to episodic and serialized animated television series and animated feature films.

courses.title: History of Animation
courses.description: In depth survey of historical developments, styles, techniques, theory and criticism of animation as an art form.

courses.title: Introduction to 3-D Computer Animation
courses.description: Lecture and laboratory in computer animation: geometric modeling, motion specification, lighting, texture mapping, rendering, compositing, production techniques, systems for computer-synthesized animation using Maya software.

courses.title: Real-Time Animation
courses.description: The fundamentals of lighting and rendering in real-time. Creating complex, compelling and dynamic scenes and manipulating them in real-time using Unreal Engine.

courses.title: Organic Modeling for Animation
courses.description: The art of digital sculpting for animated characters, with visual effects integration. Recommended preparation: CTAN-452 or CTAN-462.

courses.title: Character Design Workshop
courses.description: The basics of character design for animation: anatomy, poses, facial expressions, silhouettes, and anthropomorphism. Development of a portfolio.

courses.title: Visual Effects
courses.description: Survey of contemporary concepts and approaches to production in the current state of film and video effects work. Digital and traditional methodologies will be covered, with a concentration on digital exercises illustrating modern techniques.

courses.title: Digital Lighting and Rendering
courses.description: Concepts, tools and techniques used to create cinematic lighting and rendering in computer-generated imagery (CGI).

courses.title: Digital Effects Animation
courses.description: All aspects of digital effects animation, including particles, dynamics, and fluids. Creating water, fire, explosions, and destruction in film.

courses.title: Animation for Projection Mapping and Live Performance
courses.description: An exploration of animation for projection mapping with hands-on learning and projects providing professional skills and workflows for helping students create their own content.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with any 3-D application

courses.title: Advanced Character Animation for Games
courses.description: Advanced techniques for animating 3-D creature characters in games. An emphasis on unique non-human fantasy characters.

courses.title: Character Modeling
courses.description: Create 3D character models from 2D designs and incorporate fundamental human anatomy into practice. Includes concepts for creating hair, fur, feathers and clothing for characters.

courses.title: Visual Music
courses.description: Creating visual music animation in a variety of forms and styles. Exploring the relationship between music, movement, and visual expression. Freshmen and sophomores not eligible.

courses.title: Directed Studies
courses.description: Individual research under faculty guidance.

courses.title: Procedural Animation
courses.description: Introduction to software packages and practices exploring current animation techniques that leverage simulation systems. Artificial intelligence as a tool for animation.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Detailed investigation of new or emerging aspects of cinema and/or television; special subjects offered by visiting faculty; experimental subjects.

courses.title: Animation: The Art and the Industry
courses.description: Seminar on the growth and development of animation studios and how they became part of the Hollywood studio system.

courses.title: Storyboarding for Animation
courses.description: Focus on film grammar, perspective, and layout, staging and acting as it relates to storyboarding for animation.

courses.title: Creative Production in Virtual Reality
courses.description: A creative studio course in producing both a linear cinematic virtual reality short film and associated real-time immersive experience.

courses.title: The Business of Animation
courses.description: Overview of the global production, media and entertainment industries and fundamental business skills, with an emphasis on animation and the animation professional.

courses.title: Compositing and the Art of Creating Visual Styles
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of compositing techniques to effectively create film looks in 3D/2D animations and visual effects.

courses.title: Environment Modeling
courses.description: Create 3D models for environments for urban and natural settings and props including vehicles, rocks, trees and furniture.

courses.title: Inside Story: Creative Development for Animation
courses.description: A creative development workshop for animated pitch storytelling, supported by an introduction to character development and story structure fundamentals.

courses.title: Design Fundamentals for Animation
courses.description: A creative design course for animators, combining visual design aesthetics with practical technique and software skill learning.

courses.title: Fundamentals of 2-D Animation
courses.description: Exploring techniques of classical hand-drawn character animation, with emphasis on performance, personality, and observation, specializing in classical Hollywood animation.

courses.title: Foundations of 3-D Computer Animation
courses.description: Foundations of computer animation: generating and editing movement, lighting, textures, rendering, creating and outputting full animated projects using Maya software.

courses.title: Fundamentals of 3-D Character Animation
courses.description: Applying traditional principles to 3-D character animation in Maya, with a focus on character performance and acting.

courses.title: Production Design for Animation
courses.description: Design with an emphasis on storytelling through character design, environment design, moment paintings, color script and look of picture. Development of a project style guide.

courses.title: Fictional World Building in Animation
courses.description: Constructing a persuasive fictional animated world via narrative techniques, a fixed premise and a degree of believability supported by five fundamental visual design elements.

courses.title: Animation Production I
courses.description: Production of an animation project from creative concept and design through completion.

courses.title: Stop Motion Puppet and Set Design
courses.description: Puppet and set design for stop motion animation while providing guidance on armature rigs that allow the character to be animated effectively.

courses.title: Animation Design and Production
courses.description: Exploring creative strategies to designing form and content. Developing style and investigating multiple techniques, including live action and sound. Production of a 30-60 second work.

courses.title: Motion Capture Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamental principles of motion capture technology explored while working through a structured series of assignments based around performance, gesture and motion.

courses.title: 2-D Motion Graphics

courses.title: Television Script Analysis

Writing for Screen and Television students only.

Open to M.F.A. Writing for Screen and Television students only.

courses.title: Ballet

courses.title: Ballet
courses.description: Continued study of Classical Ballet technique with intermediate-level barre and center work, focusing on developing greater clarity, coordination, musicality, and knowledge of ballet history and terminology.

courses.title: Ballet
courses.description: Intermediate/advanced study of Classical Ballet technique with emphasis on clarity, precision, musicality, movement quality, and artistic expression. Introduction of beats, tours, advanced adagio and allegro combinations, and optional pointe work.

courses.title: Ballet
courses.description: Advanced/pre-professional study of Classical Ballet, continuing and deepening emphasis on clarity, precision, musicality, movement quality, and artistic expression. Further development of beats, tours, advanced adagio and allegro combinations, and optional pointe work.

courses.title: Jazz Dance

courses.title: Jazz Dance
courses.description: Continued study of Jazz Dance technique at the intermediate level, focusing on African and Latin based diaspora dances with European influences, improvisation, center work, performance techniques, and strength/stretching series.

courses.title: Jazz Dance
courses.description: Advanced study of Jazz Dance technique, focusing on Broadway, commercial, and concert Jazz Dance, with a continued emphasis on improvisation, center work, and performance techniques.

courses.title: Hip Hop Dance

Inspired by the eclectic and energetic music from the Hindi-language film industry of India, Bollywood is a highly expressive dance style that combines Indian folk and classical dances with Hip Hop, Jazz, Latin and popular forms.

courses.title: International Style Ballroom Dance

courses.title: Tap Dance

courses.title: Tap Dance

courses.title: Applied Machine Learning and Data Mining
courses.description: Foundational course focusing on the understanding, application and evaluation of machine learning and data mining approaches in data-intensive scenarios.

courses.title: Security and Privacy
courses.description: Basic concepts in information security and privacy; implications of security and privacy breaches; security and privacy policies, threats and protection mechanisms; security and privacy laws, regulations and ethics.

courses.title: Data Visualization and User Interface Design
courses.description: Design and application of visualization systems for data-driven decision making; exploring, analyzing and communicating insights through data.

courses.description: Programming in Python for retrieving, searching and analyzing data from the Web. Learning to manipulate large data sets.

courses.title: Research Methods and Analysis for User Studies
courses.description: Introduction to research methods and data analysis techniques for human subject research; experimental research design, correlational research, data analysis, ensuring validity and ethics.

courses.description: Threats to information systems; technical and procedural approaches to threat mitigation; policy specification and foundations of policy for secure systems; mechanisms for building secure security services; risk management. Background in computer security preferred. Recommended previous courses of study include computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, management information systems and/or mathematics.

courses.description: Assurance that an information system will behave as expected; assurance approaches for fielding secure information systems; case studies. Recommended preparation: Prior degree in computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, management information systems and/or mathematics. Some background in computer security preferred.

courses.description: Analysis of computer security and why systems are not secure. Concepts and techniques applicable to the design of hardware and software for Trusted Systems.
courses.recommended_prep: Background in computer security, computer architecture, operating systems, software development is preferred. Recommended previous course of study is DSCI 519

courses.title: Computer Forensics
courses.description: Preservation, identification, extraction and documentation of computer evidence stored on a computer. Data recovery; File System Analysis; Investigative Techniques and Methodologies; Forensic Reports and Presentations.

courses.title: Security and Privacy
courses.description: Covers societal implications of information privacy and how to design systems to best preserve privacy. Recommended Preparation: general familiarity with the use of common Internet and mobile applications.
courses.recommended_prep: General familiarity with the use of common Internet and mobile applications

courses.title: Fairness in Artificial Intelligence

courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of Python, linear algebra, probability, and statistics. Familiarity with artificial intelligence and machine learning.

courses.title: Machine Learning for a Secure Internet

courses.recommended_prep: Mathematics and logic undergraduate courses

courses.description: Foundations of East Asian ethical and philosophical thought and how they apply to modern ethical issues, such as the death penalty, abortion or climate change.

courses.description: Contemporary economic problems of sub-Saharan economies: policies and endowments. Focus on issues of poverty, agriculture, health, macroeconomy and political economy.

courses.title: Clinical Practice Seminar in Language Teaching
courses.description: Second of two-course series focused on helping students translate theory to practice. Part B also facilitates preparation for and submission of the EdTPA.

courses.title: Race and Racism in Education
courses.description: Race, racism, racial equity, Critical Race Theory (CRT) will be explored particularly within educational institutions, with a heavy focus placed on practice.

courses.title: Foundations and Design of Educational Research
courses.description: Build knowledge, skills and perspective to design and carry out scholarship as an educational researcher.

courses.title: Racism and Anti-Blackness in Education
courses.description: A holistic understanding of the historical underpinnings, persistent pathways and contemporary pillars of racism and white supremacy in education.

courses.title: Mixed Methods Research
courses.description: Explore theoretical and practical issues surrounding quantitative and qualitative methods in educational research.

courses.title: Introduction to Curriculum and Pedagogy in Urban Schools
courses.description: General introduction to curriculum and instruction (pedagogy) affecting teaching and learning across disciplines, grade levels, and different social contexts of schooling.

courses.title: Contexts for Educational Equity, Access, and Agency
courses.description: Examines how environmental, pedagogical, and curricular choices can be cultivated with greater knowledge of culture, gender, orientation, race, learning differences and language.

courses.title: Integrated Language Development Across the Curriculum
courses.description: Understanding of language development and the connection between language and learning in school, across all curricular areas.

courses.title: Applications of Curriculum and Pedagogy, Part A
courses.description: Candidates apply content-area knowledge utilizing a repertoire of pedagogical practices responsive to the needs and interests of diverse learners.

courses.title: Identifying and Teaching to Student Differences
courses.description: Building on EDUC 671, course proceeds with greater focus on learner behavior, ability, and language to access strategies to differentiate, scaffold, and assess learning.

courses.title: Literacy Development and Instruction in Elementary Education
courses.description: Literacy development and instruction, with a focus on the importance of literacy for academic success and civic participation.

courses.title: Literacy Development and Instruction in Secondary Education
courses.description: Prepares prospective secondary teachers to integrate literacy instruction within their content area by creating authentic opportunities for learners to develop literacy skills.

courses.title: Applications of Curriculum and Pedagogy, Part B
courses.description: Building on EDUC 673, prepares candidates to apply curricular principles to lesson development and determine how content should be delivered to maximize learning.

courses.title: Applying Knowledge and Strategies for Teaching All Students
courses.description: Building on EDUC 673, prepares candidates to apply curricular principals to lesson development and determine how content should be delivered to maximize learning.

courses.title: Blended Learning Experiences for Students in Urban Schools
courses.description: Design, implement and evaluate technology-rich learning environments to customize and individualize learning opportunities and assessments for K-12 students.

courses.title: Research, Policy and Practice in Urban Education
courses.description: Development of urban education through the social, historical and political lens as it shapes and influences education research and policy.

courses.title: Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods in Education
courses.description: Basic concepts of quantitative/statistical methods common in education research, emphasizing applications with data. Introduces sampling, types of validity, statistical inference, bivariate analysis, internal/external validity.

courses.title: Proseminar in Education
courses.description: Introduction to faculty and their research; provides professional development on a variety of topics.

courses.title: Capstone Seminar
courses.description: Synthesize institutional, public and non-public sources of data to write and orally present an enrollment management plan for both campus and external stakeholders.

courses.title: Administration in Higher Education
courses.description: Administrative issues in higher education. Academic leadership related to undergraduate and graduate education. Quality standards and assessment. How administrators create efficiency, effectiveness, performance, and change.

courses.title: Financing and Assessing Colleges for Equity
courses.description: Examination of federal, state, local and individual roles in financing of higher education towards enhancing equity and reducing opportunity gaps.

courses.title: Advanced Study of Motivation: Theory, Research and Applicati
courses.description: Analysis of motivational principles; diagnosis and solutions to motivation gaps in learning environments; and motivation and efficacy theories and principles.

courses.title: Measurement and Evaluation for Decision-Making
courses.description: Collecting, analyzing, and using quantitative data to solve problems of practice and in evaluating educational institutions, programs, and policies.

courses.title: Resourcing Schools for Equity and Excellence
courses.description: Applying economic theory to the study of education. Application of market theory to education, partnerships, allocation of resources and the examination of educational enterprises.

courses.title: Education Policy and Politics
courses.description: Major issues facing educators in the 21st century. Emphasis on how educational policy can focus on incentives for schools to improve student learning.

courses.title: Evaluating and Assessing Educational System Outcomes
courses.description: Evaluating impact. Examination of key assessment theories; planning and implementation of learning and program effectiveness.

courses.title: Analyzing Organizational Change and Its Effectiveness
courses.description: Designed to help leaders apply research about learning and motivation to the strengthening of organizational performance in organizations around the world.

courses.title: Making Choices: Deciding Among Policy Alternatives
courses.description: Models of decision making including cost-benefit analysis, risk-benefit analysis, and decision analysis. Ethical considerations and the political environment. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Implementing Policy in Educational Systems
courses.description: Effective policy-making. Human and financial resources to support implementation. Targeting resources to support implementation to attain policy goals. Prerequisite: EDUC 726. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Global Trends: Emerging Ideas, Emerging Markets
courses.description: Examination of a range of emerging markets in education. Global efforts of institutions of higher education to access new markets through collaborations and offshore endeavors.

courses.title: Assessing Policy Impact in Educational Settings
courses.description: Theory and practice of educational policy evaluation. Limits of rationality and the political forces that shape policy. Preparation of an evaluation design. Prerequisite: EDUC 727. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Organizational Change and Communication Practices
courses.description: Examine importance of communication in facilitating organizational change, motivation and buy-in during times of transition. Learn how effective communication is dependent on trust and empathy.

courses.title: Economics of Organizational Change and Learning Environments
courses.description: Leadership, problem solving, communication, research, reflection, and professional dispositions will concurrently expand. Candidates will acquire the knowledge and skills to identify and implement economic change.

courses.title: Building Capacity for Organizational Change
courses.description: Focuses on learning issues related to building organizational capacity for change through leadership and development of personnel within an organization.

courses.title: Analyzing Data and Identifying Solutions
courses.description: Designed to help students interpret study data and construct evidence-based solutions for real-time organizational problems of practice.

courses.description: Explore the historical and contemporary foundations of hierarchies and relationships of power, sociocultural diversity of experiences and sociopolitical resistance within higher education.

courses.description: Examination of roles and functions of higher education from historical and contemporary perspectives, with a focus on equity and urban education.

courses.title: Research Methods and Applied Educational Ethnography
courses.description: Explore the use of quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods research to explore problems/opportunities of practice in higher education.

courses.title: Human-Centered Leadership in Sports, Part A
courses.description: Critically examine the historical origins of inequities in sports to gain insights into present-day challenges and prepare students to address current issues through human-centered approaches to leadership across various sports settings.

courses.title: Understanding Human Development and Well-Being in Sports
courses.description: Examination of human development and wellbeing in sports through a critical lens to foster equity, inclusion, social justice and holistic development in sports contexts.

courses.title: Using Data for Decision Making in Sports
courses.description: Develop skills to cultivate an inclusive, data-driven culture in sports, analyzing diverse data types to foster equity and social justice in sports context.

courses.description: Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the student's field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least one semester of enrollment in the graduate program with a cumulative 3.0 GPA.

courses.title: History and Philosophy of Coaching in Sports
courses.description: Critically examine the historical origins and philosophical approaches of sports coaching, including challenges within the context of sports and the broader society.

courses.title: Coach and Athlete Identity Development
courses.description: Apply principles of intersectional identity development for coach and athlete well-being, team dynamics and social justice.

courses.title: Leadership as a Critical Practice
courses.description: Focuses on leadership identity and critical self-reflection to develop effective, equity-minded and human-centered leadership practices.

courses.title: Foundations of Research
courses.description: Quantitative and qualitative research methods; critical analysis of existing studies; effective academic writing and synthesis skills.

courses.title: Leadership: Theories and Application
courses.description: Critical analysis and application of leadership theories to develop context-specific strategies that prioritize equity and inclusivity.

courses.title: Context of Organizational Change
courses.description: External factors impacting organizations; human-centered organizational design; evidence-based decision-making for thriving in dynamic environments.

courses.title: Cultural Humility in Leadership and Practice
courses.description: Facilitate culturally responsive interventions in mental health leadership. Address racial disparities; design, apply and assess diversity, equity and inclusion programming.

courses.title: Organization Leadership: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Apply organizational frameworks for mental health leadership. Introduce theory to enhance service delivery, prioritize client care and promote societal impact.

courses.title: Designing Organizational Change
courses.description: Critical analysis of organizational culture, structures, and processes; application of organizational change and change management theories; equity-minded organizational transformation.

courses.title: Quantitative Method and Data Analysis for Education
courses.description: Develop skills to critically assess and apply quantitative research. Explore equitable approaches through systematic collection and analysis of data, utilizing standardized tools and statistical analysis.

courses.title: Advanced Theories in Mental Health Practice
courses.description: Apply advanced clinical, counseling and psychotherapy concepts into leadership practice. Emphasis on cultural humility, evidenced-based practice, marginalized communities and self-exploration.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods and Descriptive Statistics
courses.description: Quantitative research methods for practitioner-scholars; foundational principles of designing and conducting surveys; descriptive statistics and data interpretation.

courses.title: Consultation, Program Development and Evaluation
courses.description: Acquire skills to design, implement and assess evaluation studies and consult with other mental health organizations. Focus on cultural humility via program design and evaluation.

courses.title: Current and Emerging Opportunities in Leadership
courses.description: Identification and analysis of current and emerging leadership opportunities and global and systemic challenges in the context of advancing human-centered organizations.

courses.title: Qualitative Methods and Analysis
courses.description: Qualitative research methods for practitioner scholars; systematic qualitative data collection, analysis and interpretation.

courses.description: Explores urban P-20 education through social, historical, and political lenses and how research and policy shape professional practice in Los Angeles and the United States.

courses.title: Foundations in Leadership in Education
courses.description: Provides foundational knowledge about leadership theory and practice to support students' development as critically conscious leaders who take action to address inequities in urban contexts.

courses.title: Foundations in Learning
courses.description: Supports the development of critically conscious leaders who facilitate learning in urban contexts by understanding how culture, identity and power influence learners' opportunities to learn.

courses.title: Power, Diversity and Equity
courses.description: Explores power, diversity and equity through the social, historical, and political lenses as these constructs shape and impact education (P-20) research, policy and professional practice.

courses.title: Leadership Enactment
courses.description: Provides students with the opportunity to acquire or deepen knowledge and skills related to acting as a critically conscious leaders who address existing educational inequities.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Topics
courses.description: Explore specialized clinical topics in mental health, emphasizing practical application and employee skill development in crisis intervention, trauma treatment, grant writing, budgeting and professional communication.

courses.title: Learning and Instruction in Professional Contexts
courses.description: Develop skills to teach in diverse professional settings. Emphasize adult education philosophy, instructional design, technology integration, assessment and personal teaching philosophy development.

courses.title: Facilitating Learning, Motivation and Wellbeing
courses.description: Evidence-based strategies to promote employee engagement and well-being in organizational contexts; inclusive policies and practices that facilitate employee motivation, learning and development.

courses.title: Designing Educational Organizations for Equity
courses.description: Introduction to organizational theory and design with emphasis on building and leading organizations based on the principles of equity and social justice.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Assessment
courses.description: Enhance skills related to analysis and application of assessment, psychometric trends, ethical diagnosis, treatment and culturally competent leadership. Interpret and critique psychological testing.

courses.title: Leading for Instructional Excellence and Equity
courses.description: Improves K-12 practitioners' instructional leadership capacity, addressing power and its impact on creating and perpetuating educational inequities for historically marginalized and minoritized children and adults.

courses.title: Topics in Mental Health Leadership
courses.description: Develop critical administrative skills for mental health professionals, including grant writing, budgeting, strategic planning, communication strategies and therapist burnout prevention

courses.title: Proseminar in Career Development in Mental Health Leadership
courses.description: Acquire leadership skills for diverse mental health settings, emphasizing values-driven leadership, critical self-reflection and mindful communication for individual self-care and organizational well-being.

courses.title: Curriculum and Instructional Leadership
courses.description: Social, political, economic and scholarly factors determining curriculum and instructional design and implementation and implications for formal and informal leaders in P-20 contexts are explored.

courses.title: Inter-Disciplinary Curriculum, Instruction and Assessment P-20
courses.description: Educational leaders utilize spatial data and technologies to study their leadership trajectories across urban P-20 settings and bring inter-disciplinary approaches to curriculum, instruction, and assessment.

courses.title: Research Methods 1
courses.description: Explores the historically complex relationship between education research, education (in)equity and personal practice, and will highlight the possibilities of research to foster justice in education through the examination of the utility of basic and applied quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods research.

courses.title: Research Methods 2
courses.description: Building on Research Methods 1, students learn to implement a research design by conducting pilot studies to answer quantitative and qualitative research questions.

courses.title: Leadership of Site and System Organizational Learning
courses.description: Applying leadership theory and adult learning theory to real-world challenges facing school and district leaders.

courses.description: Supports students to prepare a literature review, overview of methodology and other contextual writing for their dissertations in practice and prepare for the qualifying exam.

courses.description: Builds as students finalize their literature reviews, overview of methodology and other contextual writing for the dissertation in practice and qualifying exam.

courses.description: Builds students' knowledge and skills for analyzing quantitative and qualitative data and reporting results and findings for their Dissertations in Practice.

courses.title: Introduction to Electrical Engineering
courses.description: Electrical engineering overview: communications, computers, circuits, components, signals, electromagnetics, microelectronics; data encoding and compression, USPS and UPC product codes, DVDs, semiconductor devices, and integrated circuits.

courses.title: Introduction to Embedded Systems
courses.description: Information representations, embedded programming, digital and serial I/O, analog-to-digital conversion, and interrupt mechanisms. Elementary analog, logic and state-machine design.

courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra for Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to linear algebra with engineering applications. Weekly laboratory exercises using MATLAB.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming for Electrical Engineers
courses.description: Introduction to solving engineering problems using computational methods. Survey of various programming languages and their strengths and weaknesses. Program structure, input/output, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays.

courses.title: Linear Circuits
courses.description: Lumped circuit elements; network equations; zero-input and zerostate responses; sinusoidal steady-state analysis; impedance; resonance; network functions; power concepts; transformers; Laplace transforms.

courses.title: Distributed Systems for the Internet of Things
courses.description: Introduction to hardware, operating systems, signal processing and control, network protocols, mobile applications, databases, cloud computing, machine learning and security for the Internet of Things.
courses.recommended_prep: Experience with DIY electronics, Linux and programming in a distributed, networked environment

courses.title: Linear Systems
courses.description: Representation and analysis of linear time-invariant systems primarily for the continuous time case. Convolution, Fourier series and transform, Laplace transform, controls and communications applications.

courses.title: Physical Electronics
courses.description: Semiconductor device characteristics and applications. Physical models of electronic conduction in solids, p-n junctions, bipolar and field effect transistors and other solid-state devices.

courses.title: Electronic Circuits
courses.description: Basic analog and digital circuit design using Bipolar Junction Transistors, Field Effect Transistors and integrated circuits.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Circuits
courses.description: Digital system design and implementation; synchronous design of datapath and control; schematic/Verilog-based design, simulation, and implementation in Field Programmable Gate Arrays; timing analysis; semester-end project.

courses.title: Software Design for Electrical Engineers
courses.description: Object-oriented programming techniques, basic data structures and elementary complexity analysis for the modeling, simulation and solution of engineering problems.

courses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
courses.description: Introduction to concepts of randomness and uncertainty: probability, random variables, statistics. Applications to digital communications, signal processing, automatic control, computer engineering and computer science.

courses.title: Electromagnetics for Engineering Systems
courses.description: Electromagnetic plane-wave propagation and interactions with simple media, transmission/reception of wireless signals in complex environments. Optimization design methods for system applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
courses.description: Introduction to micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS); scaling effects; materials and structures in MEMS; MEMS sensing and actuation principles; microfabrication.
courses.recommended_prep: Mechanics of materials on the level of AME 204 or CE 225, Dynamics on the level of AME 301

courses.title: Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Crystal structures, x-ray diffraction, thermal properties of solids, diamagnetism and paramagnetism, free-electron model of metals, semiconductors, ferromagnetism, super-conductivity, imperfections in crystals.

courses.title: Introduction to Power Systems
courses.description: Components of power systems; analysis techniques in electrical power generation transmission and utilization; and environmental and economic considerations in system operations and planning.

courses.title: Power Systems Technology
courses.description: Comprehensive assessment of the technical, environmental, and regulatory challenges that affect the future delivery and utilization of electric power. Case-study analysis.

courses.title: Foundations of Robotics
courses.description: Designing and programming mobile robots; sensors, effectors, basic control theory, control architectures, planning, some advanced topics, illustrations of state-of-the-art. Weekly robot programming labs; final project.

courses.title: Communication Electronics
courses.description: Analysis, design, and experimental evaluation of transistor-level communication circuits and micro-systems. Transmission lines, impedance matching, noise, distortion, tuned amplifiers, mixers, oscillators, phase-locked loops.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming Systems Design
courses.description: Intensive introduction to programming principles, discrete mathematics for computing, software design and software engineering concepts. Not available for credit to computer sciencemajors, graduate or undergraduate.

courses.title: Embedded Systems Design Laboratory
courses.description: Specification, design, implementation, testing and documentation of a digital system project using embedded processors, programmable logic, analog I/O interfaces and application specific hardware. Capstone design experience.
courses.recommended_prep: Proficient in programming in the "C" language; knowledge of programming on the level of EE 155 or CSCI 103

courses.title: Machine Learning for Engineers
courses.description: Overview of machine learning, regression and classification, clustering and dimensionality reduction, loss-functions, over/under-fitting, cross-validation, kernel machines, decision trees and neural networks.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear systems on the level of EE 301, probability and/or statistics on the level of EE 364 or MATH 407 or CE 119 or ISE 220 or ISE 225

courses.title: Introduction to Communication Systems
courses.description: Broad treatment of analog and digital communication systems. Modulation and demodulation techniques using a carrier wave's amplitude, frequency, phase. Channel signal and noise. Review current systems.

courses.title: MOS VLSI Circuit Design
courses.description: Analysis and design of digital MOS VLSI circuits including area, delay and power minimization. Laboratory assignments including design, layout, extraction, simulation and automatic synthesis.

courses.title: Control Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Practical measurement, analysis, and control of dynamic systems; system identification; linear control system design; simulation and verification of control system performance; and experimental controller implementation.
courses.recommended_prep: AME 302ab, AME 420, and MATH 245

courses.title: Control Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Vibration measurement and analysis; simulation, design, and experimental verification of mechanical control systems; system identification; implementation of controllers; performance evaluation via experimentation and stimulation.

courses.title: Linear Control Systems
courses.description: Analysis of linear time-invariant (LTI) control systems; stability of LTI systems; frequency response, proportional-integral-differential (PID) and root-locus compensation techniques.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: Fundamentals of digital signal processing covering: discrete time linear systems, quantization, sampling, Z-transforms, Fourier transforms, FFTs and filter design.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with MATLAB

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Undergraduate Thesis
courses.description: For the undergraduate degree. Credit on acceptance of thesis. IP (EE 494a) or letter grade (EE 494b).

courses.title: Undergraduate Thesis
courses.description: For the undergraduate degree. Credit on acceptance of thesis. IP (EE 494a) or letter grade (EE 494b).

courses.title: Capstone Design
courses.description: Capstone design project for the undergraduate degree. Project topics vary from semester to semester.

courses.title: Solid State
courses.description: Atomic electronic states, molecular bonding, crystal structures, diffraction, reciprocal lattice, Brillouin zones, crystal binding, lattice vibrations, specific heat, anharmonic effects, energy bands, metals, conductivity.
courses.recommended_prep: Quantum Mechanics (EE 471 or EE 539 or PHYS 438a or equivalent). Vector analysis, linear algebra, complex variables, transforms, ordinary and partial second order differential equations (MATH 445).

courses.title: Probability for Electrical and Computer Engineers
courses.description: Rigorous coverage of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, functions of multiple random variables, covariance, correlation, random sequences, Markov chains, estimation, and introduction to statistics. Duplicates credit in former EE 464 and EE 465.

courses.title: Hardware Foundations of Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduction to ML accelerators; memory access kernels; parallelization approaches to the design of scalable ML systems; distributed ML; privacy in machine learning.
courses.recommended_prep: Matrix algebraic algorithms on the level of EE141L; Gradient descent, PyTorch, Tensorflow or similar parallel programming experience on the level of EE451; Memory systems of CPUs and GPUs on the level of EE457

courses.title: Linear Algebra for Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to linear algebra and matrix theory and their underlying concepts; applications to engineering problems; mathematically rigorous and foundational to other classes in communication, control, and signal processing.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 141 and MATH 445 or equivalent (calculus, undergraduate linear algebra, matrix theory)

courses.title: Machine Learning Hardware Accelerators
courses.description: Machine-learning accelerator architecture design; network architecture optimization, quantization, pruning; hardware/software codesign and cross layer optimizations for machine-learning models
courses.recommended_prep: Experience with HDL and RTL, Python programming at an intermediate level, and use of PyTorch or Tensorflow frameworks in simple ML projects.

courses.title: Stochastic Processes for Financial Engineering
courses.description: Theory and applications of stochastic processes relevant to financial engineering. Stochastic processes, Brownian motion, martingales, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo Simulations with financial application examples.

courses.title: Quantum Error Correction
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to quantum error correction and decoherence control, from the basics to the cutting edge, enabling students to delve into current research topics.
courses.recommended_prep: PHYS 550

courses.title: Quantum Sensing: Machine Learning, Inference and Information
courses.description: Basics of quantum mechanics, quantum sensing, quantum theory of inference, information and machine learning.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic quantum mechanics on the level of EE 539. Linear algebra on the level of EE 141. Probability on the level of EE 364.

courses.title: High-Voltage DC Transmission Systems
courses.description: AC/DC conversion processes, converter technologies, and design; harmonics, controls, and protection; AC/DC interactions and system performance; modeling, application, and installation; current-source versus voltage-source converters.

courses.title: Mathematics and Tools for Financial Engineering
courses.description: Students will build a mathematical background for studying Financial Engineering. Emphasis is on analysis, proofs and examples. Mathworks Financial toolbox will be introduced.

courses.title: Speech Recognition and Processing for Multimedia
courses.description: Speech production, acoustics, perception, synthesis, compression, recognition, transmission. Coding for speech, music, and CD-quality. Feature extraction. Echo cancellation. Audio, visual synchronization. Multimedia, Internet use.

courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Information Processing
courses.description: Basics of quantum computation and information: quantum bits and registers, unitary gates, algorithms, error correction and cryptography. Experimental realizations and near-term quantum technology.
courses.recommended_prep: An advanced course in complex linear algebra, such as EE 510

courses.title: Power Systems Analysis and Design
courses.description: Power system planning, studies, and design; time-domain modeling and analysis of power-system networks; power flow, stability, fault, and economic dispatch analysis; symmetrical components.

courses.title: Spatial Audio for Real and Virtual Spaces
courses.description: Fundamentals of audio signal processing, acoustics and human perception to understand sound in the real world and create compelling virtual auditory worlds.
courses.recommended_prep: MATLAB experience is useful but not required

courses.title: Advanced Biomedical Imaging
courses.description: Advanced scientific and engineering principles of biomedical imaging including magnetic resonance, X-ray computed tomography, ultrasound and single photon and positron emission tomography.
courses.recommended_prep: BME 513 or EE 483 or previous/concurrent exposure to linear systems and signals, Fourier Transform, and signal processing in the frequency domain

courses.title: Complex Digital ASIC System Design
courses.description: Complex digital/mixed-signal ASICs from algorithm to chip tapeout including synthesis, hardware accelerators, RTL design, physical design, specialization, verification, post-fabrication experiments. Project-based.
courses.recommended_prep: Digital circuits on the level of EE 354L; computer systems organization on the level of EE 457; VLSI circuit design on the level of EE 477; VLSI system design on the level of EE 577a/b.

courses.title: Power System Protection
courses.description: Theory of system and equipment protection, characteristics of relays, relay coordination, and system considerations.

courses.title: Renewable Energy in Power Systems
courses.description: Renewable energy sources and their integration in electrical networks. Power-flow control from highly variable resources. Cost analysis and planning.

courses.title: Power Electronics
courses.description: Fundamentals of switched-mode power converters operating under steadystate and transient conditions. Feedback control systems. Magnetic circuit design.

courses.title: Optics
courses.description: Geometrical optics, electromagnetic wave propagation, reflection and refraction at interfaces, imaging with lenses and mirrors, optics of the eye, optical instruments (microscopes/telescopes/cameras), and polarization.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 370L

courses.title: Optical Materials, Instruments and Devices
courses.description: Optical materials and devices; design and theory of selected optical instruments and components; properties of modulators; optical sources and detectors; emerging technologies relevant to system design.

courses.title: Nonlinear Optics
courses.description: Theory of nonlinear optical susceptibility and application to self-focusing, harmonic generation, and parametric interactions. Raman and Brillouin scattering. Coherent spectroscopy.
courses.recommended_prep: Maxwell's equations and Fourier transforms on the level of EE 572

courses.title: Network Processor Design and Programming
courses.description: Design, implementation, and programming of a custom multi-core RISC-V-based network processor and hardware accelerators using reconfigurable hardware in a SmartNIC in a realistic network testbed.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 450

courses.title: Materials Characterization
courses.description: Characterization of solid structure by X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, atomic force and tunneling microscopy and elemental analysis by photoemission, X-ray fluorescence, Auger, energy loss spectroscopies.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate physics, chemistry, mathematics; graduate level preparation in quantum mechanics or solid-state physics

courses.title: Wireless Communications
courses.description: The mobile communication channel; techniques used to combat the channel; cellular communications; multiple-access techniques; example mobile communication systems.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic electromagnetic theory, digital communications systems; EE 510

courses.title: Analog Integrated Circuits
courses.description: MOSFET operation and models; elementary amplifier configurations; biasing and references; frequency response; noise; feedback; operational amplifiers; frequency compensation; non-linearity and mismatch; passive and active filters.

courses.title: Modern Solid-State Devices
courses.description: Integrated-circuit technologies for mixed-signal communication and data systems. Constituent device models and their limitations. Contemporary research topics.

courses.title: Computing Principles for Electrical Engineers
courses.description: Survey of computing principles and practice of software design: object-oriented and non object-oriented, testing, template libraries, time-space complexity, data structures, algorithms, and dynamic programming.
courses.recommended_prep: Exposure to computer programming

courses.title: A Computational Introduction to Deep Learning
courses.description: Deep learning frameworks for training multilayer perceptrons, convolutional and recurrent neural networks; Python, virtual environments, linux and shell scripting, cloud computing, including GPUs and datasets.
courses.recommended_prep: Graduate standing and a typical undergraduate ECE background including the equivalent of EE 105 and EE 155 and some exposure to a high-level scripting language such as Python or Matlab.

courses.title: Internet and Cloud Computing
courses.description: The theory, architecture, hardware/software, and programming of the Internet and its protocols, cloud computing, networks for cloud computing, how they interact with Internet of Things.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 457 and knowledge of C/C++ programming

courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: Fundamental skills for modeling and controlling of dynamic systems for robotic applications and graphics animations; control theory; kinematics; dynamics; sensor processing; real-time operating systems; robot labs. Recommended preparation: Basic knowledge in linear algebra (matrices and vectors), calculus, programming in C/C++ or any another language or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Applied and Cloud Computing for Electrical Engineers
courses.description: Introduction to cloud applications; software development and deployment within cloud platforms; interactive user-facing interfaces; API development; databases, virtualization, asynchronous execution, testing and scalability.

courses.title: Nanotechnology for Materials, Electronics, and Circuits
courses.description: Nanotechnology for advanced nanomaterials, nanoelectronics devices, and circuits, including the rigorous treatment of electronic band structures of carbon nanotubes, graphene, and two-dimensional materials.

courses.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Foundations of symbolic intelligent systems, search, logic, knowledge representation, planning, learning.

courses.title: Random Processes in Engineering
courses.description: Probability Axioms. Random vectors and processes, their convergence and limit theorems. Stationary processes, Markov chains, Martingales, Gaussian processes. Basic calculus of random processes. Wiener filtering.

courses.title: Inference and Estimation: Theory and Algorithms
courses.description: Bayesian and non-Bayesian hypothesis testing and estimation, sufficient statistics, exponential families, expectation-maximization, approximations, Kalman filtering and smoothing, recursive Bayesian tracking.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 510

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
courses.description: Image sampling, 2-D image transform, image enhancement, geometric image modification, morphologic processing, edge detection, texture analysis, image filtering and restoration.

courses.title: Advanced Electromagnetic Theory
courses.description: Classical electromagnetic field theory and its usage in understanding and analytically modelling advanced applied electrical engineering devices.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 572L

courses.title: Wave Interactions with Random and Inhomogeneous Media
courses.description: Analyses and applications of electromagnetic wave scattering and propagation in inhomogenous media, including random media and periodic structures.

courses.title: Integrated Memory Devices and Technologies
courses.description: Fundamental device physics, integration technology and cutting-edge innovations in integrated microelectronic memory devices and systems, and their applications in data storage and emerging beyond-von-Neumann computing.
courses.recommended_prep: Understanding of basic semiconductor device physics and fabrication technology is useful, but not required

courses.title: VLSI System Design
courses.description: MOS logic; system design; memory design; datapath subsystem design; circuit simulation; basic device physics; simple device layout: structured chip design; timing; project chip; silicon compilers.

courses.title: VLSI System Design
courses.description: Semi-custom ASIC VLSI design flow; RTL coding, logic synthesis, automatic placement & routing, memory and interface design, signal integrity solutions, hardware acceleration and approximation

courses.title: Robotic Mobility
courses.description: Robot gait design; the kinematics and dynamics of locomotion; control adaptations for complex terrains.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra on the level of EE 510, Arduino and servomotors on the level of EE 109, and C++ programming on the level of EE 355

courses.title: Linear System Theory
courses.description: Analysis of linear dynamical systems by state-space and input-output techniques; stability, controllability, observability; observer-based controller; linear quadratic regulator.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 510

courses.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
courses.description: State-space Models. Equilibrium points. Limit Cycles. Linearization. Nonlinear Phenomena. Lyapunov Stability. Analysis and Design of Nonlinear Systems. Passivity. Backstepping. Feedback and Input-Output Linearization.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 585

courses.title: Quantum Information Theory
courses.description: Quantum Shannon theory: quantum channels and entanglement; dense coding, teleportation, quantum compression, and quantum capacity theorems. Open problems in quantum communication.
courses.recommended_prep: A strong working knowledge of complex linear algebra and probability theory (at the level of MATH 225, MATH 307, EE 364, etc.); knowledge of quantum information at the level of EE 520 or EE 514

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Reconstruction
courses.description: Principles of magnetic resonance imaging. Fourier-based acquisition and reconstruction, tissue contrast, system imperfections, artifact correction, advanced image reconstruction including AI, quantitative biomarkers, laboratory experiments.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra (on the level of EE 510), Biomedical imaging (BME 525), Linear control systems (EE 482), Probability and Statistics (EE 503), and write/modify signal and image processing code in MATLAB

courses.title: Computational Methods for Inverse Problems
courses.description: A rigorous description of vector space and functional analysis concepts and tools that are useful for solving inverse problems in real-world applications.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 503

courses.title: Robust Multivariable Control
courses.description: Singular values of the various sensitivity matrices are introduced to quantify the benefits of multivariable feedback systems operating in an uncertain environment and controllers are designed for the worst-case disturbances making them "robust."
courses.recommended_prep: Nonlinear and Adaptive Control on the level of EE 587

courses.title: Wavelets and Graphs for Signal Processing and Machine Learning
courses.description: Multirate signal processing, wavelets and filter banks. Overcomplete and sparse signal representations. Graph signal processing. Applications to compression, sensing, time-frequency analysis, and machine learning.

courses.title: Wireless Networks
courses.description: Introduction to wireless networking technologies; fundamental architectural and design principles used at all protocol layers; optimization, performance evaluation and implementation using mathematical analysis, simulations, and experiments.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 467 or equivalent; familiarity with Matlab and C programming

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: The course content will be selected each semester to reflect current trends and developments in the field of electrical engineering.

courses.title: Microelectromechanical Systems
courses.description: Exploration of the technology methods and physical principles of MEMS, and survey various MEMS of current interest.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of microfabrication, electromagnetic fields and waves, and mechanics

courses.title: Quantum Optimization Algorithms
courses.description: Introduction to quantum computing; analysis of quantum algorithms; matrix manipulation, gradient computation and optimization.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra on the level of MATH 471, mathematical optimization on the level of ISE 630 or ISE 631. Prior knowledge of quantum mechanics is not assumed.

courses.title: Survey of Energy and Power for a Sustainable Future
courses.description: Power production includes conventional fossil fuels, synthetic fuels, hydroelectric, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass and nuclear. The environmental consequences of various energy sources are discussed.
courses.recommended_prep: Graduate standing in Engineering, Physics, or Chemistry

courses.title: Mixed-Signal Integrated Circuits
courses.description: Fundamentals of sampling and discrete-time signals; analog to digital converters; digital to analog converters; switched-capacitor circuits.

courses.title: Integrated Communication Systems
courses.description: System- and transistor-level analysis and design of integrated circuits for wireless communications. Wireless communication concepts; radiofrequency transceiver architectures; low-noise amplifiers; mixers; oscillators; power amplifiers.

courses.title: Deep Learning Systems
courses.description: Neural networks for nonlinear regression, classification, reinforcement learning; back-propagation learning for multilayer perceptrons, convolutional and recurrent networks; applications in audio processing vision and autonomy.

courses.title: Machine Learning II: Mathematical Foundations and Methods
courses.description: Supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised machine learning; domain adaptation and transfer learning; human interpretability. Feasibility of learning, model complexity, and performance (error) on unseen data.
courses.recommended_prep: Experience with Python at the level of EE 541. Familiarity with general machine learning methods including regression and classification and with computational complexity at the level of EE 538

courses.title: Multimedia Data Compression
courses.description: Lossless compression, vector quantization, audio/speech coding, JPEG and JPEG-2000, MPEG and H.26x video compression standards, image/video quality assessment and emerging multimedia compression techniques and applications.
courses.recommended_prep: EE 503 and C/C++ programming on the level of EE 355

courses.title: Advanced Computer Vision
courses.description: Fundamental issues in computer vision: theory, algorithms and applications. Image formation, image segmentation, inference and measurement of 3-D, motion analysis, object and activity recognition.
courses.recommended_prep: Calculus, analytical geometry, linear algebra and probability theory. Programming in C or C++, data structures, algorithms

courses.title: Computer-Aided Design of Digital Systems
courses.description: A contemporary look at solving VLSI design problems using computer aided design and machine learning, including models, algorithms and techniques for physical design and synthesis.
courses.recommended_prep: MOS VLSI circuit design on the level of EE 477 is required; recommended are VLSI system design (e.g., EE 577a), algorithm analysis (e.g., CSCI 570), programming (e.g., CSCI 455x)

courses.title: Law, AI and Intellectual Property for Engineers
courses.description: Detailed introduction to the modern American legal system with a special focus on current artificial-intelligence techniques and intellectual-property doctrines.
courses.recommended_prep: Some familiarity with modern programming languages and statistical software packages like R and MATLAB; basic techniques in probability and statistics on the level of EE 503

courses.description: A weekly seminar series led by ECE faculty and guest lecturers about current and emerging areas of electrical and computer engineering research.

courses.description: Exploring and analyzing the ethical and social impact of technological innovation and advancement through humanities-based inquiry.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Ethical issues in artificial intelligence including algorithmic bias and interpretability, data privacy and control, autonomous systems and relationships with AI entities.

courses.title: Special Topics

courses.description: Writing of engineering curriculum- and research-related projects for PhD students. Focus is on conference papers, dissertations and proposals, journal articles and other forms.

courses.description: Academic and professional presentation skills for PhD students. Preparation for qualifying exams, conference paper presentations and other forms of oral communication. courses.title: Principles of Emergency Management
courses.description: Explores the historical development of emergency management as a distinct discipline in the United States and abroad, including theories, terminology and international coordination.

courses.title: Emergency Management Policies and Regulations
courses.description: Examines policies, regulations, politics and budgets that impact emergency management domestically and internationally in the government, non-profit and private sectors.

courses.title: Social and Cultural Competency in Emergency Management
courses.description: Explores how emergency management practices and community interactions can help address social, economic and cultural inequities while building increased resilience.

courses.title: Emergency Management Administration
courses.description: Examines the administrative functions of an emergency manager, including project management, policy implementation, acquisition of funding and managing diverse teams.

courses.title: Critical Decision-Making in Emergency Management
courses.description: Explores how to manage and assess information to limit risk and make ethical, critical decisions under both steady-state and crisis situations.

courses.title: Emergency Management and Disaster Planning
courses.description: Examines the necessary components of deliberate and crisis action plans that are used to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.

courses.title: Operational Coordination in Emergency Management
courses.description: Focuses on the complexity of post-disaster immediate and long-term response and recovery challenges in local, state, federal and international jurisdictions.

courses.title: Critical Infrastructure in Emergency Management
courses.description: Examines the wide spectrum of security threats to critical infrastructure and how to strengthen infrastructure protection and resilience through collaborative partnerships across sectors.

courses.title: Emergency Management Communication
courses.description: Creating inclusive and credible messages of risk across the disaster life cycle through a variety of methods.

courses.title: Driving Successful Outcomes in Emergency Management
courses.description: Explores how effective emergency management leaders develop trust, avoid ethical pitfalls, strengthen partnerships, and promote access throughout the disaster life cycle.

courses.title: Equity and Resilience in Emergency Management
courses.description: Examines resilience in emergency management as it pertains to areas such as planning, mitigation, disaster logistics and supply chains.

courses.title: Emergency Management Capstone
courses.description: Demonstrate knowledge and skills developed throughout the emergency management program in an integrated way.

courses.title: Environmental Engineering Principles
courses.description: Analysis of water, air and land pollution, including hazardous waste; engineering of mitigation measures; water and wastewater treatment systems.
courses.recommended_prep: CE 110

courses.title: Energy Systems and Environmental Tradeoffs
courses.description: Energy fundamentals; critical issues facing energy extraction, cultivation, transformation, transportation, consumption and disposal; environmental impacts.

courses.title: Contaminant Transport in the Environment
courses.description: Fundamentals of the physical mechanisms controlling solute transport in environmental flows.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of environmental engineering principles on the level of ENE 200

courses.title: Particulate Air Pollutants: Properties/Behavior/Measurement
courses.description: Particulate air pollutants, their measurement and instrumentation methods and their effects on the environment and human health; optical properties and visibility degradation.

courses.title: Air Pollution Fundamentals
courses.description: Quantitative overview of air pollution and the physical and chemical processes that describe its behavior.
courses.recommended_prep: Environmental engineering principles on the level of ENE 200

courses.title: Water Supply and Sewerage System Design
courses.description: Design of water supply systems, storm drains, sanitary sewers, and lift stations.

courses.title: Environmental and Regulatory Compliance
courses.description: Federal and state environmental laws; environmental impact assessment techniques; permitting for industrial facility construction and operation.

courses.title: Energy and the Environment
courses.description: The environmental impacts of energy extraction, cultivation, transformation, transportation, and consumption.

courses.title: Potable Water Reuse
courses.description: Fundamentals of potable water reuse from theory to practice; indirect and direct reuse; pathogens and treatments; regulations; and operations. Includes guest presentations and site visit.
courses.recommended_prep: Physicochemical Processes on the level of CE 523, Biological Processes on the level of CE 553, and Aquatic Chemistry on the level of ENE 562

courses.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Application of the fundamentals on the physical laws governing fluid flow and analyzing transport of contaminant in the environment and the risks involved.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate fluid mechanics on the level of CE 309 or AME 309.

courses.title: Physiochemical Processes in Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Concepts and applications of physicochemical processes in engineered systems, including coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, adsorption and membrane processes.
courses.recommended_prep: CE 363 and CE 485

courses.title: Applied Air Quality Management
courses.description: Air pollutants, emission levels, and air borne concentrations; Links between pollutant emissions, air quality measurements and health effects; Environmental management in private or public sectors.
courses.recommended_prep: Knowledge of general chemistry on the level of CHEM 105bL or CHEM 115bL; thermodynamics on the level of AME 310; and calculus on the level of MATH 226 or MATH 229

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A study of emotional intelligence through literature, history and the arts with a focus on anger, happiness, love and empathy.

courses.description: An exploration of the culture, vibrance, heritage, mythology, variety, and pathology of a city that was born in hopes and captured the worlds imagination. Duplicates credit in ARLT 101g.

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Close study of Shakespeare's plays and poems to introduce his language, stagecraft, literary "genius," social and literary contexts, precursors and rivals, and legacy.

courses.description: History, political-economy and aesthetics of the African Diaspora with emphasis on Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe and Africa.

courses.description: Intensive reading of major writers, 1800-1950.

courses.title: Introduction to Narrative Medicine
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of literary modes of narrative and their uses in medical understanding, character formation, social identity, and relations between mind and body.

courses.title: Introduction to Dramatic Literature
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

courses.description: Historical survey of the traditions of lyric poetry from Shakespeare to the contemporary, examining the genre's multiple forms of literary, visual, and aural expression.

courses.description: Literary travel using novels to explore regional culture and unify the study of literature, history, geography, politics and social studies.
