courses.title: The Firm in the National and International Economy
courses.description: The economic environment of business and international forces influencing business. Duplicates credit in GSBA 526 and GSBA 544.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Introduction to and overview of the fundamentals of entrepreneurship and corporate entrepreneurship - the practice of employing entrepreneurial skills and approaches within an organization. (Duplicates credit in BAEP 549, BAEP 551, GSBA 550ab.)

courses.title: Problem Solving and Decision Making: An Integrative Approach
courses.description: An integrative, multi-disciplined and immersion-based approach to addressing unstructured business situations and imperfect data using a variety of analytical tools and critical thought processes.

courses.title: Management and Organization of the Creative Industries
courses.description: How creative industries (motion pictures, television, publishing, radio, music, arts, games) operate and are organized. Critical discussion of pressing issues that these industries face.

courses.title: The Perspective of Top Management
courses.description: Using cases, students are introduced to top management issues of executive leadership, environmental and strategic analysis, use of financial statements, organizational assessment and design, technology management and decision support systems.

courses.title: Management of Operations
courses.description: Analysis of operations management and business functions; managerial accounting; finance; marketing; production; data processing and information systems; human resources management.

courses.title: Functional Strategies and Implementation
courses.description: Developing functional strategies and interdependence to achieve organizational goals; negotiations, conflict resolution; communication strategies; organizational effectiveness; implementation and change strategies; self-assessment and individual presentations.

courses.title: The Role of the Senior Executive
courses.description: Introduction to strategic management; executive leadership; environmental analysis; international context; financial growth strategies; social, legal and macroeconomic issues; role of CEO with boards, media and other publics; business ethics, strategic planning project. Recommended preparation: GSBA 534

courses.title: Environmental Analysis: Establishing Competitive Advantage
courses.description: Development of strategic planning processes; analysis of economic, social, political environment; forecasting; futures research; macroeconomics; international economics; technological developments; multinational management simulation; field projects.

courses.title: Strategic Planning for Growth
courses.description: Formulation and implementation of strategies in different organizational and environmental contexts; financial growth strategies; comparative management; impact of taxation; technology strategies; product development and new market strategies. (Duplicates credit in GSBA-572)

courses.title: Strategic Planning for Growth
courses.description: Formulation and implementation of strategies in different organizational and environmental contexts; financial growth strategies; comparative management; impact of taxation; technology strategies; product development and new market strategies. (Duplicates credit in GSBA-572)

courses.title: Managing Strategic Change and Implementation
courses.description: Management of the strategic change process for the total organization including implementing growth strategies, use of consultants, corporate governance, implementation in a multinational environment, leadership and power, use of technology, innovation, corporate cultures, executive succession, corporate relations.

courses.title: The Executive of the Future
courses.description: Forecasting future environments; the role of the executive in the future, changing organizations; executive development; personal development goal setting.

courses.title: Business Management and Operations
courses.description: Thematic focus on the formulation and implementation of business strategies related to issues affecting businesses including managerial accounting, operations, financial, and legal.

courses.title: The Global Context and International Business
courses.description: Impact of political, economic, social/cultural and institutional factors on business performance and industry structure in a global context. May require international travel.
courses.recommended_prep: MBA required courses

courses.title: The Global Context of Business (IELP)
courses.description: The economic and political realities of cross-border commerce in the 21st century. IELP. Requires international travel.
courses.recommended_prep: IBEAR MBA first term required courses

courses.title: International Business Consulting Project
courses.description: IBEAR team consulting projects addressing international business problems. Projects culminate in written and oral presentations to corporate clients.

courses.title: Practicum
courses.description: Experiential learning through practical training. Graded CR/NC.
courses.recommended_prep: Completion of required course work in a Marshall graduate

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: Apply concepts learned to a complex strategic team project resulting in a presentation to a sponsoring company, written report, and postmortem reflection.

courses.title: Field Research in Business
courses.description: Individual or team projects studying the business practices of an industry, company, government agency, country, geographic region, etc. Proposal, data collection, analyses, and written report. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Independent Research in Business
courses.description: Independent research beyond normal course offerings. Proposal, research and written report/paper required. Open only to Masters Students. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Internship in Business
courses.description: Supervised on-the-job business experience in the student's area of interest. (Curricular Practical Training) Graduate business students only. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Research Practicum in Business
courses.description: Hands-on practical experience working with a Marshall faculty member on an ongoing research project. Open only to master's and doctoral students. Graded Credit/No Credit.

courses.title: Consulting Project in Business
courses.description: Individual or team project solving real business problems for an existing business entity, domestic and/or international. Proposal, field research, analyses and oral and written presentations. Open only to master and doctoral students.

courses.title: Selected Issues in Economic Theory I
courses.description: Methodology and research perspectives of economics; contribution of the economics paradigm to accounting, management, finance, marketing, and decision sciences.

courses.title: Causal Inference Research Methods
courses.description: Contemporary approaches to causal inference in observational data for applied research in the social sciences.
courses.recommended_prep: one semester of graduate level econometrics and knowledge of STATA and R

courses.title: Selected Issues in Economic Theory II
courses.description: Further investigation of selected topics in methodology and research perspectives of economics. Topics vary in response to new developments and current trends in the field.

courses.title: Research
courses.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.description: Credit on acceptance of Dissertation.

courses.title: Foundations of Global Security
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A survey of theories and challenges relating to International Relations and security studies broadly defined from WWI to present conflicts including human, environmental and economic concepts.

courses.title: Security and Global Governance
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Major theoretical approaches to the study of war; focus is on recent issues in security studies.

courses.title: Transnational Crime and Global Illicit Networks
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to and overview of transnational organized crime; its effects on international security, political, social and economic development of countries around the world.

courses.title: National Intelligence and Global Security
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploration of how intelligence affects global security and the formation and implementation of foreign and security policy.

courses.title: Human Security and Humanitarian Intervention
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explore causes of human security threats, challenges to state sovereignty and actions to address failed states, conflicts and protect people through humanitarian intervention.

courses.title: Global Human Rights
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores competing conceptions of human rights, whether human rights are universal, problems of enforcement and the role of human rights in foreign policy.

courses.title: Human Impact of Genocide and Mass Violence
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of the consequences of genocide and mass violence on human security and individual well-being and an exploration of processes to address mass atrocities.

courses.title: Introduction to Human and Evolutionary Biology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the major and field of human and evolutionary biology; sub-disciplines, career options and areas for research; guest speakers.

courses.title: Nutrition for Life
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: To develop an understanding of Nutrition, especially as it pertains to optimal health and prevention of diseases. A study of macro and micro nutrients.

courses.title: The Science of Sport
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The physiological and nutritional basis of human performance. Factors that facilitate and limit athletic achievement. Lecture, 3 hours; laboratory, 2 hours. Not available for major credit. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 205Lxg.

courses.title: Mediterranean and Healthy Lifestyles in the World
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores and contrasts the core components of the traditional mediterranean lifestyle to those of other lifestyles in the world. Biological and anthropological perspectives for following sustainable lifestyles to improve and maintain personal health.

courses.title: The Pharmacology of Performance-Enhancing Drugs
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Evaluation of drugs, nutritional supplements, and ergogenic aids that are purported to enhance human athletic performance.

courses.title: Human Anatomy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Major organ systems; functional implications of their relationships; gross and microscopic examination with an emphasis on practical skills in recognizing, dissecting, and differentiating anatomical structures. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 301L.

courses.title: Nutrition and Metabolism
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Gastrointestinal physiology and energy metabolism as it relates to macronutrient intake. Theories and principles of nutrition and their impact on metabolic regulation. Prerequisites: BISC 220L or BISC 221L. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 200.

courses.title: The Human Machine
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An exploration of how the human body works and why it works the way it does; draws from the fields of anatomy, biomechanics, physiology, engineering and paleoanthropology.
courses.recommended_prep: HBIO 200Lg

courses.title: Muscle Physiology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of the skeletal muscular system (anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and development) and its functional properties under both normal and pathological conditions.

courses.title: Integrative Pathophysiology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of the immunological processes and pathophysiological changes that occur as consequences of various human diseases and conditions.

courses.title: Nutrition and Disease
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Principles of diet therapy for the prevention and treatment of human disease.

courses.title: Genetics and Disease
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An overview of the genetic underpinning of human health and disease. Inheritance of mendelian diseases, common diseases, developmental diseases and cancer; prenatal testing, genetic counseling and genetic therapies.

courses.title: Motor Control and Learning
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories of control and learning applied to motor performance; variables affecting performance in exercise, games, sports and dance.

courses.title: Physiology of Movement
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The physiological effects of exercise and training on musculoskeletal and circulatory systems, and the biomechanics of athletic performance

courses.title: Endocrinology and Metabolism
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Regulation of metabolic pathways and endocrinology in health and metabolic diseases.

courses.title: Biomechanics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Kinematic and kinetic analysis of human motion. Emphasis on performance enhancement and injury prevention.

courses.title: Metabolic Diseases
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the etiology, prevention, and treatment of metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus and obesity that are major threats to public health.

courses.title: Applied Human Physiology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The physiology of the respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, musculoskeletal, digestive, endocrine and nervous systems in humans, with application to human health and pathology.

courses.title: Neurobiology of Feeding Behavior and Obesity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Neurobiological systems that control feeding behavior and energy balance with an emphasis on the determinants of obesity.

courses.title: Prevention of Athletic Injuries
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Application of scientific principles to conditioning, protecting, and rehabilitating the athlete.

courses.title: Evaluation and Rehabilitation of Athletic Injuries
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Application of scientific principles to evaluating and rehabilitating athletic injuries.

courses.title: Laboratory Experience in Kinesiology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Practical laboratory experience in basic and applied exercise physiology, biochemistry, and/or biomechanics. Emphasizing development of laboratory techniques. Prerequisites: HBIO 203, HBIO 301, HBIO 302, HBIO 320. Duplicates credit in former EXSC 491.

courses.title: U.S. Health System: Healthcare Access and Delivery
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to U.S. health system with comprehensive overview of insurance coverage and benefits, reimbursement, access to healthcare and biopharmaceuticals, and the delivery of healthcare services.

courses.title: Comparative International Healthcare Systems
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Comparative analysis of healthcare coverage and financing policies across countries. Examine its relationship to drug coverage, access, reimbursement, pricing policies and impact on biopharmaceutical market.

courses.title: Foundations of Product Development and Commercialization
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to product development and commercialization of new healthcare technologies. Principles of clinical development, regulatory pathways, market access, reimbursement, pricing, and commercial product launch strategies.

courses.title: Business Implications of Healthcare Policy
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Overview of healthcare policies that impact payers, employers, healthcare industry, state/federal agencies and consumers.

courses.title: Applied Economic Analysis of U.S. Health Policies
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Evaluate healthcare policies' costs and benefits for diverse stakeholders using case studies and quantitative methods. Equip yourself to advocate for policy changes with data-driven insights.

courses.title: Healthcare Decision Analysis and Modeling
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Quantitative methods of evaluating business, policy, pharmaceuticals, medical care resource allocations. Budget Impact Models, Decision Trees, Sensitivity Analysis tradeoffs between treatment strategies, interventions, risks, outcomes.

courses.title: Health Economic and Outcomes Methodology
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Comprehensive review of the strategies used in drug value assessment with a focus on health economics and outcomes research and application to healthcare decision making.

courses.title: Healthcare Literature Analysis and Applications
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Conduct literature evaluations using practical approaches to analyze and critique medical and health economic literature with the aim of optimizing health policy and business decisions.

courses.title: Introduction to Healthcare Data Analytics
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Learn methods for working with large health data sets, including developing an analytic plan and selecting an appropriate data source, as well as practical skills needed to manage and use large health data sets to accomplish an analytic goal.

courses.title: Healthcare Data Analytics II
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Develop an analytical plan and conduct analysis of health-related datasets using RStudio and design data visualizations to summarize findings to support healthcare decision makers.

courses.title: Seminars in Healthcare Decision Analysis
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Weekly seminar and literature series, review and discuss policy, biopharmaceuticals, insurance, global healthcare access issues. Student lead discussions, expert guest speakers, group projects, critical thinking.

courses.title: Healthcare Consulting Enterprise Team Project
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Work as a consultant to conduct market research and apply decision analysis methods to design strategies for healthcare products and services or company pipelines.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate or professional degree in pharmacy, medical or sciences, engineering, business and/or equivalent experience in the healthcare industry

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Internship for Curricular Practical Training
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the student's field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least one full academic year of enrollment in the graduate program with a cumulative 3.0 GPA.

courses.title: Hebrew I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Focuses on the acquisition of proficiency and communicative skills in speaking, reading, writing, and comprehension as well as cultural literacy.

courses.title: Hebrew for Business, Technology and Media
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Effective communication in Hebrew, exploration of Israel's economy in the context of globalization, improving language skills for use in the global job market.

courses.title: Hebrew II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A continuation of Hebrew I. Offers a higher level of skill development in reading, writing and conversation. Prerequisite: HEBR 120.

courses.title: Hebrew III
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Continuation of Hebrew II; stress on grammar, composition, and conversation. Prerequisite: HEBR 150.

courses.title: Modern Hebrew Language (Hebrew IV)
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines Hebrew in depth and introduces students to Modern Hebrew literature through major poems, novels and films from the 20th and 21st centuries. Prerequisite: HEBR 220.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Special topics in Hebrew.

courses.title: The Worlds of Medieval Europe
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The social, political, religious, intellectual and cultural landscapes of Europe and the Mediterranean, c. 300 to c. 1400.

courses.title: The Emergence of Modern Europe
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Political, intellectual, and cultural developments in Europe, 13001815. Renaissance and Reformation; absolute monarchy, scientific changes, and Enlightenment; French Revolution and Napoleon.

courses.title: Modern Europe
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The Enlightenment, French Revolution, industrialization, Darwinism, socialism, nationalism, technological revolutions, mass culture, imperialism, race, fascism, communism, world wars, genocide, migration, the Cold War, terrorism.

courses.title: The Korean Past
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A topical and chronological study of the major political, social, and intellectual forces that have shaped the history of Korea.

courses.title: Introduction to the History of Japan
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Japan from the earliest times to the present; social, cultural,and political dimensions.

courses.title: Histories of South Asia
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History of South Asia from the tenth century to the present day; examines imperialism, capitalism, nationalism, and immigration.

courses.title: History of Early Africa
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Surveys the major dynamics of economic and political change in Sub-Saharan Africa before the imposition of European colonial rule in the late nineteenth century.

courses.title: African History Since 1880
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Surveys the social, economic and political lives of Africans since the imposition of European colonial rule in the late nineteenth century.

courses.title: The Arts and Society in Latin America, Colonial to Contemporary
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of the art, architecture, and visual culture of Latin America from the colonial period to the present, focusing on connections to culture and society.

courses.title: History of Science: Antiquity to the Scientific Revolution
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the history of premodern science and the social and intellectual processes and practices that have shaped the work of scientists.

courses.title: Approaches to History
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Methods and theories of historical interpretation of evidence; uses of archives; modes of presenting the past to the public. Required of all History majors. Duplicates credit in former HIST-300.

courses.title: How to Be An American: Global Histories of U.S. Citizenship
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History of United States citizenship from its origins to the present day, with particular attention to relationship between law and culture.

courses.title: Race in America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the origins of the idea of race and how this idea influenced the development of the United States from the colonial period to the present day.

courses.title: Histories of Dialogue, Disagreement, and Democracy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Traces American political disagreement from nationhood until the present day, exploring rhetoric, protest, and partisanship while connecting historical discourse to students' present-day civic engagement

courses.title: Film, Power, and American History
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: U.S. motion pictures as both a response to and comment upon major events, problems, and themes in 20th century America.

courses.title: The Russian Monarchy: Representation, Power, and Autocracy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the Russian monarchy and its representation in history and the arts. It studies film, literature, painting, sculpture, historiography, and political ideologies.

courses.title: History of California
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A thematic approach to California history from precontact to present; focus on peoples, environment, economic, social, and cultural development, politics, and rise to global influence.

courses.title: History of Science, Technology and Medicine
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The political, cultural, and social forces that have shaped scientific achievements in the modtern age.

courses.title: Business and East Asian Culture, 1800-Present
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Business history of East Asia (China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong) as related to culture, politics, and society.

courses.title: The Byzantine Empire, 324 - 1453
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of Byzantine political, social, economic, legal, cultural and religious history and its legacy today; primary sources and approaches which historians use to reconstruct the richness and complexity of the Byzantine past. Contacts with Arabic, Latin, Slavic, Georgian, Armenian, Persian, Turkic and Aramaic cultures; Byzantiums own Greek, Roman and Christian heritage.

courses.title: Ottomans and Empire: Anatolia, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean World
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of the history of the Ottomans and their imperial subjects.

courses.title: Heritage Archaeology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introduction to the field of heritage studies as it is practiced today, examining archaeological, ethnohistorical and ethnographic theory and methodologies, mixed-methods approaches and research.
courses.recommended_prep: ANTH 202

courses.title: Archaeology of Egypt and the Near East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of archaeology and excavated artifacts from Egypt and the Near East.

courses.title: The Renaissance
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The flowering of arts, literature, and learning at the end of the Middle Ages.

courses.title: Native Americans in American Public Life
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Role of Native Americans in American public life from colonial times to the present; Native American societies and governments and their relations to the U.S.

courses.title: The Crusades
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines wars between European Christian and Muslim armies in the Middle East, 1096-1291 and their cultural, military, religious and artistic legacies.

courses.title: Anti-Semitism, Racism and Other Hatreds
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History and contexts of anti-Semitism, racism and other discourses about difference examined through religious, national and cultural forms in Europe and in the US.

courses.title: The Holocaust in 20th Century Europe
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The origins and development of anti-Jewish persecution in Germany, resulting in the systematic mass murder of Europe's Jews during World War.

courses.title: The British Empire: 1588-1834
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Emergence of the British Empire, emphasizing colonies in the Americas; the development of imperial economy, imperial wars, slavery and abolitionism.

courses.title: History of the Samurai
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Development of the Japanese samurai from the 6th to the 16th centuries. Recommended preparation: a course in East Asian history

courses.title: History of Japan, 1550-1945
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Development of Japan as a modern world power; tradition and change in Japanese life; impact of Western culture, politics, and diplomacy from 1550 to 1945.

courses.title: Japan Since 1945
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of the impact of World War II, American occupation, and rapid economic growth on Japan's politics, society, economy, and culture; Japan as a post-modern nation.

courses.title: History of China Since 1800
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Western impact and dynastic decline; problems of the Chinese Republic; nationalism and communism.

courses.title: The American Revolution
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Origins, course and consequences of the American Revolution; the post-war establishment of the Constitution.

courses.title: The American Civil War
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The causes, course, campaigns, and consequences of the American Civil War, 1861-1865.

courses.title: Mexican Migration to the United States
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Mexican migration from the 1850s to the present, emphasizing labor migrants to the United States.

courses.title: The African-American Experience
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An historical and social analysis of the African- American experience from Colonial times to the present.

courses.title: History of the Mexican American
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Racial and cultural background of Mexico; immigration and conquest; the Mexican in California and the southwest; the rise of contemporary Mexican-American consciousness.

courses.title: Introduction to Asian American History
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Comparative examination of the social, economic, and political experiences of Asian immigrants and their descendants in the U.S., 1840s-present.

courses.title: Modern Iran
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History and culture of modern Iran from the nineteenth century to present through historical and ethnographic approaches to Iran today, richly contextualizing events and people.

courses.title: Feminist Histories of South Asia
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History of South Asia with attention to questions of gender, sexuality and power with a focus on the eighteenth, nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

courses.title: Sex and the City: Constructing Gender in London, 1700-1900
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores changes in gender expectations in England between 1700 and 1900 through readings and one-week travel to London

courses.title: Gender, Madness and Modernism in Freud's Vienna
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An exploration of modernism, madness, Jews and politics in Vienna around 1900 which foregrounds women, gender and sexuality. Includes international travel to Vienna.

major_restrictions.groupDescription: Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

courses.title: Heretics and Prophets in the Middle Ages
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Beliefs of European heretics 1000 - 1400 and practices of religious persecution, with special consideration given to problems of evidence gained through interrogation or torture.

courses.title: History of Soviet Russia: 1917-1991
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The birth of the totalitarian regime, the emergence of the superpower and the socio-economic, political, cultural developments that culminate in its demise.

courses.title: European Intellectual and Cultural History: The 20th Century, 1920 to the Present
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intellectual and cultural trends of contemporary Europe, including Dadaism, Surrealism, Western Marxism, Fascism, Existentialism and Structuralism.

courses.title: The German Question: Nation and Identity in Modern Central Europe
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A seminar on the making, unmaking and re-making of the German nation-state, with particular attention to issues of race, class and gender in German identity.

courses.title: Histories of the Apocalypse
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A historical overview of apocalyptic hopes and fears, from Revelations to the present. New World explorations, utopian communes, nuclear war, zombies, climate change.

courses.title: Environmental Issues in Society
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploration of the major social, political, economic, religious, and philosophical disagreements that exist between scholars, leaders, and citizens concerning today's most serious environmental issues and problems. Not available for credit to environmental studies majors and minors.

courses.title: International Relations: Introductory Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to contending theoretical and analytical approaches; development of critical, evaluative, cognitive, and analytical competencies regarding historical and contemporary issues.

courses.title: International Relations: Approaches to Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to theoretically oriented research approaches and designs; emphasis on the logic of argumentation.

courses.title: Historical Approaches to International Relations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to historical research methods with an emphasis on historical texts and modes of discourse.

courses.title: The Global Economy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Economic and political concepts necessary to the understanding of the modern global economy. Topics include international trade, foreign investment and migration.

courses.title: Leadership and Diplomacy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The role of leaders, diplomatic leadership and creativity in statecraft, providing a deep understanding of the theoretical and practical dimensions of diplomacy.

courses.title: National Intelligence and the Shaping of Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The focus is intelligence to improve the making of policy, with attention to collection; overt and covert, operations; domestic intelligence; and oversight in democracies.

courses.title: Managing New Global Challenges
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines the strategies for managing global issues in the post Cold War period. Explores ways that international institutions, national governments and non-state actors work separately and together to provide order and control over complex international issues areas. courses.title: International Organizations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The emergence of international organizations as a permanent feature in world politics; role of the United Nations Organization as well as regional international organizations.

courses.title: Contemporary International Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of recent events, forces, and conditions in the international political system.

courses.title: Economic Globalization
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Globalization makes national borders and regulations increasingly obsolete. Analyzes the economic foundation of globalization, its consequences and efforts to manage it.

courses.title: Peace and Conflict Studies
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Interdisciplinary study of the pursuit of peace, including causes of wars, arms races, conflict resolution, peace movements, nonviolent resistance, and peace with justice.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to statistical analysis with R, with applications to the study of International Relations: data manipulation, hypothesis testing, regression, causality, text analysis, visualization, and network analysis.

courses.title: Religions and Political Violence
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introduction to debates about the intersection of religion and conflict in politics and international affairs; theoretical, classical, and contemporary issues.

courses.title: The Political Economy of Africa
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Understand contemporary outcomes across the African continent; examine the effects of, among others, ecology, the slave trades, European colonialism and geopolitics.

courses.title: Violent Conflict
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Origins and evolution of violent conflict among humans; modern efforts to end conflict; recent research in archaeology, anthropology, biology, economics, political science and psychology.

courses.title: Human Security and Humanitarian Intervention
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explore causes of human security, international responses to issues like violence, displacement and climate change; and the costs, benefits and effects of humanitarian intervention.

courses.title: Technology and International Relations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Impact of technological advances to global security and development. Focus on surveillance and cyber conflict; nuclear weaponry, aviation and UAVs missiles and BMD; submarines and ASW.

courses.title: Civil War, Peace Building and International Intervention
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the causes of civil war, the dynamics and consequences of civil war and how peace is or is not built.

courses.title: North-South Relations in the Global Economy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of inequality in relations between developed and developing states; contending views on the causes and legacies of imperialism; development strategies and aid.

courses.title: The Global Finance and Monetary Regime
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The international financial and monetary regime, its evolution and the problems facing it today

courses.title: Politics of the World Economy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploration of questions and concepts in international economics and politics, especially as they relate to flows of trade, capital, people, and problems across borders.

courses.title: The Global Economy 2040
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of key ideas from economics, demography and technology. Guest lecturers illuminate possible conditions of the Global Economy in 2040.

courses.title: Money, Guns and Oil
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the relationship between economics, security, and U.S. foreign policy. Topics covered: U.S. grand strategy, Chinas rise, energy security, resource competition, and the resource curse.

courses.title: Public Health and International Relations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of threats to global security, state sovereignty and population health posed by infectious diseases, natural disasters, war and civil conflict.

courses.title: The Political Economy of China
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Sources, consequences, challenges to China's economic growth, including rural and urban economies, entrepreneurship, central and local governments, inequality, trade, investment, finance, demographics, and the environment.

courses.title: The Politics and Strategy of Weapons of Mass Destruction
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Causes and effects of use and spread of nuclear, biological and chemical weapons; responses to WMD, including deterrence, preventive war, and non-proliferation policies and negotiations.

courses.title: U.S. Foreign Policy Since World War II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of U.S. foreign policy since 1945 as a basis for understanding significant new trends. Explanation of contemporary issues in U.S. relations with other nations.

courses.title: The Global South in World Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Origin, concepts, realities and ideals of the non-aligned movement, focusing on the role of the United States in the developing world.

courses.title: Russian and Post-Soviet Foreign Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of Tsarist and Soviet experience as background to detailed examination of the political, economic and ideological forces behind contemporary Russian foreign policy.

courses.title: Human Rights in Post-Soviet Eurasia
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Course examines the struggle for the protection and expansion of human rights in the Post-Communist space across Russia, Ukraine, Caucasus and Central Asia.

courses.title: Power and Authority in the Middle East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A comparative examination of social relations of power and institutions with a special focus on intellectual traditions, the law, and social movements.

courses.title: Urban Politics in the Global South
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of social and economic justice in the questions of urban governance facing cities in the developing world.

courses.title: The United States and the Middle East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Critical perspectives on U.S. relations with the Middle East, including the discourses surrounding democracy and globalization.

courses.title: The Political Economy of Latin American Development
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The main economic development themes and strategies in Latin America over the past century. The interplay between domestic and international variables, and the resulting dynamic changes.

courses.title: Politics and Democracy in Latin America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines Latin America's experience with democracy emphasizing events since the 1980s. Analyzes the roles of interest groups, ideology, domestic politics, bureaucratic processes, perceptions and analogical reasoning.

courses.title: Mexico and its Relations with the United States
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of Mexico and U.S.-Mexico relations, both historically and in the present day, to understand better the challenges in this key bilateral relationship.

courses.title: Global Civil Society: Non-State Actors in World Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of diplomatic and moral relationships between sovereign states and transnational non-state actors, both benevolent (humanitarian groups and philanthropies) and malevolent (mercenaries, pirates and terrorists).

courses.title: Introduction to International Security
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Key concepts in international security studies; historical evolution of international warfare and diplomacy; contemporary international security issues.

courses.title: Asian Security Issues
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to key security trends in the Asia-Pacific region, emphasizing strategic competition between U.S., Russia, and China; regional military capabilities; rise of neutrality politics.

courses.title: Terrorism and Counterterrorism
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of terrorism and responses to terrorism, including how societies understand and deal with terrorism; focus on ethical and normative issues.

courses.title: Directed International Relations Field Study
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive internship experience in international relations professional areas with academic research component (may be repeated for credit different semesters)

courses.title: Theories of War
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Causes of war; means of prevention and consequences of war.

courses.title: Chinese Foreign Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The domestic and international sources of Chinese foreign policy; political, military, and economic issues in China's relations with its neighbors.

courses.title: Applied Data Science for International Relations 1
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to statistical computing and data visualization in R. Focus on visualization of descriptive statistics; create publication-ready figures for actual faculty research projects.

courses.title: Applied Data Science for International Relations 2
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intermediate statistical computing and data visualization in R. Focus the on graphical presentation of complex statistical relationships. Students create publication-ready figures for actual faculty research projects.

courses.title: Political Economy of Corruption
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines causes, consequences and how to combat corruption as an economic, political and social problem.
courses.recommended_prep: IR 213 and IR 330

courses.title: The New Triangle: China, the U.S. and Latin America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: China's rise in the international political economy raises policy research questions, including an analysis of how this trend relates to U.S and Latin American relations. Recommended preparation: Micro and macro economics

courses.title: Seminar on Economics and Security
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to important economic issue areas that are understood as security-related in the contemporary world: population, food, trade, debt, etc.

courses.title: Commercial and Financial Globalization-Trends, Challenges
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Factors determining the feasibility, desirability and limits of economic globalization; the dynamics triggered by the Global Financial Crisis and the backlash against Globalization.

courses.title: Historical Memory, Identity, and International Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Seminar on the role of historical memory in conflicts, in foreign policy formation, and in the creation, alteration, and defense of state identity.

courses.title: Comparative Genocide
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An interdisciplinary treatment of the tragic phenomenon of genocide. Subject matter includes historical cases and analysis of contemporary global efforts toward prevention.

courses.title: Cities of the Middle East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An examination of the economic, political and cultural forces operating in a number of Middle Eastern cities.

courses.title: The Political Economy of Autocracy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of autocracy, the world's most common form of government: its political economy, the role of elections, parties, repression, propaganda and civil resistance.

courses.title: Political Economy of Redistribution
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Course examines inequality in the Global South and compares tax and welfare regimes to understand how states pursue redistribution and development.

courses.title: State-Building, Institutions in Middle East and North Africa
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The interaction of institutions, preferences and historical legacies in the building of state-institutions in the Middle East and North Africa.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Selected topics in various special areas within international relations, which may vary from semester to semester or within semesters.

courses.title: Persian I

courses.description: Introduction to contemporary Persian (Farsi). Oral practice, listening and reading comprehension, grammar and vocabulary necessary for simple spoken and written expression. (Duplicates credit in former MDES-120)

courses.title: Persian II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Continuation of Persian I. Prerequisite: IRAN 120. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 150)

courses.title: Persian III
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intermediate Persian (Farsi). Building conversational skills, listening and reading comprehension, grammar and vocabulary necessary for intermediate level spoken and written expression. Prerequisite: IRAN 150. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 220)

courses.title: Persian IV
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Continuing Intermediate Persian (Farsi). Building conversational skills, listening and reading comprehension, grammar and vocabulary necessary for intermediate level spoken and written expression. Prerequisite: IRAN 220. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 250)

courses.title: Advanced Persian I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Advanced verbal and written expression in Persian, including deeper understanding of Persian culture. Prerequisite: IRAN 250. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 320)

courses.title: Advanced Persian II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Continuation of Advanced Persian I. Prerequisite: IRAN 320. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 350)

courses.title: Introduction to Industrial and Systems Engineering
courses.description: A combination of plant tours, laboratory experiences, and lecture are used to introduce the philosophy, subject matter, aims, goals, and techniques of industrial and systems engineering.

courses.title: Solving Engineering Problems using Python
courses.description: Engineering examples are used as a platform to introduce computer programming skills for problem solving; critical thinking skills.

courses.title: Foundations of Probability Modeling
courses.description: Techniques for modeling uncertainty: discrete and continuous random variables, probability distributions, expectations and conditional probability; Poisson processes, Markov chains and queuing decision models.

courses.title: Foundations of Data Analysis
courses.description: Sampling distributions; confidence intervals and hypothesis testing; analysis of variance; regression; data aggregation; prediction and classification.

courses.title: Engineering Project Management
courses.description: Managing a project intended to create an engineered system. Methods, processes, tools. Lessons-learned from actual practice. Case studies from real projects. Presentations by student teams.

courses.title: Optimization
courses.description: Modeling, solution analysis and applications of complex decision problems using linear, dynamic and integer optimization.

courses.title: Enterprise Data Analytics
courses.description: Methodology to store, organize, cleanse, harmonize and stage enterprise data for analytics. Report, visualize, slice and dice, forecast and predict trends.

courses.title: Principles and Practices of Systems Engineering
courses.description: Systems as complex collaborative ensembles of interconnected components. Theory and practice of requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, operation and disposal. Case studies from real projects.

courses.title: Human Factors in Work and Systems Design
courses.description: Role of humans in technological systems; human-systems integration; ergonomics; anthropometry and workstation design; work methods and measurement; human error, safety and accident analysis.

courses.title: Planning and Scheduling for Production and Supply Chains
courses.description: Production, resource and service planning, forecasting, scheduling, vendor and location selection, inventory; integrated decision systems for the control of production, services and supply chains.

courses.title: Discrete Systems Simulation
courses.description: Modeling of complex discrete event systems, input and output analysis, system evaluation via experimentation on the simulation model, applications to industrial and systems engineering problems.

courses.title: Socio-Technical Systems and Work Organizations
courses.description: Design, modeling and analysis of complex systems, challenges they present and methods for resolving those challenges. Impact of technology on work and organizational design.

courses.title: Engineering Decisions, Economics and Ethics
courses.description: Principles of economic analysis and decision analysis for engineering systems, including applications in financing, developing and comparing new technologies.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Senior Design Project
courses.description: Investigate client organization operations, evaluate alternative designs to meet client needs, complete preliminary design review.

courses.title: Senior Design Project
courses.description: Develop the detailed design including countermeasures for risks, complete critical design review, implement the project plan, close-out the project.

courses.title: Construction Accounting, Finance and Strategy
courses.description: Fundamental accounting principles, financial analysis and financial control, strategic management and a review of alternative project delivery methods.

courses.title: Health Analytics

courses.recommended_prep: Statistics on the level of ISE 225; programming on the level of ISE 150 (familiarity with R would be helpful). Course illustrates health examples of predictive analytics and data mining, so prior preparation in ISE 529 and ISE 535 is helpful but not required.

courses.title: Practicum in Health Care Systems
courses.description: Application of performance and efficiency tools to streamline hospital operations. Group projects collaborating with hospital staff.
courses.recommended_prep: Engineering statistics at the level of ISE 225

courses.title: Logistics and Inventory Systems
courses.description: Practice in inventory management, computerized procedures, materials requirements planning. Deterministic and stochastic demand systems with static/dynamic models.

courses.title: Advanced Production Planning and Scheduling
courses.description: Dependencies among long, intermediate and short-range planning and scheduling of production systems considering objectives, technological constraints and solution algorithms.
courses.recommended_prep: prior knowledge of operations research and probability theory.

courses.title: Engineering Project Management
courses.description: Methods, processes and tools for managing projects to create engineered systems. Project management; engineering economics; risk management. Industry-drawn large-scale engineering case studies. Team project presentations.

courses.title: Stochastic Processes for Financial Engineering
courses.description: Theory and applications of stochastic processes relevant to financial engineering. Stochastic processes, Brownian motion, martingales, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo Simulations with financial application examples.

courses.title: Engineering Management of Systems Integration
courses.description: Foundations of systems integration; advanced topics in systems integration including generative artificial intelligence (AI); data analytics for predicting and supporting engineering decisions.

courses.title: Foundations of Analytics
courses.description: Foundational tools, technologies and methodologies for analytics. The statistical basis of analytics. Understanding and preparing data. Python, SQL and exploratory data analysis.

courses.title: Quality Management for Engineers
courses.description: Principles of quality management, quality philosophies and frameworks, role of leadership and strategic planning to improve quality, process management, measurements to improve quality and performance.

courses.title: Optimization Methods for Analytics

courses.title: Applied Generative Artificial Intelligence for Enterprises

courses.title: Fundamentals of Data Engineering
