courses.title: Arts Journalism: Storytelling and Production
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Reporting and writing on the arts; strategies for arts journalism in the digital era; survey of essays and reviews by great critics.

courses.title: Arts Criticism and Commentary
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Writing workshops and independent fieldwork; development of critical skills to write socially valuable criticism and commentary about art, entertainment and culture.

courses.title: Master's Thesis
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis.

courses.title: Master's Thesis
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis.

courses.title: Master's Thesis
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

courses.title: Critical Thinking: The Art and Science of Not Getting Fooled
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Researching and writing about how not to get fooled as a journalist; includes research, writing and discussion. Open only to journalism and specialized journalism majors.

courses.title: Follow the Money: Business and Economics
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Reporting and writing on business, economics and public finance; students produce a series of professional projects for publication.

courses.title: Journalism Capstone Project
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Production of a journalism capstone project with multimedia elements for a master's degree. Projects can be single stand-alone pieces, or series of pieces.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: Seminar in selected topics in journalism.

courses.title: Jewish History
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Major ideas, personalities, and movements in Jewish history from antiquity to the present in light of the interaction of the Jews with the general culture.

courses.title: Jewish Histories of the Modern Middle East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores Jewish participation in the social, cultural, political and economic life of the modern Middle East.

courses.title: Exploring the Hebrew Bible
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploring the Hebrew Bible, the world in which it arose, and influential texts, including work from Ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia and the Southern Levant.

courses.title: Judaism
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Jewish beliefs, practices, and history from the biblical period to the present; Judaic contributions to Western civilization.

courses.title: The Holocaust
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Historical background and responses to the Holocaust, withspecial emphasis on ethical implications.

courses.title: Food and Faith
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Investigates how food and food traditions create and traverse religious and social relationships between Jews, Christians and Muslims by exploring religious traditions, practice, and ethics.

courses.title: The Eastern European Jewish Experience: Literature and Film
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analyzes works by different artists -- writers, filmmakers, painters -- in order to understand the significant contribution that the Jewish experience in Eastern Europe has made to Jewish communities worldwide.

courses.title: Holy War And History: Jews, Christians, Muslims
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Investigates the engagement in war by Judaism, Christianity and Islam by examining history and theology and looks at religious justifications and condemnations of war.

courses.title: The Sephardic World
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Sephardic Jews trace their ancestry to medieval Iberia and now comprise a global diaspora. Explore the creation and expansion of the Sephardic diaspora.

courses.title: Jewish Names: People, Families, Pets and Organizations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduces history and customs related to Jewish names, from individuals to organizations to places by discussing name popularity, histories of name changing and naming rituals.

courses.title: Representing: Contemporary Sephardic and Mizrahi Jews
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Jewish experience outside of Europe is explored through film and literature. Topics include Jewish-Muslim relations, Orientalism, transnationalism, linguistic histories, notions of homeland and gender.

courses.title: Scripture and Polemic in Judaism, Christianity and Islam
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Origins of Scriptures and their polemical environments in earliest Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Scripture as polemic and legitimation, and cross-religious/cross-cultural interpretation and argument based on scriptural themes.

courses.title: Jews, Judaism and Race
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examine the history of race and racialization in Jewish life, culture and history across the world and the impact of race on Jewish tradition.

courses.title: The American Jewish Experience in Film
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A survey of American Jewish history through the medium of film, with particular emphasis on the experience of the post-war generation.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Korean American Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploration of critical issues in U.S. politics through the lens of Korean Americans.

courses.title: Latin I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Essentials of Latin grammar and vocabulary.

courses.title: Latin II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Essentials of Latin grammar and vocabulary, continued. Basic reading skills.

courses.title: Latin III
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Reading Latin literature. Introduction to reading and translation of classical Latin prose and poetry. Extensive grammar review.

courses.title: Ovid and Classical Mythology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Selections from the Metamorphoses and Fasti; collateral reading on classical mythology.

courses.title: Readings in Latin Literature
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Readings in various authors and genres of latin literature.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit. Prerequisite: consent of instructor.

courses.title: Law and the U.S. Constitution in Global History
courses.description: By examining key constitutional moments involving race, rights, and revolutions, students will explore how legal meaning changes over time.

courses.title: Stereotypes, Prejudice and the Rule of Law
courses.description: Examines how stereotypes and prejudice undermine equal justice under the law but also how creative word work and art can promote racial justice.

courses.title: Law and Society
courses.description: Sources and structure of law; history of Bill of Rights emphasizing effect on criminal justice system; limits of law in solving problems in American society.

courses.title: Introduction to Criminal Law
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive analysis of the criminal justice system and an overview of the fundamentals of substantive criminal law.

courses.title: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence: Ethics and Law
courses.description: Analyzes the ethical dilemmas and societal implications of artificial intelligence and debates the future of artificial intelligence regulations and laws.

courses.title: Personal Data in the 21st Century
courses.description: Examine how governments and corporations confront information privacy conflicts. Analyze various perspectives on information privacy laws and their place in society.

courses.title: Fundamentals of the U.S. Legal System
courses.description: Introduces the U.S. legal system and its relationship to basic principles of the rule of law. Examines lawmaking institutions, judicial processes and contemporary legal issues.

courses.title: Intellectual Property and Technology
courses.description: Examines how American law protects and facilitates intellectual property and its modern utility. Provides a practical understanding of laws regulating patents, copyrights and trademarks.

courses.title: Immigration Law for a New America
courses.description: Examines current immigration law in America, the normative debates over immigration policies and the role the government plays in expanding or limiting immigration rights.

courses.title: The Legal Profession
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic aspects of the legal profession.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on the Law
courses.description: Examines law and the legal system from different disciplinary perspectives. It explores how various disciplines provide different insights to the legal regime.

courses.title: Exploring Courthouses in Los Angeles
courses.description: Gain hands-on experience by observing the inner workings of the criminal and civil law system through lectures and courtrooms visits.

courses.title: Current Court Cases
courses.description: Exposes students to the impact of legal decisions on society through analysis of pending and recent cases on the courts docket.

courses.title: Children and the Law
courses.description: Examines topics such as children's suggestibility, decision-making, and risk and resiliency all as they apply to legal settings.

courses.title: Concepts in American Law
courses.description: The main concepts and topics in American law, in the historical, economic and cultural contexts in which they have developed.

courses.title: Voting Rights and the Law
courses.description: Examines the basic themes surrounding the legal regulation of elections with a focus on voting rights.

courses.title: International Influence: Law and Power
courses.description: Examination of the philosophic and political concepts that underpin international influence, while learning how this structure impacts the modern incentives and interests of international actors.

courses.title: Issues in the Use of AI in Law and Regulation
courses.description: Focuses on the role artificial intelligence plays in a variety of aspects of the law through humanities-based approaches like ethics, linguistics, sociological and economics approaches.

courses.title: Love, Sex, Money, and Power: How Law Shapes Families
courses.description: Examines how the law affects lovers, spouses, parents, and children from multiple perspectives, including racial justice, feminism, morality, economics, and legal theory.

courses.title: Global Justice for Mass Atrocities and Genocide
courses.description: Learn about international law and courts trying these cases, while also reflecting on whether criminal trials are the best response to bringing healing and reconciliation to affected societies.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Entertainment Law
courses.description: Examines key legal principles governing the entertainment industry by exploring legal challenges faced by professionals in music, film, sports, gaming and other areas of entertainment.

courses.title: Law, Enslavement and Race
courses.description: Studies how law, politics and culture interacted to shape the institution of enslavement and the development of modern conceptions of race.

courses.title: Sports Law
courses.description: Examines the relevance and application of legal structures to all participants in the sports enterprise by providing an overview of legal and ethical issues.

courses.title: Law and the Modern Athlete
courses.description: Covers legal frameworks that affect today's athletes and students working in sports: amateurism, negotiation, gambling, social media, agents and finding jobs in sports.

courses.title: Law and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Examines areas of the law that impact entrepreneurs, starting, operating and financing businesses. Topics include: selection of business entities; securities laws and issues that arise in fundraising; employment law; contracts; torts; intellectual property; global expansion; mergers and acquisitions; and IPOs.

courses.title: Introduction to Law and Economics
courses.description: An exploration of core aspects of the US legal system (property, contracts, torts, criminal law, civil procedure) from the perspective of basic economics theory.

courses.title: Law and Homelessness
courses.description: Examines the current housing crisis by interweaving tenant/landlord law, local ordinances, historical exclusionary policies and reviewing current reporting and scholarship.

courses.title: Refugee Law and Forced Migration
courses.description: Examines international, regional, and U.S. refugee law, state obligations, implementation challenges, protection gaps, and contemporary displacement issues across the United States, Mexico, Canada, and European Union.

courses.title: American Legal History
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introduction to the study of law from a historical perspective; explores the interaction of law, culture and politics from the Revolution through the New Deal.

courses.title: Cybersecurity and Cybercrime
courses.description: Studies the rise of cybercrimes and cybersecurity measures in recent years and their impact on society. Topics include cyberattacks, digital forensics, information privacy and others.

courses.title: Psychology and Law
courses.description: Explores issues of responsibility and credibility. Intentional and unintentional behavior. Clinical biases. Topics include witness credibility, confessions, cults, hostages, battered persons, and repressed memories.

courses.title: Mental Health Law
courses.description: Foundational legal and practice concepts at the intersection of law and psychology through three intersecting systems: the mental health, the criminal and the immigration systems.

courses.title: Individual Rights in U.S. Constitutional Law
courses.description: Explores the U.S. Bill of Rights and the limits that the Constitution imposes on the state majority's ability to impose its will on an individual.

courses.title: Regulatory Law
courses.description: Introduces legal and social ideas and issues surrounding regulatory law - how and why regulations are developed, along with the accountability and enforcement of regulations.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings.

courses.title: Undergraduate Law Review
courses.description: Introduces students to the basics of legal writing and research, with a focus on legal scholarship and law review-type journal articles.

courses.title: Legal Studies Capstone Project
courses.description: A cumulative experience demonstrating a student's depth of knowledge in applying research and writing skills on examining the legal system.

courses.title: Law Internship
courses.description: Intensive law-related experience with a non-profit organization, public agency, government agency or private company.
courses.recommended_prep: 8 units of LAW courses

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Selected topics of current interest.

courses.title: Overseas Studies
courses.description: Off campus coursework; title of course taken at host institution appears as a section title.

courses.title: Procedure I
courses.description: Consideration of the participants in litigation; private and public plaintiffs, defendants, and courts. Information exchange, process, outcomes, and costs of lawsuits.

courses.title: Contracts
courses.description: The interpretation and enforcement of promises and agreements.

courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.description: The crime problem and the legislative response to it through substantive criminal law; administration of criminal justice through police, prosecutorial, sentencing, and penological discretion.

courses.title: Legal Profession
courses.description: Functions of the lawyer in modern society; history and organization of the legal profession; the adversary system; equal access to justice; other problems of ethics and professional responsibility.

courses.title: Property
courses.description: The idea of property as understood through economic and philosophical concepts. Rights in land, water and other natural resources. Forms of shared ownership (e.g., landlord and tenant), and a survey of mechanisms for controlling land use.

courses.title: Constitutional Law: Structure
courses.description: Considers the delineation of spheres of responsibility between the judiciary and legislature, the nation and the state, and the government and the individual.

courses.title: Torts I
courses.description: Individual's obligation not to harm others; bases for compensating persons who are harmed, either by holding responsible whoever is at fault or by invoking other principles of liability, including the efficiency of resource allocation and the spreading of losses.

courses.title: Legal Research
courses.description: Examination of the basic sources of law for federal and California jurisdictions, utilizing a vast array of sources from books to computer-assisted research and analyzing research methodology and techniques. Graded CR/D/F.

courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.description: Two-semester course focusing on developing analytic and communication skills. Lawyers will analyze legal principles and incisively apply them to facts. Graded CR/D/F.

courses.title: Effective Writing for Professionals
courses.description: Focuses on professional writing structure based on audience, tone, form and purpose.

courses.title: Legal Research, Writing, and Advocacy I
courses.description: Development of legal research, writing, and advocacy skills. Emphasis on objective legal writing, including memoranda, and researching case law through primary and secondary sources. Registration restricted to Law students.

courses.title: Legal Research, Writing, and Advocacy II
courses.description: Continuation of LAW 515. Development of legal research, writing, and advocacy skills. Emphasis on persuasive legal writing, including appellate briefs, and researching statutory and administrative law. Participation in a moot court program. Registration restricted to Law students.

courses.title: Transactional Law Research
courses.description: This course strengthens legal research skills in transactional law, focusing on corporate finance, mergers, tax, and industry reports through hands-on exercises and strategic methodologies.

courses.title: Introduction to U.S. Legal System
courses.description: The basic structure of government in the U.S., including the constitutionally mandated division of power in the federal government and the federal system of power sharing between state and federal systems. A comparative perspective on selected substantive and procedural matters, such as common law reasoning, jury trials, adversary process, and various aspects of civil procedure. Open to incoming LL.M. students only.

courses.title: Topics in American Law
courses.description: This course will provide LL.M. and M.C.L. students with a survey of various topics in American law including criminal law, evidence, family law, constitutional law, torts, wills and trusts, administrative law and property law. Open to LL.M. and M.C.L. students only.

courses.title: Entertainment Law and Industry
courses.description: Provides a detailed survey of entertainment law, entertainment-related transactions and litigation, and legal issues facing the entertainment industry.

courses.title: Mass Torts
courses.description: Examines how courts, lawyers, litigants, and financial institutions, respond when a single course of conduct allegedly injures hundreds, thousands, or millions of people.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Intellectual Property Law
courses.description: Focuses exclusively on issues related to copyright and fair use, trademark, trade secrets and related laws that seek to protect intellectual property.

courses.title: Fundamental Business Principles
courses.description: Exposes students to everyday business and finance vocabulary, concepts and modes of analysis. Strongly recommended for students without significant prior business experience. Graded CR/D/F.

courses.title: Ethical Issues for Nonprofit, Government and Criminal Lawyer
courses.description: Covers legal ethics issues with an emphasis on access to justice, nonprofit practice settings and duties of prosecutors and defense attorneys. Fulfills Legal Profession requirement.

courses.title: Constitutional Law: Rights
courses.description: Examines constitutional rights particularly ones protected under the Equal Protection/Due Process Clauses and related questions of judicial role and theories of interpretation.

courses.title: Law for Business
courses.description: A student-run periodical that publishes student-written and peer-edited articles relevant to the intersection between law and business.

courses.title: Intellectual Property Trademark
courses.description: Explores U.S. trademark law. Topics include trademark infringement and dilution, trademark selection, clearance, enforcement, federal registration and maintenance, the tension between trademark rights and the First Amendment, trademark licensing and other transactions, trademark fair use and the right of publicity.

courses.title: Law and the Fundamentals of AI
courses.description: Provides a robust understanding of artificial intelligence, emphasizing its relevance and applications in the legal domain and delves into the foundational concepts of AI.

courses.title: Legal Issues of AI in Media and Entertainment
courses.description: Addresses evolving issues in using generative AI to produce commercial products and services relating to intellectual property rights such as copyright and trademark.

courses.title: AI Ethics, Privacy and Regulation
courses.description: Explores the ethical, legal and privacy implications involved with using Artificial Intelligence focused on case law, statutes and current and proposed AI regulations.

courses.title: Business of Law: Future of Legal Service Delivery
courses.description: Explores the business of law, legal service delivery as it has traditionally been undertaken and its current transformation, and the primary drivers of change throughout the business of law ecosystem.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence: Law, Policy and Legal Practice
courses.description: Explores how AI is transforming law and legal practice, how law governs AI, and how lawyers can use emerging technologies effectively, ethically, and with sound professional judgment.

courses.title: Rights Theory
courses.description: A philosophical inquiry into the nature, structure, and justification of rights. Legal rights feature prominently, but the perspective throughout is philosophical rather than doctrinal.

courses.title: Human Resource Compliance
courses.description: Provides an overview of human resource related law, and various legal issues involved in the employment relationship.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Skills for U.S. Law Studies I
courses.description: Explores and develops the legal communication and analytical skills necessary to the practice of law.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Legal Writing Skills
courses.description: Explores purpose and form of legal documents and emphasizes effective communication.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Legal Writing Skills
courses.description: Explores purpose and form of legal documents and emphasizes effective communication.

courses.title: Presentation Skills for International Lawyers
courses.description: Explores the art of public speaking and effective communication in legal settings.

courses.title: Persuasive Advocacy
courses.description: Explores the communication and presentation skills necessary for persuasive legal advocacy.

courses.title: U.S. Common Law Analysis and Skills
courses.description: Explores how judicial opinions interact with other sources of law and develop law in the United States.

courses.title: Academic and Professional Skills for U.S. Law Studies II
courses.description: Explores effective legal communication and professionalism skills.

courses.title: Introduction to Litigation in U.S. Courts
courses.description: Provides an overview of the United States legal system for those unfamiliar with common law courts, including the mechanics of the U.S. Court system in both criminal and civil courts, as well as more detailed analysis of torts and intellectual property disputes.

courses.title: Practical Mediation Skills Clinic
courses.description: Students learn basic and advanced mediation skills, practice their skills in simulated mediations, and upon certification by the instructor, mediate in the Los Angeles County courts.

courses.title: Global Regulatory Compliance
courses.description: Introduction to regimes that regulate business practices on a global level and compliance of such regimes, such as Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, OECD Anti-Bribery Convention, and other regulations.

courses.title: Externship for Graduate and International Program Students
courses.description: An externship allows a student to gain hands-on professional experience in legal and business settings. Students will be placed with a legal services provider, business or organization, government agency or state or federal judge under faculty supervision. All externships include an initial orientation and subsequent academic assignments. A maximum of 8 units may be earned over two externships.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

courses.title: Internship for Curricular Practical Training
courses.description: Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the student's field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least one semester of enrollment in the graduate program with a cumulative 3.0 GPA.

courses.title: Environmental Policy and Natural Resources Law
courses.description: Introduces environmental policy and natural resources law, surveying treatment of biodiversity, fisheries, water, protected lands, forests, and the general themes and conflicts of environmental management.

courses.title: Regulatory Compliance
courses.description: Provides an overview of regulatory compliance law and the ways that various organizations ensure compliance with governing laws and regulations.

courses.title: Taxation
courses.description: Federal tax statutes, technical issues and social problems involved in tax planning, tax litigation, and reform of the tax laws.

courses.title: Criminal Procedure
courses.description: Criminal procedure in the courts, and the regulation of lawenforcement by the courts through rules of evidence andinterpretation of the Bill of Rights.

courses.title: Business Organizations
courses.description: Organization of economic activity especially the modern corporation as institutions of social power. The roles of managers, owners, and regulatory agencies in shaping processes ofdecision making.

courses.title: Real Estate Transactions and Finance
courses.description: An in-depth look at the most prevalent transactions and finance tools related to both residential and commercial real estate. Topics include: purchase and sale of realty; property valuation; brokerage agreements; land conveyance and the recording acts; escrows, title insurance and closings; investment vehicles and deal structures; mortgage lending and commercial finance; and foreclosures.

courses.title: Gifts, Wills, and Trusts
courses.description: Gratuitous transfer of wealth, especially the transmission of wealth from one generation to the next as a settlement of family affairs. Comparative analysis of the legal mechanisms of gifts, wills, and trusts. Introduction to problems of fiduciary administration.

courses.title: Evidence
courses.description: The purpose and character of trial. Problems of adversary presentation and the nature of proof. The basis for admission and exclusion of evidence in judicial proceedings.

courses.title: California Civil Procedure
courses.description: Examines the California rules of civil procedure. Emphasizes California law, with some discussion of the differences between state and federal procedure.

courses.title: Corporate Governance
courses.description: Examines the purpose, evolution and history of corporate governance standards, priorities and culture of boards, shareholder/stakeholder engagement, and corporate social responsibility, as it relates to law.

courses.title: Accounting for Lawyers
courses.description: The lawyer's skills needed to understand the financial affairs of a business client.

courses.title: Practicing Commercial Real Estate Transactional Law
courses.description: Provides an in-depth exposure to the practice of commercial real estate transactional law, including an analysis of the differing perspectives of each side of a transaction and a hands-on study of how lawyers negotiate and document various types of commercial real estate transactions.

courses.title: Disability Rights Law and Practical Skills
courses.description: Examines the various federal and California state laws addressing discrimination on the basis of disability from a litigators perspective, emphasizing both substantive law as well as legal practice skills.

courses.title: Free Speech on Campus
courses.description: Examines the basic doctrinal components of Free Speech law necessary to understand and analyze the case studies.

courses.title: Money in Politics
courses.description: Studies the statutes and cases governing campaign finance in America and the latest research into their effects.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.description: Creating, regulating and dissolving family relationships. Explore moral and power relations among men, women, children, and the State. Develop skills to help clients in families.

courses.title: Remedies
courses.description: Comparison of the remedial goals of contracts, torts, and property and the impact of procedural devices in law and equity. Damages, injunctions, specific performance and restitution. Remedial theory and transactional application.

courses.title: International Investment Law and Arbitration
courses.description: Examine the protection offered to foreign investors through international investment agreements, which includes recourse to arbitration against the host states.

courses.title: Real Estate Joint Ventures Between Capital Sources and Devel
courses.description: Explores real estate joint ventures, formed by institutional capital sources and local developers or operators, through review and discussion of hypothetical fact patterns and contract provisions. Various issues attached to real estate transactions are also explored, including topics such as: finance, development, zoning and purchase agreements for commercial property.

courses.title: Mediation Clinic I
courses.description: Students receive the training required to become professional mediators for civil cases in the L.A. County Superior Court, and mediate these cases.

courses.title: Mediation Clinic II
courses.description: Continuation of LAW-630

major_restrictions.groupDescription: Juris Doctor/Master of Arts in Economics

courses.title: Business for Lawyers
courses.description: This course introduces law students to the tools, concept, and language of business. It is premised on the belief that to excel as a business lawyer, one must understand the business world from the perspective of the clients one counsels and assists. The course will cover, in compressed form, the basic subjects from the MBA program which are most useful to lawyers. Open only to law students.

courses.title: Legal Analysis of Evidence
courses.description: Legal analysis of the rules of Evidence using problems designed to improve analytic skills and problem-solving. Taken in conjunction with Evidence.

courses.title: Employment Discrimination Law
courses.description: Examines the regulation of employment discrimination under federal law. Pays primary attention to issues of race, sex, age and disability discrimination.

courses.title: Labor Law
courses.description: The interrelation of labor, business, and government in collective bargaining, federal regulation of union and management practices and pressures, especially through the Taft-Hartley Act.

courses.title: International Trade Policy
courses.description: Examination of the institutions and laws that regulate international economic relations. Students will be introduced to the major international agreements and national laws that regulate international trade goods, services and capital.

courses.title: Trauma-Informed Lawyering
courses.description: An introduction of trauma and trauma-informed practice within the legal field. Learn the skills to represent trauma survivors and address vicarious trauma.

courses.title: Secured Transactions
courses.description: This is a course on Chattel paper and secured transactions involving personal property under Article 9 of the Uniform Commerical Code and some related bodies of law.

courses.title: Social Movement Lawyering Practicum
courses.description: Disassembling structural racism using law, research and community organizing through work with the Coalition for Property Tax Justice.

courses.title: Corporate Taxation
courses.description: Tax principles and practice applicable to business, especially problems of formation, liquidation, and reorganization.

courses.title: Transactional Practice - The Syndicated Loan Agreement
courses.description: Involves issues including loan restructuring; what loan agreements cover; how representations, covenants, default and financial and repayment terms interrelate; and how security documents fit in. Graded CR/D/F.

courses.title: Bankruptcy: Debtors and Creditors I
courses.description: Bankruptcy of the poor, imprudent or unlucky, and of unsuccessful business. The mechanisms of our law for distributing the debtor's property and discharging his obligations.

courses.title: Topics in Entertainment Law
courses.description: Contemporary topics in the field of entertainment law.

courses.title: Entertainment Law
courses.description: An examination of how the courts are handling selected, "cutting edge" topics in entertainment law. The topics will include the scope of and limitations on the right of publicity; fair use and parody defenses to copyright infringement; future technology clauses in rights contracts; and copyright and defamation issues arising in the online world. Previous entertainment law courses recommended, but not required.

courses.title: Computer Crime Law
courses.description: Examines the legal and policy issues involved with the emergence of cyber crimes and cyber security issues, including government access and privacy issues.

courses.title: Music Law in Practice
courses.description: Focus on contract drafting and negotiation issues relevant to an artist's pursuit of a career in the music business.

courses.title: Television and Digital Media
courses.description: An in-depth study of television industry legal concepts, contracts, business structures and economic models.

courses.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
courses.description: Problems of integrating the corporate, securities, tax, business, antitrust, accounting and contractual aspects of corporate mergers and aquisitions.

courses.title: Land use and Development Law
courses.description: A practice-oriented introduction to various elements of land use and real estate development law.

courses.title: National Security Law Seminar
courses.description: Examination of the nature of United States' national security law, focusing on how it is created, violated and enforced.

courses.title: Public International Law

courses.description: History and evolution of archival practice, and the strategies and tools needed for contemporary and future-facing archival management, preservation and digital curation.

courses.title: Justice, Equity and Ethics in Information Organizations
courses.description: History, theory and potential of social justice in library and information organizations, with the goal of implementing services and programs for diverse stakeholders.

courses.title: Transformative Technologies in Library and Information Scien
courses.description: Role of technology in libraries and information organizations, and potential use and ethical considerations of contemporary and emerging technologies to enhance library services.

courses.title: Capstone in Library and Information Management
courses.description: Knowledge and skills gained throughout the MMLIS program are synthesized in a culminating capstone project, and deployed in service of career advancement.

courses.title: Communication Disorders in Our Communities
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to hearing disorders, motor speech disorders, and pragmatic disorders. The impact of these on effective communication. Common methods of diagnosing and intervening.

courses.title: In a Word
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Words as tools for discovering properties of the human mind. How words are formed of and form various units. Experiments exploring judgments about word interpretation.

courses.title: Language and Society
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Discourse patterns among diverse social groups in institutional and interpersonal settings; interrelationships among language practices and gender, socioeconomic status, ethnicity; social structures and cultural values as reflected in language policies and practices.

courses.title: American Sign Language I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Familiarization with ASL and fingerspelling. Covers visual and gestural communication, comprehension through receptive language skills, basic conversational proficiency, general insights into American Deaf culture.

courses.title: Deaf Cultures and Signed Language Communities
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores Deaf culture and signed language communities as linguistic, social, and cultural groups. Topics include history of signed languages, cultural values, education, and technology.

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Empirical study of the sounds and structures of human language;syntax and semantics; language change; linguistic universals.

courses.title: Human Language and Technology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of human linguistic competence and technologies that simulate it. Phonetics, vibration and signal processing, speech recognition, neural networks.

courses.title: Introduction to Phonology and Morphology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A survey of topics in phonology and morphology.

courses.title: Introduction to Syntax
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A survey of topics in syntax.

courses.title: Introduction to Semantics and Pragmatics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to meaning in natural language and the methods from logic applied to its study.

courses.title: Human Language as Computation
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of language as a complex natural system that requires elaborate mental computation.

courses.title: Sociolinguistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Language and society: theory and methods in sociolinguistics; dimensions of language variation including gender, identity, class, age, region; personal-level interactions to national-level language policies.

courses.title: Second Language Acquisition
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories of second language acquisition in children and adults; comparison of first and second language acquisition including psychological, social, and individual factors.

courses.title: Morphology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Formal analysis of linguistic data, familiarization with new theoretical models, abstract reasoning in linguistic theory.

courses.title: Phonetics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Familiarization with the articulation and transcription of speech sounds. Also vocal tract anatomy, acoustics, speech technology, non-English sounds, perception. Includes laboratory exercises.

courses.title: Children's Learning and Cognitive Development
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Principles of learning and cognitive development from infancy through adolescence. Prerequisite 336.

courses.title: Philosophy of Language
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The nature of communication, meaning, reference, truth, necessity, speech acts, convention, and language.

courses.title: Language, Linguistics and Mind
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Topics of current interest at the crossroads of philosophy of language, philosophy of mind and linguistics.

courses.title: Field Methodology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Elicitation techniques and methodological principles; recording and analysis of phonological, syntactic and semantic structures; practical approaches to procedures used in urban and rural settings.

courses.title: Natural Language Processing

courses.title: Speech Synthesis and Recognition
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to speech synthesis and speech recognition technologies from both a phonetics point of view and a computational point of view.

courses.description: Recording and analysis of a living language as employed by a native speaker of that language.

courses.description: Acquisition of grammatical, discourse, and conversational competence; strategies and structures.

courses.title: General Phonetics

courses.description: Familiarization with articulation, transcription, production, and acoustic analysis of the speech sounds found in the world's languages. Also speech technology, perception, and disorders. Includes laboratory exercises.

courses.description: Chemical bonding and structure in crystalline, amorphous and molecular solids; tendency and mechanisms for chemical change; homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria.

courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.description: Basic material science, atomic bonding, crystalline structures, structural and mechanical behavior and characterization of metals, concrete, wood, composites and asphalt.

courses.title: Confectionery Manufacturing Science and Technology
courses.description: Candy production technologies. Chemical and physical mechanisms that affect taste, texture and appearance. Future trends and data science. Problems facing modern candy industries including sustainability.

courses.title: Physical Properties of Polymers
courses.description: Introduction to polymer physical properties and characterization, relationship to synthesis techniques and processing techniques, natural and synthetic materials, property optimization and modern applications.
courses.recommended_prep: CHEM 325aL

courses.description: Introduction to machine learning (ML) for materials applications; basic concepts of machine learning, statistics and probability.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic Python programming and basic calculus

courses.description: Classical thermodynamics, chemical potential, pure phases and mixtures; interphase relationships; binary and ternary solutions; free energy and activity; galvanic cell, electrochemical potential and Pourbaix diagram.

courses.title: Diffusion and Phase Equilibria
courses.description: Phase equilibria, phase diagrams, diffusion, planar defects, nucleation and growth, spinodal decomposition, phase transformation.

courses.title: Crystals and Anisotropy
courses.description: Stereographic projection; Laue back reflection method; crystal orientation; line and planar crystalline defects; tensors; susceptibility; permeability and permittivity; stress and strain; piezoelectricity; elasticity.
courses.recommended_prep: course work in matrix algebra and tensors on the level of AME 509 or AME 525

courses.title: Semiconductor Physics
courses.description: Semiconductor bonds, crystallography, band structure assumptions, group theory, band structure results, k.p. method, quantum wells, wires and dots, superlattices, amorphous, organic semiconductors, defects, statistics, surfaces.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate differential calculus, linear algebra, statistics, programming, Newtonian mechanics, waves, Maxwells equations

courses.title: Micro- and Nano-Fabrication Technology
courses.description: Physical basis of technologies for the fabrication of micro- and nano-scale devices. Thin-film deposition, etching, and material modification processes; pattern transfer methods.
courses.recommended_prep: graduate standing in engineering, physics, or chemistry

courses.title: Machine Learning in Materials, Chemical and Energy Engineeri
courses.description: Introduction to machine learning, basics of python programming and data science tools; hands-on projects of materials and process modeling based on machine learning methods.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic Python programming on the level of TAC 115; Calculus on the level of MATH 229; Linear Algebra on the level of EE 141 or MATH 225/235/245; and Probability on the level of CHE 305.

courses.title: Materials Science for Energy Transitions
courses.description: Survey of materials science issues relevant to a zero-carbon energy future; material properties; the influence of extreme environments; manufacturing considerations; and sourcing of materials.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate introductory materials science course (MASC 310 or equivalent)

courses.title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Quantum mechanics for engineering majors who work with solid-state devices, quantum electronics, and photonics. Schroedinger equation, perturbation theory, electronic and optical processes.
courses.recommended_prep: Experience with linear algebra, Newtonian mechanics, Maxwells equations, and MATLAB

courses.title: Practical Electron Microscopy
courses.description: Theory and practice of advanced materials characterization using scanning and transmission electron microscopy; analytical methods, techniques and practical applications.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with materials science and characterization at the levels of MASC 110L and MASC 534.

courses.title: Introduction to Photovoltaic Solar Energy Conversion
courses.description: The physical principles, implementation materials, devices and manufacturing costs of solar cells and panels for photovoltaic conversion of solar radiation to electricity.
courses.recommended_prep: Undergraduate physics (electricity and magnetism - e.g., PHYS

courses.title: Basics of Atomistic Simulation of Materials
courses.description: Introduction to atomistic modeling and simulations of materials usingMolecular Dynamics and Monte Carlo methods, basic concepts and how tocharacterize materials properties.

courses.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Materials and Processes
courses.description: Modeling of materials and processes such as mechanical, thermodynamical, and transport properties using Molecular Dynamics simulation, interatomic potentials including long-range coulomb interactions and quantum corrections.
courses.recommended_prep: Basics of Molecular Dynamics

courses.description: Review of Algebra. Real numbers, linear equations and inequalities, functions, graphs, systems of equations, exponents, polynomials, factoring, rational expressions, radicals, quadratic equations and solutions. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Contemporary Precalculus
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Equations and inequalities; functions; graphs; polynomial and rational functions; exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric function; analytic geometry.

courses.title: Foundations of Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introduction to the basic tools of statistics. Descriptive statistics; probability; expected value; normal approximation sampling; chance models; tests of significance.

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematics for Business and Economics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Functions, graphs, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, matrices, systems of linear equations.

courses.title: Calculus for Business and Economics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Derivatives and extrema. The definite integral and u-substitutions. Functions of several variables and their extrema; constrained optimization.

courses.title: Calculus I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Limits; continuity, derivatives and applications; antiderivatives; the fundamental theorem of calculus; exponential and logarithmic functions.

courses.title: Calculus II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A continuation of MATH 125: trigonometric functions; applications of integration; techniques of integration; indeterminate forms; infinite series; Taylor series; polar coordinates.

courses.title: Calculus II for Engineers and Scientists
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Trigonometric functions; applications of integration; techniques of integration; indeterminate forms; infinite series; Taylor series; polar coordinates. Engineering and physics applications. Prerequisite: MATH 125. (Duplicates credit in MATH 126 and MATH 127)

courses.title: Elementary Probability and Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Descriptive statistics, probability, discrete and continuous random variables, expectation and variance, sampling, Central Limit Theorem, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. Emphasis on health science. Prerequisite: MATH 118xg or MATH 125.

courses.title: Linear Algebra and Linear Differential Equations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues, systems of linear differential equations.

courses.title: Calculus III
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Vectors, vector valued functions; differential and integral calculus of functions of several variables; Green's theorem, Divergence theorem, Stoke's theorem.

courses.title: Calculus III for Engineers and Scientists
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A continuation of 129; vectors, vector valued functions; differential and integral calculus of functions of several variables; Greens theorem. Engineering and physics applications. Prerequisite: MATH 126, or MATH 127, or MATH 129.(Duplicates credit in MATH 226 and MATH 227)

courses.title: Linear Algebra and Applications
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces, inner products and norms, linear transformations, eigenvalues, singular value decomposition. Applications such as image compression, graphs, networks or linear programming.
courses.recommended_prep: Math 126 or any USC math course beyond Calculus 1

courses.title: Mathematics of Physics and Engineering I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: First-order differential equations; second-order linear differential equations; determinants and matrices; systems of linear differential equations; Laplace transforms.

courses.title: Mathematical Reasoning and Problem Solving
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Preparation for reading and writing proofs with applications from major branches of mathematics, focusing on axiomatic structures and transformations that preserve structure.

courses.title: Statistical Inference and Data Analysis I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Probability, counting, independence, distributions, random variables, simulation, expectation, variance, covariance, transformations, law of large numbers, Central limit theorem, estimation, efficiency, maximum likelihood, Cramer-Rao bound, bootstrap.

courses.title: Statistical Inference and Data Analysis II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, p-values, likelihood ratio, nonparametrics, descriptive statistics, regression, multiple linear regression, experimental design, analysis of variance, categorical data, chi-squared tests, Bayesian statistics.

courses.title: Seminar in Problem Solving
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Systematic approach to solving non-standard and competition level math problems on inequalities, infinite sums and products, combinatorics, number theory and games.
courses.recommended_prep: MATH 126 or MATH 127 or MATH 129

courses.title: Probability Theory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Probability spaces. Main families of discrete and continuous distributions and relations among them. Moments, characteristic functions, sequences of random variables, laws of large numbers, Central Limit Theorem.

courses.title: Mathematical Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Principles for testing hypotheses and estimation, confidence intervals, methods of moments, maximum likelihood, information inequality, likelihood ratio tests, goodness of fit and nonparametric methods.

courses.title: Fundamental Concepts of Modern Algebra
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Sets; relations; groups; homomorphisms; symmetric groups; Abelian groups; Sylow's theorems; introduction to rings and fields.

courses.title: Fundamental Concepts of Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The real number system, metric spaces, limits, continuity, derivatives and integrals, infinite series.

courses.title: Fundamental Concepts of Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Implicit function theorems, Jacobians, transformations, multiple integrals, line integrals.
courses.recommended_prep: one 400-level Mathematics course, excluding MATH 450

courses.title: Theory of Numbers
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the theory of numbers, including prime factorization, congruences, primitive roots, N-th power residues, number theoretic functions and certain diophantine equations.

courses.title: Applied Combinatorics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Mathematical induction, counting principles, arrangements, selections, binomial coefficients, generating functions, recurrence relations, inclusion-exclusion, symmetric groups, graphs, Euler and Hamiltonian circuits, trees, graph algorithms; applications.

courses.title: Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The Euclidean plane and its isometries. Models for the hyperbolic metric, isometries, linear fractional maps, geodesics. Spherical geometry.

courses.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Vectors, elements of vector analysis, applications to curves and surfaces, standard material of differential geometry.

courses.title: Topology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Cardinals, topologies, separation axioms. Compactness, metrizability, function spaces; completeness; Jordan curve theorem.

courses.title: Mathematics of Physics and Engineering II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Vector field theory; theorems of Gauss, Green, and Stokes; Fourier series and integrals; complex variables; linear partial differential equations; series solutions of ordinary differential equations.

courses.title: Data Science with Python
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Python implementations of: data collection, data wrangling, exploratory data analysis, dimensionality reduction, unsupervised / supervised learning, clustering, classification, common predictive statistical / machine learning algorithms, model validation.

courses.title: Mathematics of Machine Learning
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Mathematical aspects of Machine Learning. PAC Learning, VC-dimension and complexity. Linear predictors (regression, perceptron, SVM). Convex learning and gradient descent. Neural networks and backpropagation.

courses.title: History of Mathematics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Evolution of mathematical ideas and techniques as seen through a study of the contributions of eminent mathematicians to the formulation and solution of celebrated problems. Recommended preparation: upper division MATH course.

courses.title: Game Theory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Impartial games, partisan games, zero sum games, von Neumann Minimax Theorem, general sum games, Nash equilibrium, fixed point theorems, evolutionary game theory, signaling, coalitions, auctions, social choice theory.

courses.title: Dynamic Modeling
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Formulation and study of models arising in population dynamics, growth of plankton, pollution in rivers, highway traffic, morphogenesis and tidal dynamics: stability, oscillations, bifurcations, chaos. The lab will consist of computer simulation of models using commercially available software.

courses.title: Theory and Computational Methods for Optimization
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Methods for static, dynamic, unconstrained, constrained optimization. Gradient, conjugate gradient, penalty methods. Lagrange multipliers, least squares, linear, nonlinear dynamic programming. Application to control and estimation.

courses.title: Topics in Linear Algebra
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Polynomial rings, vector spaces, linear transformations, canonical forms, inner product spaces.
courses.recommended_prep: MATH 410

courses.title: Introduction to Theory of Complex Variables
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Complex numbers and functions. Power series, analytic functions, harmonic functions. Complex integration, Cauchy's theorem, Cauchy's formula. Conformal mapping. Applications in physics and engineering.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Graduate Colloquium
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Lectures directed to mathematics graduate students by faculty of the department and by outside speakers. Problem solving workshops. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Theory of Probability
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Construction of probability spaces using measure theory; conditional expectation; properties of expectation; weak and strong laws of large numbers; characteristic functions; weak convergence.

courses.title: Theory of Probability
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: a: Probability spaces; distributions and characteristic functions; laws of large numbers, central limit problems; stable and infinitely divisible laws; conditional distributions. Prerequisite: 525a or 570. b: Dependence, martingales, ergodic theorems, second-order random functions, harmonic analysis, Markov processes.

courses.title: Stochastic Differential Equations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Brownian motion, stochastic integrals, the Ito formula, stochastic differential equations, analysis of diffusion processes, Girsanov transformation, Feynmann-Kac formula, applications.

courses.title: Algebra
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Groups: Sylow theorems, simple, solvable, nilpotent, and linear groups; group extensions, free groups, finitely-generated abelian groups. Fields: Galois correspondence, algebraic extensions, finite fields, cyclotomic fields

courses.title: Algebra
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: B: Commutative Algebra: Integrality, Hilbert Basis theorem, Hilbert Nullstellensatz; Modules: modules over PID's, chain conditions, tensor products; Noncommutative Rings: Jacobson radical, Artin-Wedderburn theorem, Maschke's theorem.

courses.title: Data Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Major parametric and non-parametric statistical tools used in biomedical research, computer packages including SAS. Includes laboratory. Lecture, 2 hours; laboratory, 2 hours.

courses.title: Data Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Statistical methods for analysis of categorical data including dichotomous, ordinal, multinomial and count data, using Stata package. Includes laboratory.

courses.title: Financial Informatics and Simulation (Computer Labs and Prac
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Experimental laboratory trading for financial markets using double auctions: handling statistical packages for data analysis. Practical training in virtual market environments, using financial trading system software.

courses.title: Lie Theory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to complex semisimple Lie algebras including classification via root systems, Cartan and Borel subalgebras, and the classification of representations via dominant weights.

courses.title: Algebraic Geometry
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Geometry of varieties and schemes including sheaf theory, morphisms of schemes, projective schemes, coherent and quasi-coherent sheaves, line bundles, and projective space.
courses.recommended_prep: MATH 535a

courses.title: Complex Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theory of analytic functions--power series and integral representations, calculus of residues, harmonic functions, normal families, approximation theorems, conformal mapping, analytical continuation.

courses.title: Real Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: a: Measure and integration over abstract measure spaces, Radon-Nikodym theorem, Fubini's theorem, convergence theorems, differentiation. Prerequisite: 425ab. b: Metric spaces, contraction principle, category, Banach spaces, Riesz representation theorem, properties of Lp, Hilbert spaces, orthogonal expansions, Fourier series and transforms, convolutions. Prerequisite: 525a.

courses.title: Stochastic Calculus and Mathematical Finance
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Stochastic processes revisited, Brownian motion, Martingale theory, stochastic differential equations, Feynman-Kac formula, binomial models, basic concepts in arbitrage pricing theory, equivalent Martingale measure. Recommended preparation: Math-225, Math-407. Duplicates credit in the former MATH-503.

courses.title: Stochastic Calculus and Mathematical Finance
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Advanced topics in stochastic analysis, asset pricing in continuous time, stochastic control, Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations, incomplete markets, American options, exotic options, term structure of interest rates. Duplicates credit in the former MATH-506.

courses.title: Combinatorial Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Inversion formulas, generating functions and recursions, partitions, Stirling numbers, distinct representatives, Ramsey's theorem, graph theory, block designs, difference sets, finite geometrics, Latin squares, Hadamard matrices.

courses.title: Differential Geometry
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Elementary theory of manifolds, Lie groups, homogeneous spaces, fiber bundles and connections. Riemannian manifolds, curvature and conjugate points, second fundamental form, other topics. Prerequisite: 440.

courses.title: Differential Geometry
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Geometry of manifolds. Connections and curvature. Riemannian manifolds and geodesics. Symplectic manifolds, complex manifolds and Kahler manifolds.

courses.title: Algebraic Topology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Spaces up to homotopy equivalence. CW complexes. Fundamental group and covering spaces. Simplicial and singular homology and cohomology. Homological algebra. Manifolds and Poincare duality.

courses.title: Algebraic Topology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Vector bundles, classifying spaces and characteristic classes. Steenrod operations. Spectral sequences. Homotopy groups and homotopy theory.

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Parametric families of distributions, sufficiency. Estimation: methods of moments, maximum likelihood, unbiased estimation. Comparison of estimators, optimality, information inequality, asymptotic efficiency. EM algorithm, jacknife and bootstrap.

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Hypotheses testing, Neyman-Pearson lemma, generalized likelihood ratio procedures, confidence intervals, consistency, power, jackknife and bootstrap. Monte Carlo Markov chain methods, hidden Markov models.

courses.title: Mathematical Statistics for Data Science
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to mathematical statistics for data science including theory of estimation and inference for parametric statistical models, point estimation, hypothesis testing, algorithms and implementation.

courses.title: Mathematical Foundations of Statistical Learning Theory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Binary classification, empirical risk minimization, support vector machines, voting algorithms and AdaBoost, Vapnik-Chervonenkis combinatorics, concentration-of-measure inequalities, sparse recovery problems, high-dimensional convex geometry.

courses.title: Machine Learning in Quantitive Finance
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Mathematical foundations of machine learning, machine learning algorithms, applications in financial forecasting, derivatives valuation and hedging, portfolio optimization.

courses.title: Foundations of Mathematical Data Science
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introduction to the principles behind and algorithms employed in data science including methods of linear algebra, probability theory and optimization theory; data science applications.

courses.title: Statistical Consulting and Data Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Coverage of modern statistical methods as applied to practical consulting and data analysis, and the use of the R statistical language.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with basic statistics and probability is desirable

courses.title: Mathematical Fluid Dynamics

courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Existence, uniqueness and continuation of solutions, differential inequalities, linear systems, Sturm-Liouville theory, boundary value problems, Poincare-Bendixson theory, periodic solutions, perturbations, stability, fixed point techniques.

courses.description: Hands-on computational biology course drawing on examples from genome biology, systems biology, and bioinformatics. Exercises involve programming, data analysis, and readings from the literature.

courses.description: Introduction to Narrative Medicine and history of health humanities; examine theories of narrative, trauma, witnessing, identity as related to health care and the clinical encounter.

courses.title: Narrative Medicine II: Methods and Pedagogy
courses.description: Advanced study in Narrative Medicine; study current methods and best practices for designing, facilitating and evaluating narrative medicine workshops.

courses.title: Creative Writing and Its Applications in Narrative Medicine
courses.description: Introduction to creative writing in the clinical setting; study of nonfiction/journalism, memoir, fiction and poetry; work toward a creative project that incorporates narrative medicine methods.

courses.title: Research Methods in Narrative Medicine
courses.description: Explore philosophical underpinnings of qualitative research and its use in health research; develop specific methodologies for data collection and assessment in Narrative Medicine.

courses.title: Intersubjectivity: Lived Bodies/Relational Selves
courses.description: Introduction to philosophical, anthropological and sociological considerations of intersubjectivity and experience; narrative approaches to intersubjectivity and relational self-making focusing, especially on clinical encounters.

courses.title: Narrative Ethics: Illness, Disability, Equity and Community
courses.description: Examine the relationship between illness and disability narratives and their familial, social and institutional contexts; develop skills in interviewing, close reading and writing toward publication.

courses.title: Immigrants, Illness and Narrative Medicine
courses.description: Apply narrative medicine methods to the study of fictional and non-fictional illness narratives from the immigrant perspective in the United States.
courses.recommended_prep: MDED 501 or MDED 510

courses.title: Health Justice
courses.description: Use historical and social scientific data and analysis to examine the conjuncture between race and racism in medicine as an institution, clinical practice, body of knowledge and stakeholder in efforts for equitable healthcare practices, policies and professional formation.

courses.title: The Global Middle East

courses.title: The Modern Middle East

courses.title: Politics, Ideologies, Cultures of the Global South

courses.title: Politics of Film and Literature in Modern Iran
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores contemporary Iranian society through the study of social tensions created by poverty-wealth, tradition-modernity, masculinity-femininity, and notions of religio-political authority as reflected in the literature and films of the country.

courses.title: Ancient Empires
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History and cultures of the ancient empires of southwest Asia, from Cyrus the Great to the establishment of Islam.

courses.title: The Arab-Israeli Conflict
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Major developments and issues in Arab-Israeli conflict from late Ottoman period to the present.

courses.title: The International Relations of the Contemporary Middle East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to problems and issues in the Middle East today: religio-ethnic rivalries, conflicting nationalisms and ideologies, the Arab-Israeli conflict, Middle East oil.

courses.description: Study of archaeology and excavated artifacts from Egypt and the Near East.
