courses.title: Skills and Strategies for Future Medical Professionals
courses.description: Development of academic strategies and exploration of pre-professional preparation for careers in medicine and healthcare. Open only to students in the Keck PREP Scholars Program.

courses.title: Healthcare Foundations: Core Concepts and Terminology
courses.description: Introduction to and discussion on clinically relevant topics such as social determinants of health, medical ethics and legal and regulatory aspects, in preparation for experience in the clinical setting.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Innovation and Analytics
schools: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
programs: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
courses.description: Introduction to data innovation and analytics, converting data to knowledge and insights, statistical techniques, analytics models, implementing data analytics through real-world examples and situations.

courses.title: Introduction to Machine Intelligence
schools: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
programs: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
courses.description: Introduction to artificial intelligence and machine learning through programming models, training models with several methodologies, support vector machines, decision trees, ensemble learning and random forests.

courses.title: Introduction to Professionalism and the Practice of Medicine
courses.description: An introduction to professionalism and skills required in the practice of medicine and careers in health care.

courses.title: What Is Primary Care Medicine?
courses.description: An exploration of the practice of primary care medicine which will discuss what primary care is and differences between primary care and specialist care.

courses.title: Introduction to Healthcare Innovation
schools: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
programs: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
courses.description: Introductions to various health innovations, including pathways, technology, techniques and outcomes. A framework for innovation in healthcare and overview of tools for health innovators.

courses.title: Challenges in the Forefront of Biomedical Ethics
courses.description: Examination of fundamental ethical concepts and principles in clinical health care and biomedical research. Use of film, case studies and discussion. Recommended Preparation: MDA-110 or MEDS-220.

courses.title: The Community Impact of Historical Trauma
courses.description: Examines collective experiences of historical trauma in various populations through a macro lens, focusing on promotion of mental health equity in impacted populations.

courses.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences and Trauma
courses.description: Examine the impact of adversity experienced during childhood with social development and neurodevelopment throughout the lifecycle and the bi-directional relationship with society through a trauma lens.

courses.title: Mental Health and Climate Change
courses.description: Explores ways that changing climate affects individual and collective mental health, including concepts related to building individual and collective resilience to environmental threats.

courses.title: Team-Based Care: Roles of Mental Health Professionals
courses.description: Explores evidence-based interdisciplinary team care in healthcare, focusing on roles of mental health professionals on these teams and communication amongst professionals in different disciplines.

courses.title: The Science of Altruism
courses.description: Explores the science behind altruism, volunteerism, compassion and how helping others impacts individuals physically, psychologically and behaviorally through lectures, projects and experiential learning.

courses.title: Human Cadaveric Anatomy
courses.description: Anatomical structure and function of the major regions of the human body as related to health and disease, using clinical cases, lectures and cadaveric demonstrations.

courses.title: The Brain in Health and Disease
courses.description: Neurological diseases are examined through learning the anatomy and physiology of the human brain.

courses.title: Neurochemistry of Addiction: Drugs, Brain, and Behavior
courses.description: The neurochemistry of psychiatric illness and addiction, introduction to brain and nervous system biochemistry, anatomy and disease states. Covers prescribed medications and drugs of abuse.
courses.recommended_prep: BISC 320 or BISC 330 and MEDS 330

courses.title: Skeletal Biology and Pathology
courses.description: Overview of the cellular make-up of the human skeleton, the functions of bones, clinical application of this knowledge towards bone-related diseases, and introduction to technological advances in orthopedic surgery.

courses.title: Bench to Bedside: Application of the Basic Sciences
courses.description: A theoretical basis of laboratory approaches that help the biomedical or physician scientist in understanding the etiology of disease and targeting disease processes.

courses.title: Organ Failure: Non-Communicable Chronic Disease
courses.description: An examination of frequently treated diseases with the greatest impact on society. Involvement of medical specialists as guests.

courses.title: Vertebrate Development and Regeneration
programs: Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine
courses.description: Overview of the biological processes involved in vertebrate development and regeneration, including the cellular interactions and signal transduction pathways guiding organ development and repair.
courses.recommended_prep: cell biology or molecular biology

courses.title: Health Care Systems: A Doctor's Perspective
courses.description: An examination of the health care system of the United States, from the perspective of the physician and other health professions. Particularly covers health care systems as a workplace and how medical professionals fit into and operate within it.
courses.recommended_prep: MEDS 280

courses.title: Medical Examiner-Coroner: Investigating Death
courses.description: Emphasizes the team-based approach used by forensic scientists, medical examiners and coroners to investigate the circumstances and determine the cause/manner of death. Prerequisites: BISC 220 or BISC 221 and MEDS 220. Open only to sophomores, juniors, and seniors.

courses.title: Collaborative Prototyping in Health Innovation
schools: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
programs: Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation
courses.description: Health innovation collaborative capstone project; ideating, prototyping and evaluating a health innovation prototype driven by an industry-based or community-based prompt/project.

courses.title: Introduction to Surgical Principles
courses.description: Introduction to the spectrum of surgical care, taught by surgeons, with the goal of developing an appreciation of the role that surgery plays in society. Prerequisites: BISC 220 or BISC 221 and CHEM 103 or CHEM 105a or CHEM 115a and MEDS 220. Open only to juniors and seniors.

courses.title: Cancer: Biology, Research, Prevention and Therapy
courses.description: The basic aspects of cancer biology, prevention, diagnosis and therapy, as well as guest lectures by oncology researchers and health professionals.

courses.title: OB/GYN: The Medicine and Surgery of Reproduction
courses.description: An introduction to the practical realities of modern obstetric and gynecology practice from the point of view of practicing surgeon scientists at USC. Prerequisites: BISC-220 or BISC-221 and MEDS-220.

courses.title: Directed Research in Biomedical Science
courses.description: Individual research and readings.
courses.recommended_prep: MEDS 300, MEDS 360.

courses.title: Social Emergency Medicine: Practicum with the CHLA CHAT Team
courses.description: Explores the social determinants of health through supervised on-site practicum with the Community Health Advocates Team at Childrens Hospital Los Angeles and didactic sessions.

courses.title: Basic Concepts in Global Health
courses.description: Exploration of global health issues facing resource-poor societies; emphasizes contributing factors including behavioral and physiological bases, economic, social, and political context.

courses.title: Core Principles System I
courses.description: Introduction to basic medical concepts and biological system functions; examination of core principles of science and medical treatment.

courses.title: Core Principles System II
courses.description: Continuation of concepts from MEDS 503L: basic medical concepts and biological system functions; examination of core principles of science and medical treatment.

courses.title: Global Health Modules, Malaria
courses.description: Critical issues in international control and treatment of malaria. Exploration of biological and epidemiological fundamentals of human-parasite interaction including dynamics of transmission among populations.

courses.title: Global Health Modules, Tuberculosis
courses.description: Exploration of biological and epidemiological fundamentals of tuberculosis including dynamics of transmission among populations. Overview of clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment of infections.

courses.title: Global Health Modules, Tropical Disease
courses.description: Examination of prevalent tropical diseases: epidemiology, clinical manifestations, treatment, impact on economies of tropical countries. Key issues related to these diseases; World Health Organization responses.

courses.title: Cultural Humility in Health and Medicine
courses.description: Practical approach to the development of professional skills for providing culturally sensitive clinical health services to ethnically and linguistically diverse patients.

courses.title: Global Oral Health
courses.description: Better understand the key issues impacting global oral health, how better care can help reduce the disease prevalence, and ways to prepare the next generation of global health leaders to address the key issues. Open only to Global Medicine majors.

courses.title: Medical Spanish for the Health Professions
courses.description: Spanish language course for students planning to enter the health professions. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Emerging and Re-emerging Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Exploration of the threat of major worldwide epidemics and diseases with a focus on the recent emergence of new plagues.

courses.title: Zoonotic Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Background information on a group of infections that are transmitted via animal contact. Understanding of the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, treatment, and impact of the diseases on the economies of the countries in which they are found. Recommended preparation: MEDS 500. Open only to graduate students.

courses.title: Global Health Modules, Sexually Transmitted Infections
courses.description: Examines clinically relevant perspectives from distinguished international authors on STI issues and the devastating effect on particular geographical regions around the world.

courses.title: Foundation of Medicine: Anatomy, Physiology, and Pathology
courses.description: Fundamentals of physiology, chemistry, anatomy, biochemistry and microbiology, as well as pharmacological issues, mathematical basis of lab instruments or techniques, and computational modeling

courses.title: Foundation of Medicine: Anatomy, Physiology, and Pathology
courses.description: The basics of human anatomy (gross anatomy, histology, radiographic anatomy), physiology (cellular physiology, organ system areas) and pathology (general, systemic, cellular pathology).

courses.title: Non-communicable Diseases
courses.description: A conceptual framework for understanding global challenges faced in the management of non-communicable diseases, including heart disease, diabetes, chronic lung disease, and cancer.

courses.title: Clinical Medicine and Healthcare Delivery in Panama
courses.description: A two-week course providing students with hands-on experience in the practice of rural medicine as they gain exposure to the various socio-economic factors present in Bocas del Toro, Panama. Recommended preparation: MEDS 500, MEDS 501, MEDS 510, MEDS 511, MEDS 514, MEDS 515. Open only to Global Medicine majors.

courses.title: Global Nutrition
courses.description: A systematic survey of basic and clinical nutrition that provides an overview of critical public health-nutrition issues in both the developing world and industrial society.

courses.title: Maternal and Child Health in South Africa
courses.description: Examination of country-specific factors affecting pregnancy, pre-natal care, and childbirth in South Africa, with analysis of factors contributing to health inequality and methods to mitigate healthcare challenges.

courses.title: Global Palliative Care
courses.description: Exploration of the provision of palliative care and analysis of factors affecting the increased burden of palliative care provision facing developing regions of the world.

courses.title: Interprofessional Team Dynamics in Healthcare
courses.description: Examination of typical composition and function of interprofessional healthcare teams. Exploration of roles of team members and purview of care issues and common challenges, including medication management, inpatient/outpatient decision making, and care plan implementation.

courses.title: Case Studies in Interprofessional Healthcare
courses.description: Survey of the specific roles each member of an interprofessional health team plays in the provision of care, based on their professional training. Application of diverse health professional expertise to case studies in healthcare.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunology
courses.description: Provides an in-depth examination of topics in molecular and cellular immunology through lectures, discussions, data analysis and oral/written student presentations.

courses.title: Molecular Biology of Cancer

courses.title: Foundations in Health Education and Promotion
courses.description: Overview and application of behavioral theories to the field of health education and promotion. Examines the determinants of health behavior and strategies for change at the individual, group and community level.

courses.title: Foundations of Public Health
courses.description: Overview of public health concepts and issues, including population health; ethics; health disparities, determinants, and systems of care; global health; policy; health promotion; environmental health.

courses.title: Practice of Public Health
courses.description: Introduction to the application of strategies and tools for practice in public health, including policy advocacy, leadership and management, program planning and evaluation, health communication.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 502

courses.title: Quality in Health Care
courses.description: Examines quality assessment at different levels of the health care system including health plans, physicians, hospital and integrated system performance.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 502 or PM 508

courses.title: Overcoming Real World Challenges in Global Health
courses.description: Overview of program implementation challenges in global health contexts, including best practices for establishing effective cross-cultural collaborations, working with key leaders, and operationalizing complex interventions.

courses.title: Public Health Services Research Methods
courses.description: A practical examination of methods and data sources used to evaluate public health services and conduct policy research and evaluation within health care delivery systems.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 508

courses.title: Health Service Delivery in the U.S.
courses.description: Historical development of the American health care system; determinants of health care utilization; role of health care providers; health policy; public health services; and health care finance.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 502

courses.title: Principles of Biostatistics
courses.description: Concepts of biostatistics; appropriate uses and common misuses of health statistics; practice in the application of statistical procedures; introduction to statistical software including EXCEL, SPSS, nQuery. Laboratory.

courses.title: Data Analysis
courses.description: Methods and applications for modeling longitudinal, time-to-event and multi- level data. Includes laboratory using R package. Lecture 2 hrs; laboratory 2 hrs. Prerequisites: PM-511b.

courses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
courses.description: Terminology/uses of epidemiology and demography; sources/uses of population data; types of epidemiologic studies; risk assessment; common sources of bias in population studies; principles of screening. Recommended preparation: algebra

courses.title: Experimental Designs
courses.description: Statistical methods for analysis of various experimental designs. Parametric analysis of variance (ANOVA), repeated measures methods, crossover designs, non-parametric ANOVA.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 511a

courses.title: Multivariate Statistics in Health Behavior Research
courses.description: Advanced training in multivariate statistical techniques involving general linear modeling, mixed modeling and basic latent variables analysis in health behavior research

courses.title: Biostatistical Consulting
courses.description: An overview of the tools used by statisticians for solving statistical problems. Introduces students to the field of biostatistical consulting.

courses.title: Biostatistical Consulting
courses.description: Reinforce concepts in biostatistical consulting and will expose students to the practice of biostatistical consulting

courses.title: Research Methods in Epidemiology
courses.description: Study design, ascertainment of study objects, questionnaire development, various methodological issues in study design and interpretation including bias, measurement error, confounding and effect modification.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 518a Statistical Methods for Epidemiological Studies I, II

courses.title: Research Methods in Epidemiology
courses.description: Overview of epidemiologic research in cancer. Selected cancer sites will be covered to highlight study design and conduct, exposure assessment, data analysis and interpretation.

courses.title: Statistical Methods for Epidemiological Studies I, II
courses.description: Principles and methods used in epidemiology for comparing disease frequencies between groups. Restricted to the analysis of binary outcome variables.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 512

courses.title: Moving Toward Health Equity in the United States
courses.description: A thoughtful perspective on U.S. health services delivery while introducing students to social inequalities in health.

courses.title: Advanced Statistical Computing
courses.description: Techniques for the solution of statistical problems throughout intensive computing; iterative techniques, randomization tests, the bootstrap, Monte Carlo methods. Lecture and required laboratory.

courses.title: Pre-Departure Training to Optimize Global Health Experiences
courses.description: A comprehensive pre-departure training course intended to enhance the learning experience for all KSOM learners participating in global health (STEGHs).

courses.title: Introduction to the Theory of Statistics
courses.description: a: Density distribution and hazard functions; normal, chi-square, student's t and F distributions; and sampling procedures for single factor and multiple factor designs, distributions. Recommended preparation: working knowledge of multivariable calculus and familiarity with linear algebra.

courses.title: Introduction to the Theory of Statistics
courses.description: b: Theory of estimation and testing, inference, analysis of variance, theory of regression. Recommended Preparation: college-level calculus and linear algebra.

courses.title: Design of Clinical Studies
courses.description: Design, conduct, and interpretation of results of clinical trials; emphasis on principles affecting structure, size, duration of a trial, and the impact of ethical and practical considerations.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 511a

courses.title: Culture and Health: Global Perspectives
courses.description: International variations in health status with a focus on the impact of socioeconomic status, politics, environment, education and gender in etiology of illness, access to health care, progression of disease, and recovery.

courses.title: Communications in Public Health
courses.description: Application of communication theories and methods to community health problems. Includes background assessment, program design, evaluation, social marketing, media advocacy, review of major health campaigns.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 501

courses.title: Epidemiology of Infectious Disease
courses.description: Survey of natural history of infectious disease, methods of disease control and outbreak investigation, and an overview of the epidemiology of injury. Prerequisite: PM-512.

courses.title: Program Design and Evaluation

courses.recommended_prep: PM 501

courses.title: Environmental Health: An Epidemiological Approach
courses.description: An overview of environmental health, identifying issues in assessing effects of exposure on health and potential interventions for reducing adverse health risks. Prerequisite: PM-512

courses.title: Genetic and Molecular Epidemiology
courses.description: Genetic principles; design and analysis of family studies; introduction to likelihood estimation; segregation and linkage analysis; biomarkers of exposure, susceptibility, and disease; laboratory methods; susceptibility genes; association and linkage disequilibrium.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 510, PM 511b, PM 512, PM 518a, BIOC 543

courses.title: Program Evaluation and Research
courses.description: Overview of concepts, tools, data collection, analysis methods and designs used to evaluate health promotion programs. Examples from substance abuse prevention, family planning and reproductive health programs.

courses.title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: Overview of causative factors and demographic distribution of major chronic diseases in the western world. Epidemiologic concepts, methods and research design as applied to chronic disease prevention will be emphasized. Prerequisite: PM 512.

courses.title: Social Network Analysis
courses.description: Theory, methods and procedures of network analysis with emphasis on applications to public health programs.

courses.title: Introduction to Time Series
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Transfer function models; stationary, nonstationary processes; moving average, autoregressive models; spectral analysis; estimation of mean, autocorrelation, spectrum; seasonal time series.
courses.recommended_prep: Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, statistics

courses.title: Public Health Policy and Politics
courses.description: Examination of major policy issues in the U.S. health care delivery system to understand policy options in reforming health care and reducing health care disparities.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 502 or PM 508

courses.title: Statistical Methods in Genome-Wide Association Studies
courses.description: Provides epidemiologists with an overview of current statistical problems and approaches in the design and analysis of genome-wide association studies. Prerequisites: PM 511a, PM 512. Co-requisite: PM-522a.

courses.title: Statistical Methods in Clinical Trials
courses.description: Stochastic failure process; parametric models for survival data; sample size estimation procedures for clinical trials; multivariate regression models for binary outcome and censored survival data; computer programs; multiple failure modes and competing risks.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 518a, MATH 408

courses.title: Environmental Epidemiology: Concepts, Methods, and Practice
courses.description: Examine epidemiologic methods, concepts, and statistical approaches; case-study seminars with structured critiques of current literature on human-environment interactions affecting public health. Recommended Preparation: PM-510 and PM-512.

courses.title: Cancer Epidemiology
courses.description: Explores the fundamental concepts of cancer epidemiology, including the molecular basis, descriptive epidemiology, and historical and groundbreaking studies that have impacted the field.
courses.recommended_prep: PM 512 or equivalent

courses.title: Statistical Programming With R
courses.description: The contents include: R objects, control structure, data input and output, subsetting objects, data manipulation and aggregations, character manipulation, graphics, and writing user-defined functions. Recommended preparation: Knowledge of one programming language other than R or a half-year experience programming in R.

courses.title: Intervention Approaches for Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
courses.description: Approaches for modifying health behavior in varioius settings and within diverse populations. Emphasis on practical considerations necessary to design and implement interventions with demonstrated effectiveness.

courses.title: Organizing and Mobilizing Communities for Public Health
courses.description: Survey of effective community organizing and mobilization efforts in the U.S. and abroad, using participatory, organizational, community empowerment and public-private partnership models.

courses.title: Public Health Leadership and Management
courses.description: Introduction to leadership and management concepts, tools, and practices in the context of domestic and global public health and healthcare delivery settings.

courses.title: Introduction to Global Health

courses.title: Introduction to Health Data Science
courses.description: An introduction to the toolsets needed to create workable and reproducible datasets, conduct exploratory analysis and visualizations, learn from data, summarize and communicate analytic results.

courses.title: Public Health Disaster Management and Response
courses.description: Definition and chronology of natural and man-made disasters and their effects on the global community. Structure and organization of disaster management systems and the role of humanitarian organizations.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Public Health
courses.description: Ethical principles in the distribution of health resources, conduct of global public health research, and implementation of public health initiatives across different nations, cultures, religions.

courses.title: Global Health Research and Programs

courses.recommended_prep: MPH core course work

courses.description: Introduction to reproductive health, from preconception to the neonatal and early period of human development. Heavy emphasis on the methods and public health implications.

courses.description: Provides students with hands on experience of the common methods used in conducting epidemiological studies, and designing and obtaining funding for research projects. Prerequisite: PM-512. Recommended preparation: PM 527.

courses.description: Principles of cost-benefit analysis and medical cost-effectiveness analysis with applications in medical care and the pharmaceutical field.

courses.title: Health Economics Il
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Second of part series in techniques of microeconometric analysis to inform health policy. Topics include: patents and innovation, pharmaceutical regulation, hospital competition, physician practice. Recommended Preparation: ECON-601, ECON-611 and ECON-636.

courses.title: Programming Methods for Empirical Analysis of Health Data
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to methods for analysis of large health data sets, including data selection, SAS/Stata programming under Linux, and review of claims and survey data.

courses.title: Introduction to Health Econometrics
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to statistical analysis and regression modeling for health economics and policy research. Topics include: statistical inference, principles of probability and statistics, regression models, and causal inference.

courses.title: Advanced Health Econometrics I
schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: The expansion of students' knowledge of econometric methods emphasizing, but not limited to, applications to health economics. Serves as a prelude to the advanced study of microeconomics.

courses.description: Covers the transition to independent producers of high-quality empirical research on health and health care. Peer-reviewed research will serve as case studies for class discussion and may address empirical methods.

schools: Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
courses.description: Current research in pharmaceutical economics and policy presented by outside scholars, faculty and students. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Migration and Diaspora in International Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines issues of migration, the relationship between citizen and state, economic factors triggering emigration/immigration, transnationalism, and explores the phenomenon of diasporas. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: East Asian Security Issues
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Security politics of China, Japan, ASEAN states, and Southwest Pacific nations; their strategic relations with the superpowers; regional security initiatives: nuclear-free zone politics, ZOPFAN, and indigenous military capacities. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: Conflict Processes
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Seminar in international conflict, crisis and war. General perspectives on factors that bring about war or peace. Focus on ethnopolitics and conflict processes. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: Democracy and Democratization in Comparative Perspective
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Seminar generates and tests theories of democratization. Readings will focus on Europe, Latin America, Soviet Eurasia emphasizing core theoretical and methodological aspects. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: Feminist Theory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: History of feminist theory and major perspectives of current feminist theory: liberal feminism, socialist/Marxist feminism, radical feminism, psychological feminism, spiritual feminism, and ecological feminism.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Practicum in Teaching Politics and International Relations
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Practical principles for the long-term development of effective teaching within political science and international relations disciplines. Intended for teaching assistants in Dornsife College. Graded CR/NC. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Internship for Curricular Practical Training
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Part-time or full-time practical work experience in the student's field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least one semester of enrollment in the graduate program.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Subjects in one or more fields in Political Science.

courses.title: Research Design
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The course will cover the design of experimental and observational research. We will examine both quantitative and qualitative approaches to social science research. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Introduction to Regression Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The course will introduce students to regression analysis and its application to social science research. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Qualitative Research Design
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Design multiple research approaches using qualitative evidence to evaluate the observable implications of theory. Learn deductive, construct, internal, external, and conclusion validity.

courses.title: Topics in Quantitative Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduces statistical models beyond the standard linear regression model. Topics include maximum likelihood estimation, generalized linear models and advanced methods.

courses.title: Experimental Political Science
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to experimental techniques and applications of experiments in political science. Addresses both the advantages and disadvantages of experiments in political science research. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Formal Models of Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduces basics of game theory and surveys foundational models of American, comparative, and international politics.
courses.recommended_prep: POIR 610 and POIR 611

courses.title: Advanced Quantitative Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Bayesian inference in the social sciences and causal inference literature, including experiments, matching, difference-in-difference and regression discontinuity.

courses.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Maximum likelihood estimation of binary choice models, duration models, count models, and other models in political science, international relations, and social sciences. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: American Politics and Policy Processes
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of literature; examination of approaches, concepts, and issues in the field of American politics and policy processes. Duplicates credit in former POSC 510. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Political Attitudes and Behavior
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Determinants, nature, and consequences of political attitudes and behavior exploring psychological-sociological models, political socialization and learning, and factors affecting trends in attitudes and behavior. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: Political Parties
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Parties and organizations in the political system; formal and informal organization and roles; party systems; partisanship; and electoral rules. MA and other students outside of POIR must obtain faculty permission to register for the course.

courses.title: Race and Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of how racial and ethnic diversity shapes democratic governance, identity, and belonging through critical social-scientific, theoretical, and methodological inquiry.

courses.title: Comparative Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of literature; examination of approaches, concepts, and issues in the field of comparative politics. Duplicates credit in former POSC 520. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Comparative Politics II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Seminar covering literature and methods in the study of political economy, authoritarianism, redistribution, and political conflict.
courses.recommended_prep: POIR 640

courses.title: Political Economy of Development
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Development of global state of affairs including foundations of political order and economic growth, formation of states in global perspective, survival of non-democracies and adopting inclusive institutions.

courses.title: International Political Economy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of approaches to international political economy. Intellectual roots; the management of collective goods; North-South relations are examined. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.title: Political Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Integrates findings of psychology into the study of international relations and political science. Covers foreign policy decision-making, public opinion, ideology, emotion and common heuristics and biases among other topics.

courses.title: International Security and Foreign Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the interconnected fields of international security and foreign policy, including decision making and patterns of interaction regarding international conflict. Open only to doctoral students.

courses.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.description: For students with no proficiency in Portuguese. Practice in listening comprehension, oral communication, elementary reading and writing.

courses.title: Portuguese II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: For students with some language proficiency in Portuguese; increased emphasis on listening, comprehension, oral communication, reading, and writing. Students will be required to take a Portuguese placement exam in the Spanish and Portuguese Department. Prerequisite: PORT 120.

courses.title: Accelerated Portuguese I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Encourages rapid acquisition through intensive exposure to Portuguese while following a proficiency-oriented approach. Recommended for students with a background in Spanish or another Romance language.

courses.title: Portuguese III
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive work in listening comprehension, oral communication, reading and writing, with emphasis on free expression; readings related to Portuguese culture and civilization.

courses.title: Portuguese IV
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Four-skills course with review of grammar. Writing and reading intensive. Authentic materials related to Lusobrazilian culture and civilization.

courses.title: Visions of Brazil
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Comparative study of Brazil in the context of the Lusophone (Portuguese-speaking) world, especially Portugal's former colonies in Africa. Materials drawn from literature, visual culture, music and cultural theory.

courses.title: Theory and Practice of American Democracy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theoretical, institutional, and functional aspects of American national, state, and local government and politics; contemporary issues. Recommended for freshmen and sophomores.

courses.title: Ideology and Political Conflict
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Modern political ideologies; their assumptions, perceptions, and prescriptions regarding political stability and social injustice:anarchism, communism, socialism, liberalism, conservatism, and fascism.

courses.title: Comparative Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Gateway to the major in political science. Comparative analysis of political institutions and processes in selected industrial, developing and socialist countries, in terms of contrasting ideologies, parties, elites, and economies.

courses.title: Law, Politics and Public Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Interaction between law and politics; overview of the American legal system; value conflicts and public policy questions which arise within it.

courses.title: Law and Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the rules and realities of American politics, and the role politics plays in American life and culture.

courses.title: Social Analysis of Gender
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Multidisciplinary survey of gender assumptions in relation to sexuality, mental health, social and political relations, and artistic expression.

courses.title: Human Rights
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of human rights controversies across the globe. Introduction to techniques of analysis for social issues, interdisciplinary research methods, and interpretation of complex political problems.

courses.title: Environmental Challenges
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the challenges of environmental problem-solving at the personal, local, national and global scales, focused on the issue of climate change.

courses.title: Political Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Methodological and theoretical problems of micro-analytic studies in political science. Techniques of data collection and assimilation.

courses.title: Social Construction of Race and Citizenship
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Comparative perspective on the social construction of race and citizenship. Social, economic and political experiences of selected groups in the U.S. are examined.

courses.title: Applied Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to become active in politics based on understanding the history, theory, and practices of public participation.

courses.title: State Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: American state politics from a comparative perspective. Examines political processes, differing policy outcomes and the impact of social change on system performance.

courses.title: Case Studies in Modern Leadership
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of a single leader or small set of leaders, including the strengths and weaknesses that distinguish them and the cultural forces that nurture them.

courses.title: Interest Groups and Elite Behavior
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to interest group and elite views of the American system, including recent interest group theory and findings and the general critiques of power distribution in American society.

courses.title: Political Parties, Campaigns, and Elections
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Organization and function of political parties, nominations and elections, strategy and tactics of campaigning, professional candidate management finance, political machines, voting behavior.

courses.title: Constitutional Law
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Development of constitutional law by the courts; leading cases bearing on major constitutional issues; the federal system; powers of government; civil liberties.

courses.title: International Law
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Nature, origin, and development of international law; basic principles analyzed and illustrated with cases.

courses.title: Politics of Latin America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories of development and nation-building; revolutionary and evolutionary modernization; role of history, culture, socioeconomic conditions in affecting political structures and functions.

courses.title: Middle East Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Political development in the Middle East, emphasizing historical, cultural, and socioeconomic conditions affecting political structures and functions; modernization and countervailing social, economic and religious forces.

courses.title: Politics in the People's Republic of China
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The Chinese revolution; social, political, and economic developments in post-1949 China; China after Mao Zedong (Mao Tse-tung).

courses.title: Politics of Sub-Sahara Africa
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories of development and nation-building; revolutionary and evolutionary modernization; role of history, culture, socioeconomic conditions in affecting political structures and functions.

courses.title: The Politics of Food
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Use food as a lens to analyze the social and political world.

courses.title: Comparative Political Institutions
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Institutions and processes of advanced industrial societies; political culture, interest articulation and aggregation, the governmental process.

courses.title: Cities and Regions in World Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Cities and the rise of states; globalization and localization; federalism and decentralization; comparative politics of urban regions in developed and developing countries. Recommended preparation: comparative or urban politics.

courses.title: European Political Thought I
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Basic concepts of Western political thought from Plato through the contract theorists.

courses.title: European Political Thought II
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Western political thought since the French Revolution. Rise of Marxist socialism, communism, anarchism, fascism, National Socialism, other doctrines; the democratic tradition; new theories of the state.

courses.title: Political Theories and Social Reform
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Political theories and philosophies in modern times and their relation to public policy and social reform.

courses.title: Honors I: Undergraduate Seminar
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Selected topics in designated area of political science. Discussion of readings and presentation of papers.

courses.title: California Policy Research Internship
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Conducting extensive research and analysis on a major public policy challenge facing California.

courses.title: Field Research in Human Rights
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Conducting human rights research and policy work in the field

courses.title: Trial Advocacy: Theory and Practice
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Course covering substantive law, evidence, public speaking and use of societal mores in courtroom advocacy. Open only to Mock Trial team members.

courses.title: Ethnic Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of the political behavior and roles of ethnic and racial groups in the American political system; policy issues and patterns of political action are examined.

courses.title: Political Economy of Mexico
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of contemporary Mexico: the role of the state in the Mexican economy; development of the government party and opposition groups.

courses.title: Politics of Local Criminal Justice
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Roles and behavior of major legal and political participants in the criminal justice system including the police, the legal profession, judges, and the public.

courses.title: Politics and the Economy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Major techniques, politics, and values involved in the allocation of social and economic resources. Includes such topics as determination of priorities in budgetary processes, economic regulation, control of environmental change, and policies for science.

courses.title: Mass Media and Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of political content of mass media. Audience response to alternative sources of political information. Consideration of the institutional and economic as well as political aspects of the mass media.

courses.title: How Washington Really Works
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Provides students with a DC insider's understanding of American politics, campaigning and elections.

courses.title: Critical Issues in American Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive examination of critical issues of particular interest in the field of American politics.

courses.title: The Politics of Human Differences: Diversity and Discriminat
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A comparative perspective on social and cultural forces that affect American laws and policies concerning discrimination on the basis of race or ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, and disability.

courses.title: Law in Film
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Analysis of the depiction of law in film; use of film to explore topics in jurisprudence and the politics of law and courts. Recommended preparation: POSC 130

courses.title: Civil and Political Rights and Liberties
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An examination of debates and controversies surrounding the nature and scope of civil rights and civil liberties.
courses.recommended_prep: POSC 340 or POSC 440

courses.title: Global Justice: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Classical and contemporary theories of justice, from an interdisciplinary perspective.

courses.title: Political Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Psychological forces shaping politics and persons, processes and interactions; emphasis on political socialization and cognitive and effective orientations to politics.

courses.title: Critical Issues in Law and Public Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive examination of special topics in the field of law and public policy.

courses.title: Critical Issues in Comparative Politics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive examination of critical issues of particular interest in the field of comparative politics.

courses.title: Critical Issues in Political Thought
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Intensive examination of critical issues of particular interest in the field of political thought.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Economic Analysis for Public Policy
courses.description: Economic foundations for public policy analysis; concepts of efficiency and equity, analysis of market failure and policy interventions; challenges in policy-making.

courses.title: Solving Public Problems
courses.description: Develops a framework for understanding public policy and its role in solving current complex issues. Theories, processes and institutions that shape policymaking and professional development for policymaking. Course sections may vary in policy subject emphasis.

courses.title: Planning for the Future City
courses.description: Gateway to BS, Public Policy, Management and Planning and minor in Planning and Development. City building and development process; who plans, politics of planning and development; major topics include land use, fiscal policy, transportation, sustainability, and economic development.

courses.title: Citizenship and Public Ethics
courses.description: Review of legal and ethical traditions of citizenship withemphasis on the latter; consideration of implications for currentpractice of public policy-making and management.

courses.title: The Urban Context
courses.description: The urban context for planning and policy decisions. Socioeconomic, physical and spatial structure of cities; and the underlying demographic, economic and social processes that drive their ongoing transformation.

courses.title: Social Justice Issues in Public Policy and Urban Planning
courses.description: Social justice issues through the lens of public policy and urban planning with main focus on Los Angeles; critical thinking skills about the fields and their relevance to social justice.

courses.title: PPD Practices: Internship Seminar
courses.description: Policy, planning, and development skills for practice; internship seminar; leadership, group dynamics and presentation skills; application of management; organizational diversity; reflection on experiences.

courses.title: Statistics for Policy, Planning, and Development
courses.description: Statistical applications applied to the real world; techniques including probability, sampling; hypothesis formation and testing; correlation, and linear regression.

courses.title: Finance of the Public Sector
courses.description: Justifications for and effects of government policies; tax and spending sides of government budgets; public goods; externalities; social insurance; redistribution and welfare; tax policy.

courses.title: Public Policy and Law
courses.description: Institutional foundations and analysis of public policy issues; policy formulation and implementation; application of theories; case analyses.

courses.title: Analytic Foundations for Public Policy
courses.description: Qualitative methods of analysis; ethical and political implications of policy choices; issue diagnosis and policy design skills; critical reasoning and ethics; policy leadership.

courses.title: Behavioral Insights for Policy Makers
courses.description: Climate change, public health, and other societal issues require behavior change. Learn how to design communications and behavior-change interventions, and how to evaluate their effectiveness.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Learning the institutions of health care delivery and financing; evaluating key health policy issues; understanding and using economic, statistical and mathematical tools as ways to inform health policy issues.

courses.title: Introduction to Health Care Systems
courses.description: Concepts and determinants of health and illness; health care delivery organizations and programs; the role of the administrator; issues in health care financing and access; quality evaluation; future trends.

courses.title: Crime and Public Policy
courses.description: Public policy agenda-setting, alternatives formulation, and implementation for crime and criminal justice; analysis of specific issues including crime control, death penalty, and gun control.

courses.title: AI and Urban Planning
courses.description: Exploration of the core concepts and use of AI in urban planning; developments in the field; urban applications; assessment of AI's ethics, equity and impact

courses.title: Philanthropy and Social Change
courses.description: History, theories, philosophies, and practices of philanthropy; relationship between philanthropy and nonprofit world; grant-making procedures and relation to social innovation.

courses.title: Government and Business
courses.description: Interrelated roles of business and public institutions; effects of public policies and laws on business sector; incorporates public and business perspectives.

courses.title: Urban Transportation Planning and Policy
courses.description: Current transportation planning and policy critiques. Transportation planning: the relationship to urban structure; conventional and para-transit modes; analysis of local plans.

courses.title: Sustainable Communities, Policy and Planning
courses.description: Policy and planning as shaped by sustainability theories; sustainability indicators; topics include water resources, air quality, land use regulations, environmental design, carrying capacity, ecological footprint analysis. Duplicates credit in former PPD 461.

courses.title: Mapping Urban Data for Social Change
courses.description: Examines the power of maps to catalyze action for social change or disenfranchise populations and operationalize racism. Experiments with GIS and Adobe for critical cartography.

courses.title: The Nonprofit Sector and the Public Interest
courses.description: Theories of the voluntary nonprofit sector in society and its relationship to government and business; public policies toward the sector.

courses.title: Public Policy and Planning Analysis
courses.description: Applied analytic modeling and data manipulation; visual presentation; interpretation of data; needs assessment and market failure analysis; indexing; extrapolation and simple forecasting; simple risk analysis; benefit-cost analysis.

courses.title: International Development
courses.description: Definitions and measurements of development; impact of globalization; concept and practice of international development administration and planning at local, national, and global governance levels.

courses.title: Topics in Public Policy and Urban Studies
courses.description: Seminar in cross cutting topics in public policy and urban studies that engages students with faculty and scholars in interdisciplinary research and analysis of key problems and issues in the fields.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Sol Price School of Public Policy

courses.title: Management of Public and Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: Contemporary management theory; the nature of complex organizations' organizational and intergovernmental arrangements; roles and responsibilities of managers; managerial and organizational effectiveness; organizational structure and dynamics.

courses.title: Empirical Methods for Public Policy
courses.description: Introduction to multivariate regression analysis for policy analysis; course begins with Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimation and covers some advanced topics such as panel data and experimental methods; application of these tools in a variety of policy contexts such as education, labor, and health.

courses.title: Financial Management of Public and Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: Time value of money, risk, government bonds and tax-exempt financing, cost of capital, budgeting, financial statement analysis, and working capital management.

courses.title: Comparative Urban Development
courses.description: Urbanization and urban development and growth through an international scope; globalizing cities.

courses.title: Geodesign Practicum
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Application of design concepts, planning protocols and spatial analysis skills to a complex planning or design problem sponsored by a local public, private or not-for-profit client in a studio setting.

courses.title: Management of Health Care Organizations
courses.description: Healthcare trends affecting the management of healthcare organizations; impact of regulations and reimbursement; strategies for operational success; organizational roles and responsibilities.

courses.title: Community Health Policy and Planning
courses.description: Historical perspectives on and the contemporary practice of community health planning; impact of culture, socioeconomics, and environment; policy dimensions; urban plannings role in enhancing and sustaining health.

courses.title: Health Policy
courses.description: Health policy analysis and challenges; price of health; structure of major sectors in health care; role of insurance in policy debates; trade-offs with policy decisions.

courses.description: Introduction to psychological science, including historical and contemporary approaches. Behavior examined from biological, cognitive, social, developmental, and personality perspectives. Disorders and treatments.

courses.title: Drugs, Behavior, and Society
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An integrative systems perspective of drugs; including their historical, economic, and cultural importance, psychopharmacology, addiction, relationship to crime, and therapeutic use in treating psychological disorders.

courses.title: Social Analysis of Gender
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Multidisciplinary survey of gender assumptions in relation to sexuality, mental health, social and political relations, and artistic expression.

courses.title: Scientific Inquiry and Reasoning in Health Care
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Critical analysis and reasoning skills required to solve scientific problems in human behavior, including presentation of data, logic of research design, statistics, and research ethics. Not for major credit for Psychology majors.

courses.title: Natural and Artificial Intelligence
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduces core ideas in artificial intelligence (AI) as emerging from a dialogue between psychology, neuroscience, and computer science with an emphasis on quantitative reasoning.

courses.title: Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the use of statistics in psychology: basic ideas in measurement; frequency distributions; descriptive statistics; concepts and procedures in statistical inference.

courses.title: Language and Mind
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Language within cognitive science: speech physiology and acoustics, language acquisition, reading, language disorders, perception and mental representation of words, linguistic diversity and computer analysis of speech.

courses.title: Supervised Research in Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Supervised Research with department faculty.

courses.title: Cognitive Processes
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Experimental and theoretical aspects of human memory, perception, thinking, and language. Lectures, demonstrations, and individual experiments. Prerequisite: 100g or departmental approval.

courses.title: Sensation and Perception
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Receptor processes and stimulus organization; traditional topics in the perception of objects, space, time. Laboratory demonstrations and exercises.

courses.title: Learning and Memory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Principles involved in classical and operant conditioning. Concentration on basic causes of behavior; consideration of the relevance of simple behavioral laws to complicated human behavior.

courses.title: Experimental Research Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Experimental research methods in psychology; nature and concepts of scientific method.

courses.title: Non-Experimental Research Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Non-experimental research methods in psychology. Observational, survey and data analysis exercises

courses.title: Principles of Psychobiology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The integrative study of bio-behavioral systems. Evolutionary, developmental, ecological, social, ethological, and physiological factors mediating representative behavioral and psychological phenomenon are examined in detail.

courses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Neural bases of behavior. Concentration on sensory and motor processes and the interaction of neural, chemical, and hormonal systems.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Child and adolescent behavior and associated theories; exploration of the continuity between child and adult behavior. Laboratory projects.

courses.title: Origins of the Mind
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploration of ancient philosophical questions concerning the origins of human knowledge through empirical studies of infants, animals, and adults from diverse cultures.

courses.title: Close Relationships
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Scientific perspective of close relationships: intimate relationships, friendships and others, evolutionary and biological bases of attraction and love, historical, social , cultural influences. Prerequisite: PSYC 100. (Duplicates credit in PSYC 359)

courses.title: Social Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theoretical and experimental analysis of human behavior. Social processes involved in attitudes, conformity, compliance, interpersonal perception, liking, affiliation, aggression, altruism, and group dynamics.

courses.title: Psychology of Persuasion
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A critical analysis of persuasion used to influence individuals and groups using social media and artificial intelligence based on psychological scientific theories and methods.

courses.title: Psychological Disorders
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The commonly diagnosed behavior pathologies; biological, social, cultural and developmental antecedents of abnormal behavior; principles of learning, perception and motivation, as they relate to psychopathology.

courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the scientist-practitioner model of clinical psychology, including research methods, psychological assessment and diagnosis, psychotherapeutic interventions, and treatment of special populations.

courses.title: Criminal Behavior
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Genetic, biological, psychological, and sociological characteristics of those who evidence criminal behavior; theoretical formulations to be reviewed and appraised. Prerequisites: PSYC 100. Duplicates credit in former PSYC 463.

courses.title: Introduction to Forensic Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of current topics, technologies and techniques. Students acquire a basic understanding of how forensic psychologists contribute their unique expertise to the American legal system. Prerequisites: PSYC 100. Duplicates credit in former PSYC 465.

courses.title: Stress, Health, and the Mind-Body Connection
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to psychological, biological and behavioral processes affecting physical health, including stress, coping with disease, health behaviors and socioeconomic and cultural influences on health.

courses.title: States of Consciousness: From Dreams to Drugs
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The psychological science of states consciousness including sleep, animal and machine consciousness, and altered states of consciousness as a result of drugs, meditation and hypnosis.

courses.title: Junior Honors Seminar
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Advanced study of scientific inquiry in psychology with in-depth analysis of current research by faculty in the Psychology Department. Preparation for senior honors thesis research. Prerequisite: acceptance in Psychology Undergraduate Honors Program and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Psycholinguistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Experimental and theoretical aspects of how spoken and written language is produced and understood, learned during childhood, and affected by brain damage.

courses.title: Not Easy Being Green: Decision-Making for Sustainability
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Factors to consider when making decisions that frontline sustainability and psychological barriers that stand in the way of sustainable action.
courses.recommended_prep: ENST 100 Introduction to Environmental Studies or ENST 150 Environmental Issues in Society are strongly recommended

courses.title: Current Topics In Social Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Extensive examination of select current research in social psychology, based on original research papers. Specific topics change by semester.

courses.title: Human Judgment and Decision Making
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Descriptive and normative models of decision making; topics include probability judgments, inference, correlation, emotion, mental accounting, decision analysis, lens model, equity, social dilemmas, time, risk.

courses.title: User Experience
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the field of user experience (UX), with a specific focus on theoretical foundations, research methodology and principles of design.

courses.title: Functional Imaging of the Human Brain
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the physical and physiological bases of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), and principles of functional MRI, safety, design and analysis of experiments, and operation.

courses.title: Motivated Behaviors and Addiction
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Social, environmental, and physiological influences on behaviors associated with aggression, eating, reproduction, and sleep. Will focus on behavioral disorders such as addiction.
courses.recommended_prep: Junior or Senior Standing

courses.title: Social Development of Infants, Children and Adolescents
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An analysis of selected topics and issues in child social development. Recommended preparation: PSYC 274, PSYC 314, PSYC 336.

courses.title: From Eugenics to Neurodiversity: History of DisAbility
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An introductory overview of the primary historical issues, questions, concerns and developments that directly impact our current thought and action around disability and inclusion of disabled people in society.
courses.recommended_prep: PSYC 100

courses.title: Intelligence, Problem Solving and Creativity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Psychometric and experimental approaches to the study of intelligence, problem solving, reasoning and creativity, including analysis of mental test construction and validity.

courses.title: Developmental Neuroscience of Human Behavior
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The biological underpinnings supporting social, emotional, and cognitive development from infancy through adolescence; Focus on neuroscience to understand typical and atypical development, including psychopathology.
courses.recommended_prep: PSYC 336 and/or coursework in Neuroscience

courses.title: Adolescent Development
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The adolescent years from both an applied and a research-oriented perspective. Topics include physical, cognitive, and moral development; socialization; and sexual and sex-role development.

courses.title: Science of Yoga and Meditation
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Reviews intersection between modern science and ancient contemplative practices of yoga and meditation. Explores mind-body-spirit connection through personal practice, review of contemplative texts and empirical research.

courses.title: Neural Network Models of Social and Cognitive Processes
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to using neural network or connectionist models to simulate cognitive, social, emotional and motivational processes; basic concepts and tools in computational neuroscience.
courses.recommended_prep: Basic knowledge of programming is helpful, but not required

courses.title: Social Neuroscience
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of principles and research in social neuroscience, which uses neuroscience approaches to inform social processes including empathy, inter-group relations, emotion, morality and social decision-making.
courses.recommended_prep: PSYC 355

courses.title: Social Cognition
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theory and research on cognitive processes in social behavior, to include social inference, cognition and emotion, the Self, social categorization, person memory, and attribution processes. Recommended preparation: PSYC-355.

courses.title: Cognitive Behavior Therapy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The philosophical, ethical, historical, theoretical and procedural aspects of cognitive behavior therapy (CBT), including how theory guides practice and how practice informs theory.

courses.title: Industrial/Organizational Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: I/O Psychologists develop and apply scientifically supported solutions to the workplace. "Industrial" deals with human resource functions, and "Organizational" with psychological aspects of the organization. Prerequisite: PSYC 100. Recommended preparation: PSYC 316.

courses.title: Psychology of Marriage and the Family
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories and research on family relationships across the life span, including research methods, cultural and developmental perspectives, communication, conflict, attachment, individual psychopathology, and family violence.

courses.title: Introduction to Autism Spectrum Disorder
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of individuals diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.

courses.title: Happiness: Research in Neuroscience and Positive Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Neuroscientific and psychological perspectives that investigate the basis of happiness and well-being.

courses.title: Health and Mental Health Research in Mauritius
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores research design, existing health and mental health studies and research programs in Mauritius, unique challenges of conducting international research and ethical considerations in human subjects research.

courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Advanced study of empirical approaches in psychology. Progress presentations and evaluations of Senior Honors Thesis research. In-depth exploration of issues in science. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Directed Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

courses.title: Special Topics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Selected topics in the various specialty areas within psychology. Topic will vary from semester to semester.
