courses.description: Multiple regression as a tool in experimental and non-experimental data; analysis of variance and covariance as regression on coded variables. Computer applications. Laboratory exercises.

courses.title: Research Methods in Applied Social Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Various research techniques that are useful in a variety of different real world settings, such as business, governmental agencies and charities. Open only to M.S., Applied Psychology students.

courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Applied Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines qualitative research in applied settings. Learn to design, execute and report qualitative research in response to stakeholder needs.

courses.title: Psychopathology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of psychopathology: in-depth survey of theory and research concerning psychological disorders; introduction to diagnosis. (One of 4 clinical psychology core courses: 514, 515, 619, 620.)

courses.title: Clinical Assessment
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Study of clinical assessment: test construction, measurement and predicition of behavior, major cognitive and personality assessment instruments. (One of 4 clinical psychology core courses: 514, 515, 619, 620.)

courses.title: Group Dynamics and Leadership
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theory and research on effective teams and characteristics of strong leaders. Negotiation, morale-building, managing expectancies, utilization of cultural diversity as a strength. Open only to M.S., Applied Psychology students.

courses.title: Professional Issues for Clinical Scientists
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Focus is on professionalism topics and skills central to developing as a clinical scientist, explored within a cultural context.

school_restrictions.groupDescription: Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

courses.title: Cross Cultural Psychology in Applied Settings
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of major theoretical frameworks mapping worldwide cultures and values with a focus on applying thatknowledge in organizations. Open only to master students in Applied Psychology.

courses.title: User Experience (UX) Research
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Provides a broad introduction to the social science methods UX researchers most commonly use, including qualitative approaches, and quantitative approaches.

courses.title: Concepts and Principles of Behavior Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Provides intensive training in behavioral principles and laws of learning and motivation. Focuses on broad application of principles, from basic research with nonhumans, to application across human clinical populations.

courses.title: Behavioral Assessment
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Studies theory and application of behavioral methods for skill assessment, functional assessment of destructive behavior, and learner motivation. Discusses relative strengths and limitations of direct versus indirect methods.

courses.title: Affective Computing
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Provides training in legal and ethical issues as they pertain to the professional practice of behavior analysis. Reviews the Guidelines for Responsible Conduct for Behavior Analysts, as well as the American Psychological Associations Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct.

courses.title: Applied Developmental Psychology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Review of theories of cognitive development. Analysis of research on brain functioning, perception, memory, language, reasoning and academic skills from birth to adolescence.

courses.title: Social and Emotional Development in Children
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theories of social and emotional development, including sociocultural perspectives. Analysis of research on temperament, social relationships, individuation and moral development from birth to adolescence. Open to graduate students in psychology.

courses.title: Research Methods in Behavior Analysis
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of methods for measuring behavior. Examines theoretical background for single subject research methods, practical application of research methods to treatment evaluation, and analyzes strengths and limitations of single subject research methods.

courses.title: Behavioral Interventions
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines empirically supported behavioral interventions across a range of socially relevant behavioral excesses, skill deficits, disorders, and age ranges. Focuses on least-intrusive, person-centered approaches.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior Management
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

courses.title: Origins of Human Nature

courses.description: Examines cognitive development through the lens of comparative psychology: identifying cognitive and social traits that are uniquely human or shared with other animals.

courses.title: Behavioral Approaches to Skill Acquisition
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines contemporary research on behavioral procedures for teaching complex skills to individuals of a variety ages and populations, including language, social, cognitive, vocational, and independent living skills.

courses.title: Experimental Analysis of Behavior
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines a collection of experimental procedures and findings within the experimental analysis of behavior (EAB); basic principles of operant and respondent learning and motivation; translate findings of basic research to the development of applied sciences of behavior change.

courses.title: Computational Molecular Biology

courses.description: Applications of mathematical, statistical and computational methods to data from molecular biology: significance of alignment scores, hidden Markov models, evolution and gene expression analysis.
courses.recommended_prep: Familiarity with the concepts of basic molecular biology as covered in BISC-320

courses.title: Introduction to Real Estate
courses.description: Basic understanding of the real estate industry, the process of real estate development and investment, and the key players involved.

courses.title: Real Estate Career Seminar
courses.description: Career assessment and preparation; real estate industry overview; reflection on experiences.

courses.title: Real Estate Internship Seminar
courses.description: Real estate development skills for practice; internship seminar; leadership, group dynamics and presentation skills; application of management; organizational diversity; reflection on experiences.

courses.title: Introduction to Finance in Cities
courses.description: Basic understanding of public finance, public debt, public-private joint ventures, time value of money, present value, risk and return, discounted cash flows, leverage and taxes.

courses.title: Land Use Regulation
courses.description: Land use planning and zoning; community and government relations; environmental regulation.

courses.description: Real estate overview; evolution of cities and neighborhoods; product types; introduction to valuation.
courses.recommended_prep: ECON 203

courses.description: Real estate development feasibility and analysis; underwriting local fundamentals including neighborhood and city change, real estate capital flows.

courses.title: Shaping Cities Through Real Estate
courses.description: Cities and urban form created through various real estate product types. Case studies and site visits.
courses.recommended_prep: RED 362

courses.title: History of Planning and Development
courses.description: Historical evolution of planning and development. How changing modes of planning and development have shaped the built landscape throughout the century.

courses.title: Designing Livable Communities
courses.description: Theories and concepts of livable communities and good city form; case studies of historical and current best practices; field visits; collaborative design project.

courses.title: Analyzing Real Estate Markets
courses.description: Macro and micro-analysis of urban property markets; demographics; location choice; regulation.

courses.title: Advanced Finance and Investment for Real Estate Development
courses.description: Advanced real estate principles. Underwriting property valuation and deal structure including risk and return. Debt and equity markets; difference between development and existing assets.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research and readings.

courses.title: Market Analysis for Real Estate
courses.description: Explores macro and micro aspects of residential, retail, office, and industrial markets and examines methodologies for analyzing such markets for real estate development/investment purposes.

courses.title: Real Estate Practice and Principles
courses.description: Fundamental principles of real estate analysis; economics; capital markets; development decision making; relationships between real estate markets and federal, state and local government policies; property value.

courses.title: Foundations of Real Estate Analysis
courses.description: Principles of real estate analysis; captial markets; importance of uncertainty and metrics of risk; investments; valuation techniques; use of debty and equity, leases, taxes;

courses.title: Real Estate Project Analysis
courses.description: Fundamental economic theories; analytical techniques; practical applications for market analysis of various forms of real estate.

courses.title: Finance of Real Estate Development
courses.description: Theory and methods of real estate finance and investment. Real estate investment analysis, real estate entities, taxation; introduction to securization of real estate equities, debt.

courses.title: Real Estate Capital Markets
courses.description: Explore structure, instruments and institutions of real estate capital markets. Consider linkages between real estate and capital markets. Asses role of Real Estate Investment Trusts.

courses.title: Applications of Real Estate Finance to Problems of Developme
courses.description: Advanced topics in finance applied to cases and problems of real estate development; emphasis on structuring, finance and evaluation of various types of development projects.

courses.title: Legal Issues in Real Estate Development
courses.description: Ownership and transfer of real estate; formation and enforcement of contracts; business associations; environmental regulation; taxation of property transfers; acquiring, financing, leasing of commercial property.

courses.title: Introduction to the Asset Management of Real Estate
courses.description: Overview of institutional asset management: creating and implementing investment and portfolio strategies through the development, acquisition, underwriting, and operational stages of the investment, asset disposition.

courses.title: Building Typologies
courses.description: The exploration of categories of building types, including retail, industrial, residential, office, and institutional, using key examples or case studies from each.

courses.title: Community Design and Site Planning
courses.description: Physical implementation of development projects. Students will develop concept plan, preliminary design and marketing plan for selected domestic and/or international development sites.

courses.title: Comparative International Development Workshop
courses.description: Comparative study tour focused on understanding international real estate development practices and markets, site visits and meeting with principals.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

courses.title: Real Estate Product Development
courses.description: An evaluation of various real estate development product types. Case studies and site visits.

courses.title: The World of the Hebrew Bible
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The Hebrew Bible in the cultural setting of the ancient Near East; the formation of theological and ethical concepts which have shaped Western culture.

courses.title: Religions of Ancient Egypt and the Near East
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Religions, cultures, and values of ancient Egypt and Near East (Iran, Iraq, Israel, Syria, Lebanon, Arabia, Turkey) and their legacies in contemporary society.

courses.title: The New Testament
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Historical investigation of New Testament characters, events, ethics and theology in relation to its social, intellectual, and religious contexts in the Jewish and Greco-Roman world.

courses.title: Introduction to Christianity: Antiquity to 1500
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Survey of the changing beliefs and practices of the Christian religion from its origins through early modernity (100 CE - 1500 CE), with special attention to different varieties of Christian literature.

courses.title: Indian Traditions of Mind and Body
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores a variety of sophisticated theories and practices from India relating to the mind, body, medicine and religion.

courses.title: Origins of Western Religions
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam in their origins and their development in relation to Western civilization.

courses.title: Introduction to Buddhism
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Focus primarily on works of Buddhist literature written in a variety of genres. Introduction of basic teachings that link Buddhist traditions across time and space.

courses.title: Chinese Religions and Culture
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Historical and thematic survey of Chinese religious history from earliest times to the present.

courses.title: Introduction to Islam

courses.title: Global Religions in Los Angeles

courses.description: Congregational and individual expressions of religion in Los Angeles.

courses.description: History and contexts of anti-Semitism, racism and other discourses about difference examined through religious, national and cultural forms in Europe and in the US.

courses.title: Thought and Life of Islam

courses.description: Studies of the presence and influence of Zen Buddhism and Daoism in Asian literature, with a focus on China and Japan.

Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
courses.description: How religion, ethics and spirituality are embedded, embodied and emplotted in television drama; how secular texts represent "lived religion" to increasingly diverse audiences.

courses.recommended_prep: an undergraduate degree in pharmacy, medicine or independent health sciences, engineering or equivalent mix of post-secondary training and industry experience.

courses.title: Regulation of Pharmaceutical and Biological Products

courses.title: Social Problems
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Identifying and analyzing contemporary American social problems, their causes and potential solutions; examines poverty, crime, inequality, education, social isolation and civic decline.

courses.title: Immigrant America
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of the immigrant experience in the United States. Comparative analysis of social context of migration, formation of immigrant communities, and social integration of immigrants.

courses.title: Changing Family Forms
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The peculiarity of the "modern" Western family system in historical and cross-cultural perspective; focus on the "postmodern" family crisis in the United States.

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Basic concepts of sociology with special reference to group life,social institutions, and social processes.

courses.title: Science, Technology, and Social Conflict
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Science and technology change society and how we understand ourselves. In turn, social struggles influence science. We will explore the interplay between these forces.

courses.title: Migration, Law and Society
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Migration policies worldwide are negotiated by different stakeholders and create different contexts of reception that differently impact the everyday lives and livelihoods of migrants.

courses.title: Sociology, Demography and Health
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Sociological and demographic concepts focusing on the causes of disease, health and wellness. Empirical analysis of population composition and its connection to health.
courses.recommended_prep: Prepares pre-health students for sociology portion of the MCAT. Registration priority given to pre-health students

courses.title: Grassroots Participation in Global Perspective
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theory and history behind the ideal of "the local, grassroots volunteer": a direct link between theory and research using Los Angeles as a case study.

courses.title: Sociology of Globalization
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: This course examines globalization through social and economic processes and its consequences for social conflict, economic development, human rights, social movements, and national identity.

courses.title: Sociological Theory
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Historical and contemporary approaches to sociological theory; analysis of conceptual frameworks applied to the study of society and social interaction.

courses.title: Gender and Social Justice
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Exploration of the ways in which developments and policies, including neoliberalism, the carceral state, and economic precarity, are connected and gendered.

courses.title: Sociological Research Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Logic of theory construction, research design, elementary data collection and analysis.

courses.title: Analyzing Social Statistics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Sociological measurement, univariate description, elementary correlation, introduction to statistical inference.

courses.title: Applied Social Research Methods
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Use quantitative or qualitative analysis skills to study major social issues using large existing survey data sets or qualitative methods. Become conversant in describing data to a variety of audiences.

courses.title: Health, Gender and Ethnicity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Cross-cultural notions of the body, health, and healing; historic and cultural variability of ideas of reproduction, birth, sexuality, mental illness and disability.

courses.title: Organizations: Bureaucracy and Alternatives to Bureaucracy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Importance of organizations in social life; applied analysis of everyday bureaucratic and nonbureaucratic organizational structures; techniques for using and changing organizations.

courses.title: Social Exclusion, Social Power and Deviance
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines meanings of deviance and connection with status, power, and social control. Topics include homelessness, mental health, sexuality, the body, drugs, gambling and corporate crime.

courses.title: Youth, Social Control and Public Policy
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Construction of meanings of adolescence, social change and social control. Examines how social institutions such as school, law enforcement, and the state impose social control and how this varies by race, class and gender.

courses.title: Crime, Punishment and Society
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores cultural definitions, media constructions and measurement of crime. Places crime and punishment in larger social context and examines socio-cultural, economic and political factors.

courses.title: Immigrants in the United States
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Social construction of historical and contemporary immigration to the United States, including causes of migration, immigration policies and the socioeconomic integration of immigrants.

courses.title: Latino Social Movements
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Focuses on the political experience of Latinos in the U.S. Comparative analysis of their political experiences and perspectives, their histories of identity formation, and their political organizations.

courses.title: Social Inequality: Class, Status and Power
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Inequalities in wealth, prestige and power in the United States; the American class structure and the extent of upward mobility in that structure.

courses.title: Global and Transnational Sociology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examines key issues in global and transnational sociology. Globalization is the empirical phenomenon where social, economic, and political interconnectedness across countries impacts the world.

courses.title: The Family in a Changing Society
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Changing family patterns; personality development; family unity, predicting success in marriage; the family in transition; crises such as economic changes, death, divorce; family reorganization.

courses.title: Mixing and Matching: Intermarriage in 21st Century
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: An investigation into inter-ethnic, interracial, and inter-religious marriage in the 21st century.

courses.title: Judaism as an American Religion
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The development of American expressions of Judaism as part of the American religious context, from the perspective of the social scientific study of religion.

courses.title: Men and Masculinity
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Interdisciplinary examination of social, personal meanings of masculinity; variety of male experience by social class, race, sexuality and age; emerging masculinities of the future.

courses.title: Field and Survey Experiments
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Conducting experiments to estimate causal effects, in the field and using surveys.

courses.title: Volunteers, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Everyday Pol
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Theory, practice, and history of civic life. Examines communication, personal obligation, collective imagination, and political representation, in grassroots, state-sponsored, and non-governmental organization-sponsored civic associations around the world.

courses.title: Social Movements: Power, Resistance and Political Dynamics
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: When do groups mobilize to defend or resist power? Explores collective mobilization including student protest, minority rights and labor movements, the alt-right and revolutions.

courses.title: Cities
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Organization of urban society, including such topics as segregation, urban decay, local politics, residential change and community conflict.

courses.title: Environmental Sociology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Explores the causes and possible solutions to the environmental crisis, with emphasis on the politics of environmental knowledge and regulation.
courses.recommended_prep: SOCI 270, SOCI 313, SOCI 314

courses.title: Non-Governmental Organizations/Non-profits Field Practicum
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Internship in a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO). Students will conduct sociological research on issues surrounding NGOs and the work they do.

courses.title: Key Issues in Contemporary International Migration
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Overview of contemporary patterns of international migration and its implications for receiving and sending countries, with a special emphasis on immigration to the United States.

courses.title: Sociology of Gender and Work
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Examination of gender inequality in the U.S. labor market; work-family conflict; employer remedies; comparative social policy.

courses.title: Sociology of Religion
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: The role of religion in modern society from the standpoint of sociological theory and research.

courses.title: Medical Sociology
schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Social and cultural factors in causation of disease, health care utilization and health care delivery.

schools: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
courses.description: Introduces students to the theoretical questions and methodological approaches that comprise the discipline of sociology. Experts in each subfield share their latest research with students.

courses.description: Analysis of migration and population redistribution; policies affecting such migration and redistribution. Duplicates credit in former SOCI 549.

courses.description: Critique of research literature and research methods in the area of social class and social stratification; major theories and theoretical implications of current research. Duplicates credit in former SOCI 551.

courses.title: Seminar in Race Relations

courses.description: Current racial problems in the United States and other countries; critiques of literature on race relations. Duplicates credit in former SOCI 555.

courses.description: Cultural theories and forms of cultural analysis appropriate for sociological research; critical examination of theory and research on how culture relates to social structure, social inequality, politics, institutions, and everyday interaction. Recommended preparation: SOCI 510 or prior undergraduate or graduate coursework in social science or communication studies. Duplicates credit in former SOCI 535.

courses.description: Examines the historical emergence of ideas about race, modernity and colonialism and the role of culture in shaping how we understand race today.

courses.description: Examination of theories and research on cities in the United States, examining issues such as politics, race, development, and inequality. Open only to graduate students. Duplicates credit in former SOCI 571.

Duplicates credit in former SOCI 575.

courses.description: Prepares graduate students to publish in peer reviewed journals. Prerequisite: SOCI 620 or SOCI 622. Graded CR/NC.

courses.description: Historical and philosophical foundations of social conditions in the United States and their implications for public policy.

courses.description: Examines mindbody foundations of wellness and performance, analyzing motivation, stress, identity and social determinants to support equitable, culturally responsive approaches to thriving globally.

courses.description: The historical and current context of America's juvenile justice system and its influence on children, youth and families.

courses.title: Social Work Policy Advocacy for Social Change
courses.description: Empower yourself for impactful change. Dive into policy advocacy as a social worker, exploring key concepts and strategies for social change.

courses.description: Introduces undergraduates to evidence-based social work practice, including empirical research, AI/data tools and simulation modeling for data-driven interventions in social work settings.

courses.title: Adolescent Gang Intervention
courses.description: The incidence of gangs (particularly in the Los Angeles area), gang interventions, and policies developed to address the growing gang situation.

courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Supervised, individual studies. No more than one registration permitted. Enrollment by petition only.

courses.title: Community Experience in Juvenile Justice Environments
courses.description: Provides in-class and on-site community experiences to increase knowledge and understanding of youth experience in a range of social environments focused on juvenile justice.

courses.title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment
courses.description: The person-in-environment, bio-psycho-social perspective is the lens through which theories of personality, family, group, organization, community, culture and their interactions are explored. (Duplicates credit in SOWK 503 and SOWK 505)

courses.title: Interprofessional Education and Collaboration for Geriatrics
courses.description: Students from multiple health professions learn about aging and collaborative team care through a combination of didactic and experiential learning working in a community-based setting.

courses.title: Professional Self-Care in Integrative Social Work Practice
courses.description: Focuses on the value, examination and integration of professional self-care, wellness and resilience strategies into ethical and professional integrative social work practice.

courses.title: Critical Decision Making in Integrative Social Work Practice
courses.description: Focuses on the value and application of critical thinking and decision-making into ethical and professional integrative social work practice.

courses.description: Principles underlying social work practice with emphasis on rapport building, engagement, assessment and contracting individuals, families and groups though a social change framework.

courses.title: Foundations of Integrative Social Work Practice II
courses.description: Principles underlying social work practice with emphasis on intervention, termination and evaluation with individuals, families and groups though a social change framework.

courses.description: A study of the complex and interconnecting systems of policy, programs and communities that directly and indirectly impact Social Workers' clients lives. (Duplicates credit in SOWK 534)

courses.description: Introduction to the role of scientific inquiry in advancing social work goals. Inspires students to include science in their social work identity and professional decision-making. (Duplicates credit in SOWK 562)

courses.title: Applied Learning in Practicum Education II
courses.description: Practicum seminar and placement for developing foundational skills in integrative social work practice with individuals, families, groups, communities and/or organizations.

courses.description: The power of social work and sports to promote well-being, inclusivity and personal growth. This dynamic partnership fosters positive change within individuals, communities and society.

courses.description: Critical analysis and application of empirical evidence and research methods to assess client strengths and needs and to evaluate and improve integrative social work practice.

courses.description: Assessment of mental disorders, and the rationale and organization of the system for diagnosis. Emphasis is on developing differential diagnostic skills.

courses.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving schools and educational settings
courses.recommended_prep: Introductory coursework in integrative social work or comparable preparation as determined by the program

courses.description: Theory and multimodal approaches for brief therapy and crisis intervention with a broad spectrum of clients in a range of mental health and health settings.

courses.title: Substance Related and Behavioral Addictive Disorders and Rec
courses.description: Causal exploration of substance related and behavioral addictive disorders. Evidence-based and practice informed treatment models for vulnerable individuals, groups and families.

courses.description: Provides tools to enhance the practitioner's repsonse ot the special challenges (substance abuse, HIV/AIDS, domestic violence) in public child welfare.

courses.title: Practice and Policy with Children and Families Across Settings
courses.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving children, youth and families.

courses.title: Self-Awareness and Intercultural Humility in Social Work
courses.description: Critical exploration of sociocultural context and one's own values/assumptions/biases to enhance intercultural humility in social work.

courses.title: Integrative Interventions with Children, Youth and Families
courses.description: Critical application of theory, evidence and professional standards for integrative and culturally responsive assessment and intervention, highlighting practice contexts involving children, youth and families.

courses.title: Advanced Practice in Integrated Health and Mental Health
courses.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving adult mental health and wellness.

courses.title: Advanced Integrative Social Work Practice with Complex Cases
courses.description: Critical application of theory, evidence and professional standards for integrative and culturally responsive assessment and intervention, highlighting practice contexts involving adult mental health and wellness.

courses.description: Methods and principles of management focusing on health and human service organizations, including strategic management, financial analysis, and innovative project development in social work. Prerequisite: SOWK 506, SOWK 536, SOWK 544, SOWK 546.

courses.description: Understanding major psychoactive drugs used in treatment of psychological and behavioral disorders in behavioral and primary care medical settings. Theoretical/practical approaches to treatment are examined.
